text: Therpeth tɛncɔn laa tuɔk ɛ mi̱ ci̱ möli̱kio̱lɛth pi̱i̱ni̱ tin te wi̱cpi̱i̱ni̱ rɔ käp ɛ lɔ̱ŋ ɛ lënykɛn möli̱kio̱lɛth jɔam min te wi̱i̱cdiɛn.
text_en: Surface tension happens because the water molecules at the surface of the water are strongly attracted to each other more than they are to the air molecules above them.

text: Kɛn möli̱kio̱li̱ pi̱i̱ni̱ laa cakɛn guɔ̱p mi̱ /caa nɛn wi̱i̱cpi̱i̱ni̱ min ku ŋuak tin cetkɛ libɛ laa jak kä thɔaar wi̱cpi̱i̱ni̱.
text_en: The water molecules make an invisible skin on the water’s surface that allows things like the needle to float on top of the water.

text: Jɛn puur in te thook warä min laa ca̱a̱t kɛ naath rɛy tilijä mothɛ kä rɛɛw kä ɣöŋ kamdiɛn. Jɛn muɔthdɛ kä rɛɛw jak ɛ jɛ kä ɣöö bɛɛ tilig käp, mi cäŋ ci̱ rɔ gäŋ.
text_en: The blade on a modern ice skate has a double edge with a concave hollow between them. The two edges allow for a better grasp of the ice, even when tilted.

text: Kɛ ɣöö cɛ piny puɔ̱r ɛmɔ go̱k ɛ määth, mi̱ ci̱ puur rɔ ga̱ŋ kui̱c kɛl kiɛ kui̱c in dɔ̱ŋ, laa thokdɛ min nyɔɔt rɔ kɛɛ tilij rɔ laa gɔ̱ŋ bä.
text_en: Because the bottom of the blade is slightly curved, as the blade tilts to one side or the other, the edge which is in contact with the ice also curves.

text: Nɛmɛ laa jak ɛ ramin ca̱a̱t kä ɣöö bɛ rɔ ri̱t. Mi̱ ci̱ war in laa ca̱a̱t kɛ naath rɔ ga̱ŋ kui̱c cueec, jɛn rami ca̱a̱t bɛ rɔ ga̱ŋ cuëëc, mi̱ cɛ rɔ ga̱ŋ caam bi̱ raan rɔ ga̱ŋ caam.
text_en: This causes the skater to turn. If the skates tilt to the right, the skater turns right, if the skates tilt to the left, the skater turns left.

text: Kɛ ɣöö bi̱kɛ loc kä lɛbɔl i̱nerji̱kädiɛn min wän, laa kɛn tha̱a̱ŋ i̱nerji̱kä min ci̱kɛn ɛ go̱r laa wooc min ci̱kɛn ɛ jek kä buay.
text_en: To return to their previous energy level, they must get rid of the extra energy they got from the light.

text: Laa kɛn mi̱ cetkɛ nɔmɔ laa lät kɛ kämdiɛn kɛ buay raar min kua lɛ cɔl i̱ "photon"
text_en: They do this by emitting a tiny particle of light called a "photon".

text: Thanyti̱thni̱ cɔɔlkɛn duɔ̱ɔ̱p ɛmɔ i̱ "i̱thti̱muletid i̱mi̱cɔn kä radiecɔn" kɛ ɣöö kɛn atɔ̱mni̱ laa kua kɛ i̱thti̱mulet  kɛ buay mi̱ mɛrmɛr, kä buay ɛmɔ ɛ jɛn ta̱a̱ radiecɔn.
text_en: Scientists call this process "stimulated emission of radiation" because the atoms are stimulated by the bright light, causing the emission of a photon of light, and light is a type of radiation.

text: Jɛn thurɛ min rɛwdɛ nyooth ɛ jɛ atɔ̱m kämkɛn photonni̱ raar. Ɛ puc, kɛ thuɔ̱k photonni̱ kuiy ni̱ kɛn kä tin tɛ rɛy thurɛkä.
text_en: The next picture shows the atoms emitting photons. Of course, in reality photons are a lot smaller than those in the picture.

text: Photonni̱ kuiy ni̱ kɛn kä ŋɔak tin mat kɛ pua̱ny atɔ̱mni̱.
text_en: Photons are even smaller than the stuff that makes up atoms!

text: Kɛ kɔr thaakni̱ ti̱ kuɔ̱r tin ci̱ lät kɛ jɛ cuu pi̱lamɛn in te rɛy nurä waaŋ kä cu nuur kään cɛ lät.
text_en: After hundreds of hours of operation the filament in the bulb eventually burns out and the light bulb no longer works.

text: Jɛn nuur go̱rɛ ɣöö baa gɛr. Ro̱ŋɛ kɛ ɣöö dëë raan rɔ tit mi̱ gɛɛr ɛɛ nuur.
text_en: The light bulb then needs replacing. It is necessary to be careful in replacing the light bulb.

text: Kɛɛ nhiam, baa nuur kɔn gäk gua̱a̱th gäkädɛ kiɛ baa dëbdɛ da̱a̱k.
text_en: First, the switch for the light fixture needs to be turned off or the cable disconnected.

text: Nɛmɛ ɛ ɣöö la ka̱ra̱bɛ laa lo̱ny kä thɔkɛt gua̱th in laa tekɛ adiit kä ba̱lb dëë ka̱ra̱bɛ ji̱ käp thi̱n mi̱ ci̱ rɛy thɔkɛtdä thiap kiɛ thar ba̱lblä min tekɛ adiit gua̱th in känɛ ni̱ bën raar ɛ gɔa.
text_en: This is because electricity flowing into the socket where the metallic part of bulb sits can give you a severe electric shock if you touch the inside of the socket or the metal base of the bulb while it is still partly in the socket.

text: Jɛn cuɔ̱ŋ in dii̱̱t kä ta̱a̱ in jäl kɛ riɛm ɛ lɔc, ɛ jɛn min laa duäc riɛm.
text_en: The major organ of the circulatory system is the heart, which pumps the blood.

text: La riɛm ɛ jiɛn kä lɔc kɛ rɛy rääli̱ riɛm ti̱ cɔalkɛ artɛri̱ni̱ kä laa luny ɛ kä lɔc kɛ räl riɛm ti̱ cɔalkɛ i̱ bɛini̱. Kɛn ciɛwciɛwni tin ɣöŋ cɔalkɛ kɛ i̱ kapi̱lari̱ni̱.
text_en: Blood goes away from the heart in tubes called arteries and comes back to the heart in tubes called veins. The smallest tubes are called capillaries.

text: Lɛc tri̱thɛratɔpni /ci̱kɛn luäŋ ni̱ nyuey ji̱thni̱ juacni̱ kärɔ luäŋkɛn yuan jiɛn ti̱  buɔ̱mbuɔ̱ɔ̱m kɛnɛ ciök jiɛn.
text_en: A triceratops' teeth would have been able to crush not only leaves but even very tough branches and roots.

text: Tha̱a̱ŋ thanyti̱thni̱ diiwkɛn ɛ tri̱thɛratɔpni camkɛn nör, tin la jiɛn ti̱ cetkɛ jiath in ci̱ ga̱k kɛ do̱r Krɛtaiciath.
text_en: Some scientists think Triceratops ate cycads, which are a type of plant that was common in the Cretaceous.

text: Jiɛn ti̱ti̱ cetkɛ kɛ jiath palm mi̱ tɔt kä te wi̱cdɛ kɛɛ thac kuiyni̱ ,kɛ ji̱th ti̱ muɔth muɔɔth.
text_en: These plants look like a small palm tree with a crown of sharp, spiky leaves.

text: Jɛn Tri̱thɛtharɔpni̱ dëë kɛn tekɛ thuk ti̱ buɔmbuɔɔm tin la kɛn ji̱th laa rɛt kɛ kɛ ɛ ŋot kän kɛn taŋdɛ ni̱ cam.
text_en: A Triceratops could have used its strong beak to strip off the leaves before eating the trunk.

text: Tha̱a̱ŋ thanyti̱thni̱ ŋakɛn ɛ i̱ jiɛn ti̱ti̱ tekɛ kɛ lueŋ mi̱ di̱i̱t mi̱ lot ni ɣöö derɛ tuɔk ɛn /ci̱ dainöthɔri̱ jɛ dëë cam, mi̱ cäŋ kɛ jɛn gua̱a̱th ɛmɛ  i̱thlɔɔth kɛnɛ ley tin kɔ̱ŋ cetkɛ parrɔt ( tin bä karkiɛn kä dainöthɔr) cam kɛn jith kiɛ dɛy jiɛn ti̱ tekɛ luëŋ.
text_en: Other scientists argue that these plants are very poisonous so it is unlikely that any dinosaur ate them, even though today the sloth and other animals like the parrot (a descendant of the dinosaurs) can eat poisonous leaves or fruit.

text: Dëë gra̱bi̱ty duŋ Io ɣä tho̱t i̱ di̱? Mi ci̱ cuɔ̱ŋ wi̱i̱c Io, bi̱ thiakdu wä piny /cɛ bi̱ cetkɛ ta̱a̱ e thiɛk kɛ ji̱ wi̱i̱cmuɔ̱ɔ̱n.
text_en: How would Io's gravity pull on me? If you stood on the surface of Io, you would weigh less than you do on Earth.

text: Rami̱ cop wegdɛ 200 pounds (90kg) wi̱i̱cmuɔ̱n dëë wegdɛ pëëk kä 36 pounds (16kg) kä Io. Mi̱ lot ni̱ ɣöö gra̱bi̱ty, kɛ thuɔ̱k, /cɛ ji dëë tho̱t ɛlɔŋ.
text_en: A person who weighs 200 pounds (90kg) on Earth would weigh about 36 pounds (16kg) on Io. So the gravity, of course, pulls less on you.

text: Jɛn cäŋ thiɛlɛ jɛ kra̱th cetkɛ jɛn wi̱i̱cmuɔ̱n mi̱ dëë raan cuɔ̱ŋ thi̱n. Jɛn cäŋ ɛ mat jɔam,kɛ mac, kɛnɛ plathma.
text_en: The Sun doesn't have a crust like the Earth that you can stand on. The whole Sun is made out of gases, fire, and plasma.

text: Jɛn jiɔm laa wëë kɛ ciɛw mi̱ wi̱i̱ kɛ wä rɛy ca̱ŋ.
text_en: The gas becomes thinner as you go farther from the center of the Sun.

text: Jɛn jɔkdɛ min la kɔn a nɛɛn mi̱ guickɔn Cäŋ cɔalkɛ jɛ i̱ phötöthpier, mi̱ lotni̱ ɣöö "kurɛ mi̱ lɛp"
text_en: The outer-part we see when we look at the Sun is called the photosphere, which means "ball of light".

text: Kɛ kɔr runi̱ ti̱i̱ ki̱thni̱ da̱ŋdiɔ̱k, rɛy 1610, athtrɔnɔmɛr Ji i̱talia ni̱ Gali̱lɛɔ Gali̱lɛi cuɛ nhial guic kɛ tɛlɛthkɔp kä cuɛ jek ɛn ɣöö Bɛna̱th tëë kɛ gua̱th ti̱ tɛth kɛ jɛ cetkɛ min la pay ɛ päl.
text_en: About three thousand years later, in 1610, Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei used a telescope to observe that Venus has phases, just as the moon does.

text: Känydɛ laa tuɔk ɛ kɛ ɣöö geek Bɛna̱th (kiɛ duŋdɛ jɛn Pay) min cɛ luɔ̱t Cäŋ laa buɔyɛ. Jɛn ta̱a̱ känyä Bɛna̱th mätdɛ kɛɛ thio̱ri̱ duŋ Kɔpɛrni̱ka̱th min lat ɣöö muɔ̱n wilkɛn Cäŋ.
text_en: Phases happen because only the side of Venus (or of the Moon) facing the Sun is lighted. The phases of Venus supported the theory of Copernicus that the planets go around the Sun.

text: Kɛ gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ, kɛ kɔr runi̱ kɛ 1639 Jɛrɛmaya Hɔrrɔk cuɛ ta̱a̱ in gɛr Bɛna̱th rɔ kɛ jɛ guic.
text_en: Then, a few years later in 1639, an English astronomer named Jeremiah Horrocks observed a transit of Venus.

text: Wëc Iŋland cu kɛ tëy rɛy malä kɛ kɔr mi bäär kɛ kɔr kä mëë caa nyɔk kɛ käp ɛ wut mi cɔalkɛ Danɛlaw.
text_en: England had experienced a long period of peace after the reconquest of the Danelaw.

text: Kɛ ruɔn 991 cua Ethɛlrɛd ma̱k kɛ rɛy yiëë ɛ dec mi̱ di̱i̱t mi̱ cɔali Baikiŋ mi kän met tuɔɔk ni kɛ kɔr runi Guthrum ti̱ 100 tee ci̱ wä.
text_en: However in 991 Ethelred was faced with a Viking fleet larger than any since Guthrum's a century earlier.

text: Cu dëcni ti̱ jäl kɛ rɛy yiëër ti̱ böthkɛ ɛ Olap Tri̱gbathɔn kä Ji Nɔrwɛy wä kɛ ɣöö bi̱kɛ wecdiɛn wä luɔ̱cjɔk kä Ji Dɛnmark.
text_en: This fleet was led by Olaf Trygvasson, a Norwegian with ambitions to reclaim his country from Danish domination.

text: Kɛ nhiam mëë kän duɔp decä wä kɛ gua̱thdɛ, cu Ethɛlrɛd mat kɛnɛ Olap kɛ ɣöö be luny wi̱c kä Nɔrwɛy kɛ ɣöö bi kɛ ta̱a̱ kuäärä dɛ bën nyɔk kɛ ɣɔ̱n.
text_en: After initial military setbacks, Ethelred was able to agree to terms with Olaf, who returned to Norway to try to gain his kingdom with mixed success.

text: Ha̱ŋga̱l kä rɔa ɛ kɛn ba̱ni̱ tin la̱tkɛ kɛ tet rɛy ciɛŋä min lätkɛ. Kɛn Ba̱ni̱ tuɔk kɛ lätni̱diɛn kɛɛ 1444 kɛ gua̱a̱th ee Kuäär ni̱ Thɛjɔŋ (1418-1450).
text_en: Hangeul is the only purposely invented alphabet in popular daily use. The alphabet was invented in 1444 during the reign of King Sejong (1418 – 1450).

text: Kuär ni̱ Thɛjɔŋ ɛ jɛn kuär in ŋuandiɛn kä Jɔthiɔn Dyna̱thty kä ɛ jɛn ram min luɔ̱th kɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: King Sejong was the fourth king of the Joseon Dynasty and is one of the most highly regarded.

text: Ɛ jɛn ee cak ba̱ni̱ Ha̱ŋga̱l Hunmin Jiɔgia̱m, mi̱ lotni̱ ɣöö " jɔw in lot rɔ kɛ ŋi̱i̱cni̱ nath.
text_en: He originally named the Hangeul alphabet Hunmin Jeongeum, which means "the correct sounds for the instruction of the people".

text: Tekɛ thio̱ri̱ni̱ ti̱ ŋuan kɛ ta̱a̱ ee took Thanthkri̱t rɔ kɛ jɛ. Kɛl rɛydiɛn ɛ duŋ ɣöth Aryan kui̱c caam wädiɛn kä India tee ci̱ thokdiɛn dööŋ kɛ rɔ kɛɛl.
text_en: There are many theories to how Sanskrit came into existence. One of them is about an Aryan migration from the west into India who brought their language with them.

text: Thanthkri̱t ɛ thok nɛni̱ tee wal kä cäät kɛnɛ thok Latin ee ruac kɛ naath rɛy Eurɔp.
text_en: Sanskrit is an ancient language and is comparable to the Latin language spoken in Europe.

text: Bok ee ŋa̱ckɛ ni̱ wal mëë kɔan gɔ̱ri̱jɛ caa gɔ̱r kɛ thok Thanthkri̱t. Kɛ kɔr kä mee mat kɛ Upani̱cadni, Thanthkri̱t cuɛ yaaw kɛ kui̱c ta̱a̱ kä min bi̱ böth.
text_en: The earliest known book in the world was written in Sanskrit. After the compilation of Upanishads, Sanskrit just faded due to hierarchy.

text: Thanthkrit ɛ thok mi̱ bumbum kä tekɛ ti̱ ŋuan, min ci̱ jɔɔc ɛ la ɣöö tuɔk thuk India ti̱ ŋuan thi̱n, cetkɛ min ci̱ thuk ti̱ ŋuan ben raar kä Latin kä Ji Eurɔp cetkɛ thok Pra̱nth kɛnɛ thok I̱thpɛɛny.
text_en: Sanskrit is a very complex and rich language, which has served to be the source for many modern Indian languages, just like Latin is the source for European languages like French and Spanish.

text: Kɛ mee ci̱ kör Pra̱nth thuɔ̱k, Cu Jerman rɔ tok kɛ riali̱kä kɛ ɣöö bɛ dhuɔ̱ɔ̱l Ji Bri̱ti̱c ma̱k.
text_en: With the battle for France over, Germany began to get ready to invade the island of Britain.

text: Ca̱p pɛlä köör Jɛrman cɔɔlkɛn ɛ i̱ "Opɛracin thi̱i̱laiyɔn". Mäc decni̱ Ji Bri̱ti̱c ti̱ ŋuanikɛn ti̱ thiakthiaak kɛnɛ kuakiɛn cuu kɛ riaw mee jiɛn kɛ kä Da̱ŋkirk, kɛ kui̱c ci̱ decni̱ lua̱ŋdiɛn cua mi̱ tɔt.
text_en: Germany code-named the attack “Operation Sealion”. Most of the British Army's heavy weapons and supplies had been lost when it evacuated from Dunkirk, so the army was fairly weak.

text: Duundɛ Rɔyal Nebi̱ ŋotdɛ bumni̱kɛn kä Jerman Nebi̱ ("Kri̱ɛgthmari̱nɛ") kä dee kɛn ɛni̱ ti̱caar mi̱ dëë naath ma̱k kɛ rɛy Canɔlä Ji Iŋland.
text_en: But the Royal Navy was still much stronger than the German Navy (“Kriegsmarine”) and could have destroyed any invasion fleet sent across the English Channel.

text: Kɛ ɣöö nɔ, baburi̱ Rɔyal Nebi̱ ti̱ tɔt caa kɛ yiɛ̈n gua̱a̱th ee diɛwkɛ i̱ baa kɛ ma̱k kɛ jɛ kɛ ɣöö admi̱ral dualɛ kɛ ɣöö baa babuuri̱kiɛn di̱ŋ kɛ bo̱k Jerman.
text_en: However, very few Royal Navy ships were based near the likely invasion routes as the admirals were afraid they would be sunk by German air attack.

text: Can luɔtdɛ tok kɛ lat jɛn ca̱p Ji I̱talia. I̱talia ɛ jɛn "däman in tɔt" duŋ Jerman kɛnɛ Japan.
text_en: Let's start with an explanation about Italy's plans. Italy was mainly the "little brother" of Germany and Japan.

text: Nyuän decni̱kɛ raar amäni nebi̱, cäŋni̱ mee paykɛn babuuri̱ da̱ŋuan la̱t ɛ ŋot ka̱n ko̱r i̱ tok.
text_en: It had a weaker army and a weaker navy, although they had just built four new ships right before the beginning of the war.

text: Mee go̱o̱r Ji Italia ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛ nee kɛ wi̱i̱c Aprika. Kɛ ɣöö dekɛn kɛ käp, go̱o̱rkɛn gua̱a̱th mi̱ dëë decni̱ yuɔrkɛ piny thi̱n, kɛ ɣöö dee wä ni̱ kɛ rɛy baar Mɛdi̱tɛrranian kɛ käpdiɛn kɛɛ Aprika.
text_en: Italy's main goals were African countries. To capture those countries, they would need to have a troop launching pad, so as troops could sail across the Mediterranean Sea and invade Africa.

text: Kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ, dee kɛn gua̱th decni̱kiɛn tin tekä Bri̱ti̱c päl kä dëë kɛn wä kä I̱jip. /Ciɛ jɛn la̱t ɛmɔ kärɔa, babuuri̱ köör I̱talia thiɛlɛ mi̱ gör kɛ i dee kɛn ɛ la̱t.
text_en: For that, they had to get rid of British bases and ships in Egypt. Besides those actions, Italy's battleships were not supposed to do anything else.

text: Ɛn täämɛ Japan. Japan cɛ kɔn ɛ wec mi̱ te wi̱i̱c dhuulä, cetkɛ Ji Bri̱ti̱c.
text_en: Now for Japan. Japan was an island country, just like Britain.

text: Tha̱bmari̱i̱n ɛ babur mi̱ caa la̱t kɛ ɣöö bɛ ja̱l kɛ piny pi̱i̱ni̱,kä bɛ te thi̱n kɛ gua̱th mi̱ bäär.
text_en: Submarines are ships designed to travel underwater, and remain there for an extended amount of time.

text: Tha̱bmari̱i̱n ci̱ naath lät kɛ kɛ rɛy Köör Wecmuɔ̱n in nhiam kɛnɛ Ko̱r wecmuɔ̱n in rɛwdɛ. Kɛ gua̱th ee dan laa jälkɛ ɛ määth kä /ci̱ dɛykiɛn laa räth ɛ na̱n.
text_en: Submarines were used in World War I and World War II. Back then they were very slow and had a very limited shooting range.

text: Ni kɛ tuk köör laa jälkɛ kɛ wi̱c pi̱i̱ni̱ bäpdiit, duundɛ ɣöö kɛ gua̱th ee caa rɛdaar ben tok kɛ lätni̱ kä cɛ ben raŋ cuɛ tha̱bmari̱i̱ni̱ jak kä ɣöö bikɛ ja̱l kɛ piny pi̱i̱ni̱ kɛ ɣöö /caa kɛ bi̱ kulɛ nɛn.
text_en: In the beginning of the war they mostly travelled on top of the sea, but as radar began developing and becoming more accurate the submarines were forced to go under water to avoid being seen.

text: Tha̱bmari̱i̱ni̱ Ji Jɛrman cɔalkɛ kɛ U-bötni̱. Kɛn Ji Jɛrman ŋäckɛn ja̱l rɛy yieer kɛnɛ ger tha̱bmari̱i̱nikiɛn.
text_en: German submarines were called U-Boats. The Germans were very good at navigating and operating their submarines.

text: kɛ ɣöö ci̱kɛn la̱t tha̱bmari̱i̱ni̱ ŋa̱c kɛ gua̱thdɛ, kɛ kɔr köör Ji Jɛrman /caa kɛ ŋäth kɛ ɣöö bi̱kɛn tekɛ ti̱ ŋuan.
text_en: Because of their success with submarines, after the war Germans aren't trusted to have many of them.

text: Inɔ! Kuäär ni Tutankhamun, kɛ tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱ni̱ laa cɔalkɛ jɛ i̱ "Kuäär Tut" kiɛ "Jen Kuäär Dhöl", ɛ rami̱ di̱t kɛ̈kdɛ ɛ lɔ̱ŋ kä Kua̱ar Ji Ijip tee wal kɛ jɛn gua̱th ɛmɛ.
text_en: Yes! King Tutankhamun, sometimes referred to as "King Tut" or "The Boy King", is one of the most well known ancient Egyptian kings in modern times.

text: Min gɔa thin, ka̱nɛ naŋ ɛ la rami̱ bumbum kɛ gua̱a̱th ee wal kɛnɛ ɣöö ka̱nɛ gɔa̱r rɛy buɔkni̱ ciötni̱ kua̱ri̱ tee wal ti̱ ŋuan.
text_en: Interestingly, he was not considered to be very important in ancient times and was not recorded on most ancient king lists.

text: Kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ, jɛn jek pul kunyädɛ rɛy 1922 cɛ jɛ jakä ɣöö bi̱ kɛ̈kdɛ jɔɔc. Kɛ gua̱a̱th ee mac kɛ puɔ̱l kunyä kɛ pek ee ci̱ wä, pul kunyä nɛmɛ cua päl cuŋä ɛ ka̱nɛ gueer.
text_en: However, the discovery of his tomb in 1922 made him a celebrity. While many tombs of the past were robbed, this tomb was left virtually undisturbed.

text: Kuak ti̱ ŋuanikɛn tee caa kony kɛɛl kɛ Tutankhamun caa kɛ tɔw ni̱ gɔa, amäni̱ kuak ti̱ caa täth ti̱i̱ ki̱thni̱ ti̱ la̱tkɛ kɛ guiy ti rɛlrɔ kɛnɛ dööl ti̱ bum jekdiɛn.
text_en: Most of the items buried with Tutankhamun have been well preserved, including thousands of artefacts made from precious metals and rare stones.

text: Jɛn tuk ta̱th i̱thpuk wi̱i̱l cɛ Athirian cariöt jak kä puɔl, kä pɛ̈th, kä cɛ riali̱kä kɛ ɣöö bɛɛ decni̱ leny kɛnɛ ca̱riötni̱ tin kɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: The invention of spoke wheels made Assyrian chariots lighter, faster, and better prepared to outrun soldiers and other chariots.

text: Dɛy kuiinbärä tin la nyin kuiinbärä ti̱ bɛ̈cbɛ̈ɛ̈c dëkɛn go̱k decni̱ tin yiëëth kɛ naath wuth. Kɛ gua̱a̱th 1000 B.C., cu Athi̱rian kälbäri̱ min nhiam tok.
text_en: Arrows from their deadly crossbows could penetrate the armor of rival soldiers. About 1000 B.C., the Assyrians introduced the first cavalry.

text: Ɛn Kälbäri̱ kɛɛ decni̱ tin laa nyiëny kɛ naath jɔɔk jiök tuɔ̱ruɔ̱kni. Jɛn thac jɔakdɛ ŋotdɛ ka̱nɛ ni̱ cak, kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ cuu kälbäri̱  Athi̱riani̱ ko̱r tɛr jɔɔk jio̱kni̱ tuɔ̱ruɔ̱k baaŋ .
text_en: A cavalry is an army that fights on horseback. The saddle had not yet been invented, so the Assyrian cavalry fought on the bare backs of their horses.

text: Ŋäc kɔn ɛ i̱ poli̱ti̱ciani̱ Gri̱i̱k ti̱ ŋuan, thanyti̱thni̱, kɛnɛ thuɔ̱ɔ̱r thurɛni̱. Kɛ ta̱a̱ in lotrɔ jɛn rami ŋa̱ckɛ rɛy ta̱a̱ ciɛŋä nath ɛ Ho̱mɛr, jɛn puɔit ee ci̱ kɛ̈kdɛ joor, mee cak ruaacni̱ da̱ŋrɛw tee caa gɔ̱r kä Gri̱i̱k: kɛn poɛmni̱ I̱liad kɛnɛ O̱dythɛy.
text_en: We know many Greek politicians, scientists, and artists. Possibly the most known person of this culture is Homer, the legendary blind poet, who composed two masterpieces of Greek literature: the poems Iliad and Odyssey.

text: Thophokɛli̱ kɛnɛ Ari̱thtöphani̱ kɛ kɛn pleyruaigtni̱ tin ŋa̱ck nikɛ kä pleydiɛn ɛ jɛn min guɛckɛ ni̱ jɛ  ɛ la min caa la̱t kɛ ŋua̱a̱thdɛ ta̱a̱ gɔrä wi̱i̱cmuɔ̱n.
text_en: Sophocles and Aristophanes are still popular playwrights and their plays are considered to be among the greatest works of world literature.

text: Raan Gri̱i̱k in dɔ̱ŋ min ŋa̱ckɛ ɛ gɔ̱ɔ̱r mɛthä ni̱ Paithagöra̱th, mee ŋa̱ckɛ kɛ kui̱c thio̱rädɛ min nyooth ta̱a̱ in dee ŋäc ni̱ geek duŋ rait trai-a̱ŋgɔ̱li.
text_en: Another famous Greek is a mathematician Pythagoras, mostly known for his famous theorem about relations of the sides of right triangles.

text: /Ciɛ pëk mi̱ ŋa̱ckɛ ɛ gɔa ɛn pëk nath tin ruac kɛ thok Hindi̱. Diɛw kɛ jɛ ɛn ɣöö dërɛ te kam thuɔk in rɛwdɛ kɛnɛ thok in ŋuandiɛn kä thuk tin ruac naath kɛ kɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ wi̱i̱cmuɔ̱n.
text_en: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi. It is estimated to be between the second and fourth most commonly spoken language in the world.

text: Jɛn pëk nath tin laa diël ruac /ciɛ pëk mi̱ ŋa̱ckɛ kɛ ɣöö pëk ɛ kä thuk ti̱ thiëk ɛ lɔ̱ŋ tin caa kuɛn.
text_en: The number of native speakers varies depending on whether or not very closely related dialects are counted.

text: Kɛ pëk mi̱ dëë mar mi̱ took ɛ ni̱ kä baathdɔɔri̱ 340 ɛ wä kä baathdɔɔri̱ 500 ruac kɛ kɛ thok ɛmɔ, kɛnɛ pëk nath ti̱ dëë baathdɔɔri̱ 800 dëë kɛ ruac kɛ thok ɛmɔ.
text_en: Estimates range from 340 million to 500 million speakers, and as many as 800 million people can understand the language.

text: Hindi̱ kɛnɛ Urdu cäät riëtkiɛn dundɛ gua̱cni̱ gɔa̱riɛn; rɛy ruaacni̱kiɛn ni̱ ciaŋ, nɛy tin ruac gua̱thni̱kiɛn da̱ŋrɛw liŋkɛn rɔ.
text_en: Hindi and Urdu are similar in vocabulary but different in script; in everyday conversations, speakers of both languages can usually understand each other.

text: kɛ gua̱th 15th thenciɛry, Nhiam Ethtönia caa ta̱a̱diɛn man ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛ kalciɛr Ji Jɛrman.
text_en: Around the 15th century, northern Estonia was under great cultural influence of Germany.

text: Tha̱a̱ŋ mɔŋni̱ Jɛrman go̱rkɛn ɣöö bi̱kɛ Koth nöŋ diël wecdiɛn, kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ cukɛ thok Ji̱ Ethtönia cak.
text_en: Some German monks wanted to bring God closer to the native people, so they invented the Estonian literal language.

text: Caa jɛ la̱t kɛ kɔr alphabetni̱ Ji Jɛrman kä cu kɛ ba̱ kɛl "Õ/Õ"mat thi̱n
text_en: It was based on the German alphabet and one character "Õ/õ" was added.

text: Kä mee ci̱ gua̱th wä, riëët ti̱ guan tee caa dɛn kä Jɛrman liɔmkɛɛl. Nɛmɛ cuɛ kua̱jɛn tuk gɔ̱rädiɛn.
text_en: As time passed, many words that were borrowed from German coalesced. This was the beginning of enlightenment.

text: Kɛ la̱t dhɔariɛn, jɛn ramin baa ba̱ny kuäär laa wee dëëcä nikɛ thuɔkdɛ kä bok wälrɛw
text_en: Traditionally, the heir to the throne would go straight into the military after finishing school.

text: Känɛ tuɔk inɔ, Charlɛth cu wä ni̱ jɛn kä Jam kä Tri̱ni̱ty Kɔlig, Kambrig gua̱a̱th ee gɔ̱ɔ̱rɛ Anthrɔpɔlɔgy kɛnɛ Arkiölɔgy, kä kɛ kɔrɛ mäni̱ I̱thtöry, cuɛ 2:2 jek ( ɛ digri̱i̱ piny kä clɛ̈th in rɛwdɛ)
text_en: However, Charles went to university at Trinity College, Cambridge where he studied Anthropology and Archaeology, and later History, earning a 2:2 (a lower second class degree).

text: Charlɛth ɛ jɛn ramin nhaim kä Bri̱ti̱c Rɔyal Pami̱ly min ci̱ di̱gri̱i̱ cop.
text_en: Charles was the first member of the British Royal Family to be awarded a degree.

text: Ji Eurɔp kä Turki̱ (cuëëc Thra̱c kiɛ Rumɛlia min te rɛy go̱kä Balkan) matkɛn 3% kä jɛn wec.
text_en: European Turkey (eastern Thrace or Rumelia in the Balkan peninsula) includes 3% of the country.

text: Jɛn mun duŋ Turki̱ bäälɛ 1,600 kilometres (1,000 mi) kɛ bär kɛnɛ 800 km (500 mi) kɛɛ ɣëbɣëëb, kä tekɛ ta̱a̱ mi̱i̱ buɔ̱thjɔk.
text_en: The territory of Turkey is more than 1,600 kilometres (1,000 mi) long and 800 km (500 mi) wide, with a roughly rectangular shape.

text: Pëk Turki̱, matkɛ puɔ̱l thin, naŋ ɛ 783,562  square kilometres (300,948 sq mi), kɛ 755,688 square kilometres (291,773 sq mi) tekɛ jɔk ɛ wä caam Ecia kɛnɛ 23,764 square kilometres (9,174 sq mi) rɛy Eurɔp.
text_en: Turkey's area, including lakes, occupies 783,562 square kilometres (300,948 sq mi), of which 755,688 square kilometres (291,773 sq mi) are in south west Asia and 23,764 square kilometres (9,174 sq mi) in Europe.

text: Pëk Turki̱ jak ɛ jɛ kä wec in 37th kä wi̱i̱c tin di̱t mundiɛn wi̱i̱cmuɔ̱ɔ̱n, kä dee pa̱a̱r nijɛn kɛ mat Rɛy Pranth kɛliw kɛnɛ Unaitɛd Kiŋdɔm.
text_en: Turkey's area makes it the world's 37th-largest country, and is about the size of Metropolitan France and the United Kingdom combined.

text: Turki̱ caa go̱l ɛ bar geeknikɛ da̱ŋdiɔ̱k: jɛn Bar Aegean kui̱c caam,kɛ jɛn Bar Blak nhiam kɛnɛ jɛn Bar Mɛdi̱tɛrɛnian jɔɔkdɛ.
text_en: Turkey is encircled by seas on three sides: the Aegean Sea to the west, the Black Sea to the north and the Mediterranean Sea to the south.

text: La̱dhembourg tëkɛ mi̱ bäär ɛlɔ̱ŋ duŋni̱ ɣöö jɛn cuɛ cuɔ̱ŋ kärɔa ni̱ rɛy ni̱ni̱ ti̱ tokɛ kä 1839.
text_en: Luxembourg has a long history but its independence dates from 1839.

text: Kɛ pek-in thi̱a̱k tha̱a̱ŋ Bɛlji̱ɛm cuɛ kɔnɛ tha̱a̱ŋ La̱dhembourg rɛy gua̱th ëë wal duŋni̱ ɣöö kɛ kɔrɛ cua Bɛlji̱ɛm cak ɛ Reböluciɔndiɛn kɛn Ji̱ Bɛlji̱ɛm.
text_en: Present-day parts of Belgium were part of Luxembourg in the past but became Belgian after the 1830s Belgian Revolution.

text: La̱dhembourg  cuɛ ɣɔ̱n ni̱ ciaŋ i̱ bɛ a wec mi̱ te kärɔa duŋni̱ ɣöö jɛn cua ciɛŋ rɛy Köör Wecmuɔ̱ɔ̱n I kɛnɛ Ko̱r Wecmuɔ̱ɔ̱n II ɛ Ji̱ Jiɛrman.
text_en: Luxembourg has always tried to remain a neutral country but it was occupied in both World War I and World War II by Germany.

text: Rɛy 1957 la̱dhembourg cuɛ tekä wi̱i̱c tëë took buɔ̱n min cua cɔalɛ ɛ walɛ i̱ Yurɔpiaan Yuni̱ön.
text_en: In 1957 Luxembourg became a founding member of the organization which is today known as the European Union.

text: Jɛn Dra̱kgiyal Di̱dhɔŋ s ti̱c mi̱ ca ya̱r kä Budi̱dhi̱m möna̱thteri̱ kui̱c in te nhial kä Parö Di̱thti̱rik (rɛy Pöndey Bi̱llige).
text_en: The Drukgyal Dzong is a ruined fortress and Buddhist monastery in the upper part of the Paro District (in Phondey Village).

text: Jɛn cua lar rɛy 1649, i̱ Dhabdra̱ŋ Ngawaŋ Namgiyel cua tok ɛ la ti̱c mi̱ tiɛmkɛ juc ëë caa puɔ̱t di̱ënyni̱- Ti̱betan Mɔngɔl.
text_en: It is said that in 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel created the fortress to commemorate his victory against the Tibetan-Mongol forces.

text: Rɛy 1951, mëë ci̱ mac ɛ waŋ cuu kääni̱ tha̱a̱ŋ ŋɔaani̱ kärɔ̱ nyin Dra̱kgi̱yal Dhɔŋ  ce̱tkɛ thurɛ mi̱ cie duŋ Dhabdra̱ŋ Ŋawaŋ Namgyal.
text_en: In 1951, a fire caused for only some of the relics of the Drukgyal Dzong to remain, such as the image of Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal.

text: Kɛ kɔr maac, jɛn ti̱c cuɛ duɔth kä cua gaŋ, mëë cu duɔth cua kɛl kä nyin Biɣutanä ɛ la mi̱ cuu nën tekɛ lɔ̱ɔ̱l mi̱ gɔa ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: After the fire, the fortress was preserved and protected, remaining to be one of Bhutan's most sensational attractions.

text: Ni̱ kɛ jɛn rɛy runi̱ ti̱ kur wälbädäkdiɛn18th Kambödia cua jiek kärɔa tëë kam nɛɛni̱ rɛw ti buɔ̱m-buɔ̱m kä ji̱ thiäkädɛ, Thai̱lɛ̈n kɛnɛ Biɛtnam.
text_en: During the 18th century Cambodia found itself squeezed between two powerful neighbors, Thailand and Vietnam.

text: Kɛn Ji̱ Thai̱ cua Kambödia ma̱k ni̱kä ti̱ ŋuan rɛy runi̱ ti̱ kur 18th kä kɛ rɛy 1772 kɛn cua Pi̱i̱nɔm Pëën däk.
text_en: The Thais invaded Cambodia several times in the 18th century and in 1772 they destroyed Phnom Phen.

text: Kɛ jɛn thuɔ̱k runi̱ ti̱ kur 18th pa̱ny kɛn Ji̱ Biɛtnam bä cua Kambödia ma̱k.
text_en: In the last years of the 18th century the Vietnamese also invaded Cambodia.

text: Pek mi̱ cuɔpkɛ wälbädäk wi̱kä kuɔ̱r thiɛlɛ kɛ lät kä Ji̱ Benëdhuɛla, kä ri̱w nɛɛni̱ ŋuan kä kɛ lätkɛ kɛ ta̱a̱ kuilkanä mi̱ thiɛl guir.
text_en: Eighteen percent of Venezuelans are unemployed, and most of those who are employed work in the informal economy.

text: Rɛw wi̱i̱ di̱ɔ̱kni̱ kä Ji̱ Benedhuɛla kɛn lätkɛ kɛ lätni̱ tin laa la̱tkɛ, pek mi̱ cop nuth nuthä lätdɛ rɛy inda̱thti̱ri̱ kä dhi̱e̱e̱cdiɛn lätdɛ rɛy puɔ̱r ka̱a̱kni̱.
text_en: Two thirds of Venezuelans who work do so in the service sector, nearly a quarter work in industry and a fifth work in agriculture.

text: Ɛn inda̱thti̱ri̱ in gɔa ni̱ jɛn kä Benedhuɛla ɛ liɛɛth, gua̱th in  wec ɛ jɛn min laa naŋɛ ko̱kä raar, cua guic cie ɛ pek mi̱ cop kɛl wi̱kä kuɔ̱r min lät gua̱th liɛth.
text_en: An important industry for Venezuelans is oil, where the country is a net exporter, even though only one percent work in the oil industry.

text: Ni̱kɛ nhiam mëë ci̱ wec cuɔ̱ŋ kärɔa, Thiŋɛpoor Bötanik Gardɛn cu ca̱r luäk kä dɛ ɛn dhuɔ̱ɔ̱l mi̱ ba naŋɛ ni̱kä tröpika̱ Gardɛn Ci̱ti̱ ben raar.
text_en: Early in the nation's independence, Singapore Botanic Gardens' expertise helped to transform the island into a tropical Garden City.

text: Rɛy 1981, Banda Mi̱th Joakuim, min la ɔrki̱d ɣai̱bri̱d, cua kuany cie mi̱ ɛ gaak mi̱ la duŋ wec.
text_en: In 1981, Vanda Miss Joaquim, an orchid hybrid, was chosen as the nation's national flower.

text: Ɛni̱ ruɔ̱n rɛy Laath ä la pek mi̱ cop mi̱lli̱ömni 1.5 mi̱e̱e̱th juaani̱ la jäl ɛ luɔ̱ŋ kɛrɔ̱ tɔ̱ɔ̱rä kui̱c  thɔthɛrɛn, rɛ̈t kɛ ni̱ jɛn Kir Mara, jiɛn kɛ wuɔ̱th päämni̱ kɛ kui̱ nhi̱ëëli̱.
text_en: Every year around October nearly 1.5 million herbivores travel towards the southern plains, crossing the Mara River, from the northern hills for the rains.

text: Kä la kɛnɛ loc jɔk kɛ jɛn nhiam ɛ retkɛ kɛ rɛy kuec  ̱caam, kä kɛɛl mi̱ ci̱kɛ rët kɛ rɛy kiɛɛr Mara, kɛ kɔrɛ mi̱ nhiaal dɛ̈m kɛɛ Guak.
text_en: And then back to the north through the west, once again crossing the Mara river, after the rains in around April.

text: Jɛn Thereŋeti̱ ɛ wec mi̱ tekɛ jɛn Thereŋeti̱ Naci̱ɔnal Park, jɛn Ŋörɔŋörö Kɔntherbɛciɔn Area kɛnɛ Mathwa Gëëm Ri̱dhääb rɛy Tandhania kɛnɛ jɛn Maathai Mara Naciɔnal Ri̱dhääb rɛy Kenya.
text_en: The Serengeti region contains the Serengeti National Park, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and Maswa Game Reserve in Tanzania and the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya.

text: Ŋäc kä ɣöö bi̱ media mi̱ bi̱ nath mat thi̱n tok go̱rɛ ta̱a̱ in la̱tkɛ tin lät ni̱ wän kɛnɛ tin ŋäc raan kɛ ɛ la jɛn, cie tin ci̱ ŋa̱c ɛlɔ̱ŋ rɛy ki̱lɛ̈ɛ̈thni̱ gua̱th in ti̱ rɛy nath (i̱thtöri̱buɔrdiŋ, ɣɔdi̱ö kɛnɛ riali̱ bi̱di̱ö i̱kä ɛ nyɔk, lat lɛ̈ɛ̈ŋni̱, ɛkw).
text_en: Learning to create interactive media requires conventional and traditional skills, as well as tools mastered in interactive classes (storyboarding, audio and video editing, story telling, etc.)

text: Ca̱pla̱t ŋɔani̱kɛɛl jɛn go̱rɛ ɣöö ji̱n biɛ-nyɔk kɛ guäc ɛn ta̱a̱ in bɔ̱ ŋɔaani̱ raar kɛ jɛ kä media kɛnɛ gör ŋäcä cärä mi̱ /ci̱ wi̱du bi̱ ko̱t kä kɛl.
text_en: Interactive design requires that you re-assess your assumptions about media production and learn to think in a non-linear ways.

text: Ca̱pla̱t ŋɔaani̱kɛɛl jɛn go̱o̱rɛ pröjekni ti̱ cäät kamni̱kiɛn kiɛ wɔ̱ kɛɛl, duŋni̱ bä derɛ gɔa mi̱ cuŋ nɔmɔ kɛ cuɔ̱ŋdɛ bä.
text_en: Interactive design requires that components of a project connect to each other, but also make sense as a separate entity.

text: Jɛn min ji̱äk kä ti̱i̱c  näänä kiɛ lɛnthi̱thni̱ thurɛ kä thi̱äkä ɛ jɛn min bɛɛ nööŋ ɛ la mi̱ di̱i̱t kɛnɛ ɣöö bi̱ lɛnthi̱ni̱ elemɛni̱ nämbäriɛn ɛ go̱ri̱ bi̱ pek guäcdiɛn bäriɛn di̱tni̱ jɛn ɛlɔ̱ŋ mi̱ läny praam lɛnthi̱thni̱.
text_en: The disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the focal complexity and number of lens elements required to achieve a range of focal lengths is much greater than for prime lenses.

text: Nɛmɛ cuɛ cop ni̱kä ɣöö cua riɛk mi̱ tɔt mëë ci̱ nɛy tin la̱tkɛ lɛni̱ jɛ luäŋ kɛ ɣöö  cuɛ räth ni̱kä pek in görkɛ.
text_en: This is becoming less of an issue as lens manufacturers achieve higher standards in lens production.

text: Nɛmɛ cua dhuum lɛnthɛthni̱ jakä ɣöö bɛ thurɛ ni̱ ti̱ gɔw nööŋ ti̱ la̱nykɛ lɛnthi̱thni̱ tin ca la̱t ɛ la ɣöö  /ci̱kɛ räth ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: This has allowed zoom lenses to produce pictures of a quality comparable to that achieved by lenses with fixed focal length.

text: Dɔ̱diɛn mëë cuu jiääk kä dhuum lɛnthi̱thni̱ jɛn lëpdɛ ɛ di̱i̱t (jɛn i̱thpi̱t) duŋdiɛn kɛn lɛni̱ ni̱ ciaaŋ la tëë piny.
text_en: Another disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the maximum aperture (the speed) of the lens is usually lower.

text: Nɛmɛ cuɛ jakä /ci̱kɛ pek mi̱ di̱i̱t  bi̱ naŋ kɛn dhuum lɛnthi̱thni̱ kɛ la̱tdiɛn gua̱a̱ mi̱ kuiy-buaydɛ mi̱ /thiɛlɛ pi̱la̱c.
text_en: This makes inexpensive zoom lenses hard to use in low-light conditions without a flash.

text: Riɛk kɛl ɛ di̱t ɛlɔ̱ŋ   gua̱th in laa tuɔɔkɛ ni ciaŋ,  mi̱ gɛ̈r kɛ mubi̱ kä ɣöö ba guic kɛ DVD bɛ rɔ cu i̱thkan ni̱ lɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: One of the most common problems when trying to convert a movie to DVD format is the overscan.

text: Televisioni ti ŋuan caa kɛ täth kɛ duɔ̱p mi bi̱ lo̱c nath bɛr..
text_en: Most televisions are made in a way to please the general public.

text: Kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ, tindial tin laa nɛɛni kä TV te kɛn kɛ kam, nhial, piny kɛnɛ gëëkiɛn.
text_en: For that reason, everything you see on the TV had the borders cut, top, bottom and sides.

text: Nɛmɛ la̱tkɛ kɛ ɣöö bi thurɛ waŋ i̱thki̱rnä kum kɛɛliw. Jɛn ba cu cɔli̱ ɛ ɣɔbɔri̱thkan.
text_en: This is made to ensure that the image covers the whole screen. That is called overscan.

text: Kɛ ɣöö /thiɛlɛ lua̱ŋdɛ, mi lätdi DVD, la geekɛ laa tuɔɔk ɣi bikɛ rɔ ŋuɔk bä, kɛnɛ ɣöö mi ci kuɛ̈ɛ̈n pilimkä thieek kɛ piny ɛlɔŋ, caa kɛ bi luäŋ kɛ nen kɛn dial.
text_en: Unfortunately, when you make a DVD, it's borders will most likely be cut too, and if the video had subtitles too close to the bottom, they won't be fully shown.

text: Duël tin di̱t tëë wal cikɛ cär nath bɛɛr kɛ gua̱a̱th mi bäär, no̱o̱ŋ kɛn cär ŋa̱a̱ri ko̱o̱ri jiöŋkööri, nyuaak kɛnɛ ruec Arthur ëë wal.
text_en: The traditional medieval castle has long inspired the imagination, conjuring up images of jousts, banquets and Arthurian chivalry.

text: Cuɛ ŋot tëë cuŋä   rɛy runi̱ ti̱i̱ bathdɔɔri̱ tëë caa ya̱rɛ kä jɛn la ja tiɛmkɛ ɛ thi̱a̱k rɛy cäri̱ nath kä la cua̱ bä ni̱ ta̱a̱ ko̱o̱ri̱ tëë ci̱ tuɔɔk ni̱ wal ɛlɔ̱ŋ, cuɛ ce̱tkɛ mi̱ liɛŋkɛ ni̱ pɛ̈ɛ̈n ŋɔaani̱ mi̱ took rɔ rɛy duëli̱ yieenä tin ca tɛ̈t piny.
text_en: Even standing amidst thousand year-old ruins it is easy to bring to mind the sounds and smells of battles long gone, to almost hear the clatter of hooves on the cobbles and to smell the fear rising from the dungeon pits.

text: Duŋni̱ ɣöö derɛ in jɛn luɔtkɛ ɛ min ca̱a̱tkɛ ni̱kɛ jɛ? Ɛŋu kɛn ti̱e̱c mëë kɔn kɛ la a̱kɛ nhiam? Kä ta̱th kɛ kɛ i̱di̱ ɛ nëë kä cua kɛ la̱t?
text_en: But is our imagination based on reality? Why were castles built in the first place? How were they designed and built?

text: Kɛ jɛn rɛy gua̱th ɛmɔ kärɔa, Kirbi̱ Mudhloe Ka̱thtle  cuɛ ti̱c mi̱ caa riali̱kä ɛlɔ̱ŋ mi̱ länyni̱ ka̱thtle in thuɔ̱k.
text_en: Typical for the period, Kirby Muxloe Castle is more of a fortified house than a true castle.

text: Jɛn tekɛ wärnyini̱ nääni̱ ti̱ di̱t kä pänydɛ ciwɛ ɛ /cɛ de buɔ̱m ɛlɔ̱ŋ mi̱ ca bök kui̱ ko̱o̱ri̱ kɛ kɔr gua̱th mi̱ bäär ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Its large glazed windows and thin walls would not have been able to resist a determined attack for long.

text: Rɛy 1480ni̱, mëë la̱tkɛ jɛ cua tok ɛ Kuäär ni̱ Ha̱thtiŋ, jɛn wec ɛ nëë cuɛ ce̱tkɛ mi̱ tëë rɛy malä kä ga̱k ɛ mi̱ la go̱o̱ri̱ pek mi̱ tɔt kɛ kui̱ nɛɛni̱ tin de naath ma̱k kɛ ɣöö bi̱kɛ ko̱r ka̱p rɛy wec.
text_en: In the 1480s, when its construction was begun by Lord Hastings, the country was relatively peaceful and defense was only required against small bands of roving marauders.

text: Jɛn ta̱a̱ päärä bumä cua cuɔ̱p mi̱ ci̱ döör ji̱ Yurɔpiaan mi̱ cu kɛnɛ i̱ ɛ ta̱a̱ mi̱ rɔm kɛ ɣöö bi̱ wi̱i̱ Yurɔpiaan ŋot cuŋ kɛ ɛ la kɛn.
text_en: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states.

text: Cua jɛn mëë cua ŋa̱c ɛ döör Yurɔpian diaal kɛ ga̱ŋdiɛn kɛ ɣöö de buɔ̱mni̱ wec kɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ, kä kumɛ wec cuɛ bun nɛɛni̱ tin tekɛ kɛɛl nyɔk kɛ gër kɛ ɣöö bɛ kɛ kulɛ ŋot päär buɔ̱mdiɛn.
text_en: The concept was that all European nations had to seek to prevent one nation from becoming powerful, and thus national governments often changed their alliances in order to maintain the balance.

text: Jɛn mëë Guur Ko̱r duŋ I̱thpani̱c cua jɛn tuk köör ëë nhiam kä cua̱ riɛk ëë te niɛ däärɛ mëë cuu ɛ jɛn pääri̱ bumä.
text_en: The War of Spanish Succession marked the first war whose central issue was the balance of power.

text: Nɛmɛ cua jɛn mëë di̱i̱t ëë ci̱ gɛ̈ɛ̈rɛ nööŋ, cie mi̱ ɛn buɔ̱m Yurɔpiaani̱ /känɛ lɛ ŋot ɛnɣöö bi̱ jɛnɛ ko̱r kuthni̱ tin palkɛ, Kɛ kɔrɛ, rɛy di̱ɔ̱k runi̱ Kör cua jɛn ko̱r in jɔk mëë cua lar i̱ ɛ ko̱r kuthnil tin palkɛ.
text_en: This marked an important change, as European powers would no longer have the pretext of being religious wars. Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war.

text: Jɛn tämpuɔl dua Artemith mëë tek Epi̱thɔ̱th cua däk kɛ payyietni̱ 21, 356 BCE rɛy la̱t mi̱ cua lɛl ɛ Ɣerɔthtrata̱th.
text_en: The temple of Artemis at Ephesus was destroyed on July 21, 356 BCE in an act of arson committed by Herostratus.

text: Kɛ min ca lat rɛy lɛ̈ŋä nɛmɛ, mëë cuɛ nhɔk tekä ɣöö derɛ jɔɔc kiɛ ɛni̱ gua̱a̱th bɛ ko̱k thi̱n, Kɛn Ji̱ Epi̱thɛth, kɛ kui ciaaŋ ji̱ääkä, cua lat i̱ jɛn ci̱öt Ɣeröɣhtrata̱th /ka̱nɛ met gɔ̱a̱r piny rɛy wargakni̱.
text_en: According to the story, his motivation was fame at any cost. The Ephesians, outraged, announced that Herostratus' name never be recorded.

text: Kä i̱thtörian raan Greek ni̱ Ithrabö kɛ kɔrɛ cuɛ ci̱ötdɛ ŋa̱c, mëë cua kulɛ ŋäcɛ määni̱ walɛ, Jɛn tämpuɔl cua däk nikɛɛ jɛn wäär ɛmɔ mëë cua dap  Alɛdhanɛr indi̱i̱t kɛ jɛ.
text_en: The Greek historian Strabo later noted the name, which is how we know today. The temple was destroyed on the same night that Alexander the Great was born.

text: Aledhandɛr, mëë ɛ kuär, cuɛ go̱r i̱ bɛ luak palä nyɔk kɛ lätni̱ ɛ cuɛɛ ŋɔak yuɔr kɛ kuidɛ, duŋni̱ cua kɛ lo̱k, Kɔrɛ, mëë ci̱ Aledhandɛr li̱w, jɛn luak palä cua nyɔk kɛ lätni̱ rɛy 323 BCE.
text_en: Alexander, as king, offered to pay to rebuild the temple, but his offer was denied. Later, after Alexander died, the temple was rebuilt in 323 BCE.

text: Ŋäcni̱ jɛ ɛ gɔa i̱ ɛnɣöö jakni̱ tetdu kä bi̱ lɔɔr kiɛ päl ɛ kɔ̱c ni̱ määth mi dɔ̱ŋ luɔtdɛ rɔ kä niɛ wa̱nɛ bi cu ŋot gɔ̱ɔ̱riɛ ni̱ kuurä- ɣɔ̱nɛ bä i̱ /ci̱ tetku bi̱ tuɔ̱ɔ̱p kä dɔ̱ŋ derɛɛ thi̱em.
text_en: Make sure your hand is as relaxed as possible while still hitting all the notes correctly - also try not to make much extraneous motion with your fingers.

text: Duɔ̱ɔ̱p ɛmɛ, bɛ tuɔɔk i̱ bi̱ wä kɛ mi̱ ̱jakɛ ji̱ käcuc ɛ määth ɛ määth. Timɛ ɛn ɣöö thiɛlɛ mi̱ go̱o̱r ɣöö biɛ thöt kɛ nhiet ni̱ bum ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛɛ jɔw mi̱ di̱i̱t mi̱ ce̱tkɛ jɛn pianö.
text_en: This way, you will tire yourself out as little as possible. Remember there's no need to hit the keys with a lot of force for extra volume like on the piano.

text: Mi̱ jɛn luäŋɛ rɔ, kɛ ɣöö deri̱ ba̱li̱ömdɛ rep, ji̱n lätni̱ kä pek in te piny kɛ ɣöö biɛ cu nhiɛt ni̱ lɔ̱ŋ kiɛ kɛ pɛ̈th.
text_en: On the accordion, to get extra volume, you use the bellows with more pressure or speed.

text: Maiti̱thi̱dhi̱öm jɛn ɛ duɔ̱p mi̱  guɔ̱ɔ̱r kɛ ɣöö bi̱ naath tekɛ maar mi gɔa kɛ min palkɛ, mi̱ ŋäckɛ, kiɛ mi̱ ba ta̱a̱dɛ ŋa̱c i̱ tëë thi̱n ɛn min di̱i̱t kä jɔc, min te wi̱kä ti̱diaal, yiëë in thuɔ̱k, kiɛ Kuoth.
text_en: Mysticism is the pursuit of communion with, identity with, or conscious awareness of an ultimate reality, divinity, spiritual truth, or God.

text: Kɛn ji̱ ŋäthä cuɛ go̱r tekɛ ŋäc la̱t mi̱ ro̱ŋ, gua̱th lätni̱, kiɛ rɛy cärä mi̱ wä kä cääk in thuɔ̱k/ kɛn wuutni̱ kiɛ kuth mään.
text_en: The believer seeks a direct experience, intuition, or insight into divine reality/the deity or dieties.

text: Nɛy tëë guurɛ cua go̱r i̱ bikɛ ŋot kɛ mi rɔm kɛn ɛ thi̱n kɛ dup ciaaŋä te̱e̱kä ti ca lɛy, kiɛ la̱thdiɛn lät kɛ ɣöö ba la̱tdiɛn kulɛ ŋa̱c kɛ gua̱a̱diɛn.
text_en: Followers pursue certain ways of living, or practices that are intended to nurture those experiences.

text: La̱dhembourg tëkɛ lɛ̈ŋ mi̱ bäär duŋdɛ ɣöö jɛn cuɛ cuɔ̱ŋ kärɔa ni̱ rɛy ni̱ni̱ ti̱ tokɛ kä 1839.
text_en: Mysticism can be distinguished from other forms of religious belief and worship by its emphasis on the direct personal experience of a unique state of consciousness, particularly those of a peaceful, insightful, blissful, or even ecstatic character.

text: Ɛn ŋa̱th Cikhä ɛ ŋa̱th kä ji̱ wi̱i̱ni̱ tin tä kui̱i̱ Inida. Tuɔɔkɛ rɛy wec mi̱ cɔali̱ Punjab kɛ där cɛntäri̱ ëë la 15dɛ gua̱a̱th ëë ci̱ ciaaŋ ji̱ Hindu rɔɔdɛ da̱a̱k.
text_en: Sikhism is a religion from the Indian sub-continent. It originated in the Punjab region during the 15th century from a sectarian split within the Hindu tradition.

text: Kɛn Cikni̱ laa guickɛn ŋa̱thdiɛn ɛ la mi̱ göl kä ŋa̱th Hindukä duŋdɛ ɣöö ŋickɛn ciɛŋ kɛnɛ ŋuɔ̱t ji̱ Hindu.
text_en: Sikhs consider their faith to be a separate religion from Hinduism though they acknowledge its Hindu roots and traditions.

text: Kɛn Cikni̱ cɔɔlkɛn ŋa̱thdiɛn i̱ Gurmat, ɛ la thok ji̱ Punjab mi̱ lot ni̱ "duɔ̱ɔ̱p guru". Ɛn guru ɛ ŋi̱i̱c mi̱ tä kɛɛ luɔt mi̱ di̱i̱t ɛlɔ̱ŋ rɛy ruaacni̱ ŋäthä kä ji̱ Indiani̱ diaal duŋdɛ ɣöö kä ŋa̱th Cikhä jɛn cɛ min bumni̱jɛn kä tin ŋäthkɛ ɛ kɛn Cikni̱ käp ɛ bum rɛy lätni̱i̱kiɛn.
text_en: Sikhs call their religion Gurmat, which is Punjabi for "way of the guru". The guru is a fundamental aspect of all Indian religions but in Sikhism has taken on an importance that forms the core of Sikh beliefs.

text: Ɛn ŋa̱th ɛmɔ cuaa ben yiath piny kɛɛ cɛntäri̱ ëë la 15dɛ ɛ Guru Nanak (1469–1539). Cuaa ben guɔ̱ɔ̱r ɛ guruni̱ da̱ŋ bäŋuan ti̱ kɔ̱kiɛn.
text_en: The religion was founded in the 15th century by Guru Nanak (1469–1539). There followed in succession a further nine gurus.

text: Duŋdɛ ɣöö, kɛ pay Bäkɛl 1956, Krushchev's promises were put to the test when riots in Poland, where workers were protesting against food shortages and wage cuts, turned into a general protest against Communism.
text_en: However, in June 1956, Krushchev's promises were put to the test when riots in Poland, where workers were protesting against food shortages and wage cuts, turned into a general protest against Communism.

text: Kuɛɛ laa ɣöö kɛɛ jɔak, ɛn Krucicɛb cuɛɛ dibabni̱ ja̱k kɛ ɣöö baa ŋuɔ̱t nyɔk kɛ loc thi̱n, cuɛɛ jɛ ben nhɔk bɔ̱ ɛn ɣöö bɛ ruac ëë görkɛ ɛ naath kɛ kui̱i̱ yupä kuakni̱ kä cuɛɛ cuu nhɔk ɛn ɣöö bɛ Uladithlɔw Gɔmulka ëë ŋa̱ckɛ ɛ nɛy diaal cuu nööŋ nhial ɛ la jɛn kuäär wec in pay kuany.
text_en: Although in the end, Krushchev sent in tanks to restore order, he did give way to some economic demands and agreed to appoint the popular Wladyslaw Gomulka as the new prime minister.

text: Ɛn Cuɔ̱p rɛy Lo̱o̱lä kä Indu ɛ ɛ jɛn cuɔ̱p bɔ̱ kä Run tëë ta̱a̱th kɛɛ Läŋ kui̱i̱ nhiam caam ɣɔaa kä India kɛɛliw, wëë kɛ rɛy Pakithtan ëë pay täth kɛnɛ tha̱a̱ŋ wi̱i̱ni̱ tëë nhiam caam ɣɔaa kä India kɛ nhiam caam ɣɔaa kä Apganithtan.
text_en: The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilisation in the northwest Indian subcontinent encompassing most of modern-day Pakistan and some regions in northwest India and northeast Afghanistan.

text: Ɛn cuɔ̱p ɛmɔ cuaa tia̱a̱p a gɔaa rɛy yiëër Indus River gua̱a̱th ëë kuɛɛ ciötdɛ ben jiäk thi̱n.
text_en: The civilisation flourished in the basins of the Indus River wherefore it derives its name.

text: Ɛ cieŋ ɛ mëë la tha̱a̱ŋ nɛyni̱ tin la gɔ̱a̱a̱r jɛ laa lat ɛn ɣöö mëë tuɔkɛ ɣöö bi̱ naath cop kui̱i̱ yiëër in ci̱ ben kööt in ku laa Sarasvati River,dëë jɛ cɔl i̱ Indus-Sarasvati Civilization,gua̱a̱th in ku tha̱a̱ŋ nath jɛ cɔl i̱ Harappan Civilization kɛ kɔr Harappa, in ku laa gua̱a̱th in nhiam ëë tɛ̈tkɛ kɛ ruɔ̱n 1920ni̱.
text_en: Although some scholars speculate that since the civilisation also existed in the basins of the now dried up Sarasvati River, it should be aptly called the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization, while some call it the Harappan Civilization after Harappa, the first of its sites to be excavated in the 1920s.

text: Ta̱a̱ ëë caa dëcni̱ köör kuäärä ji̱ Rööm ŋieec kɛ jɛ cɛ kɛ luäk ɛlɔ̱ŋ lätni̱ nyinä duëlwal diaal tëë naŋkɛ naath nhiam.
text_en: The militaristic nature of the Roman empire aided in the development of medical advances.

text: Cuaa däktööri  cuu moc kɛ lät kɛ Kuäär ni̱ Agäthtuth kä cuɛɛ Muktäb Duëlwa̱l kä Rööm yiath piny kɛ kui̱i̱ nɛyni̱ tëë ci̱ luny jɔk rɛy köör.
text_en: Doctors began to be recruited by Emperor Augustus and even formed the first Roman Medical Corps for use in the aftermath of battles.

text: Kɛn däktööri̱ tëë laa rɛ̈t kɛ naath kɛ nɛy ti̱ tä kɛ ŋäc mi̱ di̱i̱t rɛy wal diaal tëë la naath a jakä kä laa nin amäni̱ wäl in laa näk bɛ̈c pua̱a̱ny tin laa ka̱mkɛ raar rɛy dɛɛyni̱ jiɛn kɛnɛ ithkɔlɔpiin in laa jiëkɛ kä dɛy wal.
text_en: Surgeons had knowledge of various sedatives including morphine from extracts of poppy seeds and scopolamine from herbane seeds.

text: Cuu kɛn kɛ ŋa̱c amäni̱ ŋuɔ̱k ciökni̱ nath kɛ ɣöö /ci̱ ri̱ŋ in ci̱ tööl bi̱ lɛ wa̱a̱y a bɛ puɔ̱ny kɛɛliw dɔp amäni̱ min la riɛm laa pen ja̱l kɛnɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p in laa kɛ riɛm rɛy lɔaac kɛ ɣöö /cɛ bi̱ lɛ ja̱l.
text_en: They became proficient at amputation to save patients from gangrene as well as tourniquets and arterial clamps to stem blood flow.

text: Rɛy runi̱ ti̱ kur ti̱ ŋuan, ɛn kuäär ji̱ Rööm cɛ gɔy ti̱ di̱t nööŋ rɛy lätni̱ kɛ kui̱i̱ wal kä ɛ jɛn ci̱ ɣɔw moc kɛ ŋäc ɛ di̱i̱t ɛ tä thi̱nɛ amäni̱ walɛ.
text_en: Over multiple centuries, the Roman empire led to great gains in the field of medicine and formed much of the knowledge we know today.

text: Pi̱o̱rlan ɔrigami̱ ɛ cuuŋni̱ warɛgakä kä kɛɛl mi̱ /caa loc kä ti̱ ŋuan, Cuuŋni̱ ti̱ ŋuan ti̱ luɔckɛ /caa kɛ nhɔk, kä gua̱th diaal tin caa cuɔ̱ɔ̱ŋ täkɛ rɛy gua̱thni̱ ti̱ caa rɔ̱ riny.
text_en: Pureland origami is origami with the restriction that only one fold may be done at a time, more complex folds like reverse folds are not allowed, and all folds have straightforward locations.

text: Ɛn nɔmɔ tääthɛ wut mi̱ cɔali̱ John Ithmith kɛ rɛy runi̱ ti̱ 1970-ni̱ kɛ ɣöö bɛ nɛy tin ŋäcdiɛn kä cuɔ̱ŋ warɛgakni̱ kiɛ nɛy tin kuiy cärkiɛn kä ta̱th ŋuaani̱ ku lɛ ŋieec.
text_en: It was developed by John Smith in the 1970s to help inexperienced folders or those with limited motor skills.

text: Gaat bi̱kɛ piith kɛ ta̱a̱ tɛktɛk kä kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ kuäthä min la babkɛ do̱r ɛ ŋotkɛ kuɛ̈ɛ̈ kɛnɛ ɣöö kɛn ciɛŋ kuäthä kɛ baab yär kɛn ciɛŋkiɛn.
text_en: Children develop an awareness of race and racial stereotypes quite young and these racial stereotypes affect behavior.

text: Niɛ gua̱a̱ mɔ, gaat ba rɔ̱ jiek ɛ la nɛy ti̱ tɔt ti̱ caa tɛk kiɛ koc ɛ bab kɛkɛ kä /ci̱kɛ bi̱ lät ɛ gɔaa rɛy duëlgɔ̱rä ni̱ ciaaŋ /ci̱kɛ bi̱lɛ gɔw duelgɔ̱r gua̱th in caa ŋa̱c ɛn kuëëth kɛ baab i̱ mi̱ caa mat kɛ ta̱a̱ dööriɛn.
text_en: For instance, children who identify with a racial minority that is stereotyped as not doing well in school tend to not do well in school once they learn about the stereotype associated with their race.

text: MySpace ɛ jɛn warɛgak in diɔ̱ɔ̱kdiɛn kɛ di̱t min lät kɛ naath rɛy wec United States kä tëë kɛ ciööt nath ti̱ miliöni ti̱ 54 ɛn täämɛ.
text_en: MySpace is the third most popular website used in the United States and has 54 million profiles currently.

text: Kɛn wargakni rɛy jɔam ti̱ti̱ ci naath wi̱cdiɛn lɛ riet thi̱n ɛ lɔ̱ŋ, ce̱tkɛ nyin ŋi̱i̱ca ti̱ti̱.
text_en: These websites have gotten a lot of attention, especially in the education setting.

text: Tëëkɛ ti gɔa thi̱n rɛy wargakni tin ca gɔ̱a̱r rɛy jɔam ɛmɛ, ce̱tkɛ, ɣöö deri duɔ̱ɔ̱r tok kɛ läth thi̱n ɛ thia̱k ce̱tkɛ ruaacni rɛy jɔam ti gööl, bidiöni, thurɛni, kɛnɛ tin kɔ̱kiɛn.
text_en: There are positive aspects to these websites, which include, being able to easily setup a class page which can include blogs, videos, photos, and other features.

text: Warɛgakni Rɛy jɔam ti̱ti̱ dëë kɛ mal jek ɛ thia̱k gua̱a̱th tɔ̱wkädɛ kɛl mi ca rialikä, mi dee jɛ jakä thia̱k kɛ tietdɛ kɛnɛ ɣöö dëë mal tuany rɛc ɛ thia̱k ɛ gaat duël gɔ̱rä tin dee tuanynidiɛn kɛnɛ gɔ̱a̱riɛn buɔ̱m kä kɛ.
text_en: This page can easily be accessed by providing just one web address, which makes it easy to remember and easy to type in for students who may have trouble using the keyboard or with spelling.

text: Dëë jɛ rialikä kɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p in görkɛ kɛ ɣöö dee kuëndɛ kulɛ thia̱k kä derɛ jɛ moc bä kiɛ kɛ biɛl mi kuiy ce̱tkɛ ta̱a̱ in görkɛ.
text_en: It can be customized to make it easy to read and also with as much or little color as desired.

text: Atɛnciɔn Dɛpithit Dithɔrdär "ɛ juäy rääl mi̱ la ŋith ran laa jakä wiel, kä yuth räl pua̱a̱ny ran, kä mooc raan buɔ̱mi̱ di̱i̱t kɛnɛ la̱t mi̱ di̱i̱t".
text_en: Attention Deficit Disorder "is a neurological syndrome whose classic defining triad of symptoms including impulsivity, distractibility, and hyperactivity or excess energy".

text: /Ciɛ buɔ̱m kä raan, ɛ jɔɔk ni̱ jɛn; laa "kääpɛ pek gan da̱ŋ 3-5 kä kuɔ̱r, dëë jɛ diw ɛn ɣöö copkɛn gaat Amɛrika ti̱ miliööni̱ da̱ŋ 2".
text_en: It is not a learning disability, it is a learning disorder; it "affects 3 to 5 percent of all children, perhaps as many as 2 million American children".

text: Gaat ti̱ tä kɛɛ ADD /ci̱ kɛn rɔ̱ laa luäŋ kɛ päl piny rɛy kä tin lätkɛn kɛ ciee kɛ lät duëlgɔ̱rä, duŋdɛ ɣöö dee kɛn rɔ' pa̱l piny rɛy lätni̱ tin nhɔk kɛn kɛ ciee ŋa̱a̱ri̱ kiɛ guec kä tin nhɔk kɛn kɛ kiɛ gɔ̱a̱r rieetni̱ ti̱ /caa kamkiɛn dääk.
text_en: Children with ADD have a hard time focusing on things like school work, but they can concentrate on things they enjoy doing like playing games or watching their favorite cartoons or writing sentences without punctuation.

text: Kɛn gaat ti̱ti̱ la kɛn rɔ̱ laa jiäk rɛy rikni̱ ti̱ ŋuan, kɛ ɣöö la kɛn "laa lät rɛy lätni̱ ti̱ bɛ̈cbɛ̈ɛ̈c ti̱ riɛk nööŋ, bi̱ kɛ rɔ̱ jiäk rɛy ko̱o̱ri̱, kä bi̱ kɛ nɛy ti̱ tä kɛ ŋuɔ̱t gak" ɛ jɛn bi̱ wicdiɛn ku lɛ lät a gɔaaɔ, kɛ ɣöö /ci̱ wicdiɛn lät a gɔaa kɛ tin la̱tkɛ ɛ nɛy ti̱ loy wicdiɛn.
text_en: These children tend to get into a lot of trouble, because they "engage in risky behaviors, get into fights, and challenge authority" in order to stimulate their brain, since their brain can not be stimulated by normal methods.

text: Ɛn ADD la yiärɛ ciaaŋ maarä kɛ gaat tin kɔ̱kiɛn tin /caa luɔt kä min jakɛ kä tä i̱nɔ ŋäc kiɛ min jakɛ kä bi̱ kɛn rieet dui̱r kɛ kuën kiɛ min jak pieth runi̱i̱kiɛn kä göl kä gaat tin kɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: ADD affects relationships with other peers because other children can not understand why they act the way that they do or why they spell they way they do or that their maturity level is different.

text_en: When the individuals show several variants of a particular trait they are polymorphic.

text_en: Army ant colonies march and nest in different phases as well.

text: Kɛ ta̱a̱ in daan in laa ɣöth kɛ rɛl la kɛn la ɣöth kɛ wäär kä bi̱ kɛ lɔ̱ɔ̱ŋ kɛ cäŋdäär.
text_en: In the nomadic phase, army ants march at night and stop to camp during the day.

text: Jɛn buɔ̱l rɛɛl la kɛn jäliɛn laa took mi̱ ci̱ kuän kuɛ̈ɛ̈. Kɛ jɛn ta̱a̱ ja̱l ɛmɔ lä kɛn laa lɔ̱ŋ gua̱thni̱ ti̱ la kɛn kaa gɛɛr ni̱ ciaŋ.
text_en: The colony begins a nomadic phase when available food has decreased. During this phase, the colony makes temporary nests that are changed everyday.

text: Ɣɛn ɣöth kɛl ɛmɛ de̱rɛ pe̱k mi̱ ciä ni̱n wäl barɔw naŋ.
text_en: Each of these nomadic rampages or marches lasts for approximately 17 days.

text: Thël ɛ le̱e̱ŋu? ɣɛn ciöt i̱ "thël"ɛ rie̱t Latin mi̱ lot ni̱ ɣöö "due̱l mi̱ tɔt" kä caa rialikä kɛɛ nhiam ɛ  nɛy tin ŋa̱c kɛ ta̱a̱ maiykɔrɔthämin guic jɛ ɣɛn kuum.
text_en: What is a cell? The word cell comes from the Latin word "cella", meaning "small room", and it was first coined by a microscopist observing the structure of cork.

text: Ɣɛn thël ɛjɛn tuk ŋɔaani̱ diaal kɛ ta̱a̱ te̱e̱kä kä tin diaal tin tëk ,kä kɛn te̱ duɔ̱r kɛ thël kɛl kiɛ ti̱ ŋuan.
text_en: The cell is the basic unit of all living things, and all organisms are composed of one or more cells.

text: Thël kɛ tuk kä duɔ̱r kä te̱ kɛn kɛɛ luɔt kɛ ta̱a̱ in guɛc kɛ ni̱ tëk, kɛ thuɔ̱k dɛ kɛn laa kɛ laa cɔal kɛ i̱ "cuŋ kiɛ päny te̱e̱kä".
text_en: Cells are so basic and critical to the study of life, in fact, that they are often referred to as "the building blocks of life".

text: Ɣɛn tää ŋidhä kɛnɛ räl jɛn jakɛ la̱t kä gɔaa kɛ ɣöö laa jäkɛ räl kä puɔ̱ɔ̱ny kɛliw kɛ ɣöö bi̱ riɛm ku lɛ ja̱l ɛgɔaa puɔ̱ɔ̱ny ran ɛ thiɛl diw.
text_en: The Nervous System maintains homeostasis by sending nerve impulses through out the body to keep the flow of blood going as well as undisturbed.

text: Kɛn räl pua̱ny ɛti̱ dëë kɛ ja̱k kɛ pɛth puɔ̱ɔ̱ny kɛɛliw kä luäkɛ puɔ̱ny kɛ mi̱ de̱e̱ jɛ moc riɛk.
text_en: These nerve impulses can be sent so quickly throughout the body which helps keep the body safe from any potential threat.

text: Roth laa yär kɛn ni̱ gua̱th tin tiɔtni kɛ päär ni̱ diɛn kɛ thuɔ̱l tin bɛc bɛɛc,duŋ dɛ ɣöö ya̱r kɛ ŋɔak dial dupni̱ tin tuɔk kɛ rɔ̱ thi̱n.̱
text_en: Tornadoes strike a small area compared to other violent storms, but they can destroy everything in their path.

text: Roth la kɛn jiɛn laa yut,wooc kɛn jiɛn puɔ̱ny duël nhial, kä jak kɛn thuɔ̱rbiɛɛli̱ kä wä nhial.Min jiäk ni̱ jɛn ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ thëm dɛ ni̱ kä rɛɛw kä roth thukɛ kɛ thaakni̱ ti̱ bääl diɔ̱k.
text_en: Tornadoes uproot trees, rip boards from buildings, and fling cars up into the sky. The most violent two percent of tornadoes last more than three hours.

text: Kɛn thuɔ̱l tɔ̱ di̱t ɛtɔ̱ te̱ kɛn kɛ jɔam ti̱ 480 km/h(133m/s;300mph).
text_en: These monster storms have winds up to 480 km/h (133 m/s; 300 mph).

text: Naath te̱ kɛn lät ne̱e̱ni̱ kä lät kɛn kɛ kɛ ɣöö bi̱ ŋɔak jɔɔc ɛla ti̱ di̱t ni̱ kɛ pe̱k runi̱ ti̱i̱ bathdɔɔri̱ kɛnɛ bathdɔɔri̱.
text_en: Humans have been making and using lenses for magnification for thousands and thousands of years.

text: Kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ, kɛn yio̱m tin laa guɛc kɛ ŋɔak tin thuɔ̱ɔ̱k la̱t kɛ kɛ kä Yurɔp kɛ pe̱k runi̱ ti̱ 16 bathdɔɔri̱ ti̱ ci̱ wä.
text_en: However, the first true telescopes were made in Europe in the late 16th century.

text: Kɛn tin laa guɛc kɛ ni̱ ŋɔak kɛn lät kɛn kɛ ne̱ni̱ da̱ŋ rɛw kɛ ɣöö bi̱ gua̱a̱th te̱ ŋɔak thi̱n kulɛ thia̱k kä bi̱ kɛ jɔɔc ɛla ti̱ di̱t.
text_en: These telescopes used a combination of two lenses to make distant objects appear both nearer and larger.

text: Di̱t lɔac kɛnɛ tiɛɛl bi̱ kɛ te̱e̱ kɔn ni̱ ciaŋ kä ɛ jɛn ta̱a̱ dan min te̱ kɔn mi̱ go̱r nɛy tin ŋuan ni̱ kɛn ŋɔak  je̱k kɛ gua̱th mi̱ tɔt kɛ ta̱a̱ tiilä.
text_en: Greed and selfishness will always be with us and it is the nature of cooperation that when the majority benefit there will always be more to gain in the short term by acting selfishly

text: Mi lotdɛ rɔ, nɛy ti̱ ŋuan gɔaɛ ɣɛn ɣöö min la tää in bäär in de̱e̱ raan ɛ la̱t ɛ ɣöö de̱rɛ lät kɛ naath kɛl.
text_en: Hopefully, most people will realise that their long term best option is to work together with others.

text: Nɛy ti̱ ŋuan läk kɛn läk i̱kä kɛ cäŋɔ de̱e̱ raan wä jäl kä kuɛl mi̱ dɔ̱ŋ ɛ de̱r wi̱cmuɔ̱ni̱ ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ lɛ jäl, thääŋ nath ga̱a̱c kɛn ɛŋu te̱e̱ thɔ̱ŋɛ mi̱i̱ tha̱a̱ŋ nath ŋääth kɛnɛ i̱ tëë kɛ ti̱ cɔali̱ ɣëliani̱ kiɛ tëë kɛ ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ ti̱ tëk wi̱i̱muɔ̱n mi̱ dɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Many people dream of the day when humans can travel to another star and explore other worlds, some people wonder what's out there some belive that aliens or other life may live on another plant.

text: Duŋdɛ ɣöö,mi̱ ciää nɛmɛ mi̱ cɛ tuɔk kä dɔ̱ŋ cɛ de̱e̱ tuɔk kɛ guäth mi̱ bäär. kuɛl te̱ kɛn guäthni̱ ti̱ gööl ɛ de̱e̱ kamkɛn te̱e̱ kɛ mi̱ naŋ rɔ kɛ pe̱k mi̱ bathdɔɔri̱ ti̱  ŋuan kamdiɛn kuɛl tin "cäät"
text_en: But, if this ever does happen probably won't happen for a very long time. The stars are so spread out that there are trillions of miles between stars that are "neighbors".

text: Kä dɔ̱ŋ kɛ cäŋ kɛl, gaat ganku bi̱ kɛ cuɔ̱ŋ wi̱i̱muɔ̱n ɣɛliani̱ kä bi̱ kɛ ga̱a̱c kɛ guändɔɔŋni̱ kiɛn tëë wal.
text_en: Maybe one day, your great grandchildren will be standing atop an alien world wondering about their ancient ancestors?

text: Le̱y caa kɛ la̱t  kɛ cuɔ̱ŋ ti̱ tɔatni̱ ti̱ guan. cam kɛn ŋɔak kä bi̱ kɛ thuɔ̱k rɛy jiɛc diɛn. Le̱y t ŋuan de̱e̱ kɛ jäl.
text_en: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move.

text: Kɛ ni̱ le̱y kärɔ̱ te̱ kɛ ŋiɛth (/ɛcäŋ ni̱ min c kɛ le̱y diaal jɛn tin te̱ kɛ ŋiɛdh; re̱c in cɔali̱ jɛli̱ kɛn ɛ cäät kä tin thiɛl ŋith).
text_en: Only animals have brains (though not even all animals do; jellyfish, for example, do not have brains).

text: Le̱y kɛn jëk kɛkɛ ŋuäthni̱ diaal wi̱i̱muɔ̱n. laa tɛt kɛn piny, ke̱t kɛn rɛy ba̱bdiitni̱ kä pär kɛn nhial.
text_en: Animals are found all over the earth. They dig in the ground, swim in the oceans, and fly in the sky.

text: Ɣɛn thël jɛn ɛmi̱ kuiy ni̱ jɛn ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä lät kä tëk kiɛ tin tëk.
text_en: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of a living (things) organism.

text: Thël bëë kä rie̱t ji̱ Latin mi̱ lotni̱ ɣöö due̱l mi̱ tɔt.
text_en: Cell comes from the Latin word cella which means small room.

text: Mi̱ ci̱ tin tëk guic kɛ min laa guɛc kɛni̱ kɛ (maykɔrɔthkɔp),biɛ nɛn ɣɛn ɣöö kɛn caa kɛ la̱t kɛ kurɛni̱ marɔbakä ti̱ tɔatni̱.
text_en: If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls.

text: Röbɛt Huuk, rami̱ ŋäc thaany we̱c in cɔali̱ Iŋlaan cɛ marabakni̱ ti̱ ŋuan rɛy kä tin laa guɛckɛ ni̱ ŋɔak kɛɛ maykɔrɔthkɔp.
text_en: Robert Hooke, a biologist from England, saw small squares in cork with a microscope.

text: Cët kɛn kɛ due̱l. Ɛjɛn ram in nhiam ɣëë kɔthëli̱ ti̱ ci̱ li̱w ŋa̱c.
text_en: They looked like rooms. He was the first person to observe dead cells

text: Ɣe̱lɛmɛni̱ kɛnɛ kɔmpuɔɔni̱ de̱e̱ kɛn jiɛn kä kɛl kä de̱e̱ kɛ wä kä min dɔ̱ŋ kä caa rɔ̱ gɛr.
text_en: Elements and compounds can move from one state to another and not change.

text: Nayti̱rögi̱n ɛla ji̱ɔm ŋotdɛ ta̱a̱ dɛ ɛjɛn ta̱a̱ kä ti̱ lawlaw kiɛ li̱kuitni̱. Jɛn ta̱a̱ ka̱ ti̱ lawlaw thiɛk ni̱ kɛn kuë laa ni̱ ɣöö ta̱a̱diɛn ɛjɛn kɛlɔ.
text_en: Nitrogen as a gas still has the same properties as liquid nitrogen. The liquid state is denser but the molecules are still the same.

text: Pi̱w kɛ cäät in dɔ̱ŋ diɛn. kɛn gua̱th pi̱i̱ni̱ jɛn tëë kä rɛɛw min la ɣäydi̱rögi̱ni̱ da̱ŋ rɛw kɛnɛ ɣɔ̱kthi̱ji̱n kɛl.
text_en: Water is another example. The compound water is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

text: Ɛjɛn ta̱a̱ ɛkɛlɔ kuë laa jiɔm, mi̱ lawlaw kiɛ mi̱ bumbum.
text_en: It has the same molecular structure whether it is a gas, liquid, or solid.

text: Ɛ cäŋ ni̱ min de̱e̱ ta̱a̱dɛ rɔ gɛr,ɛla ta̱a̱ kɛ̈mɛkɔ̱li̱ kɛ /cɛ rɔɔdɛ gɛr.
text_en: Although its physical state may change, its chemical state remains the same.

text: Thaak ɛmi̱ te̱ kɛɛl kɛ kɔn, kä jɛn tëë rɛy nyini̱ kɔn tin lät kɔn kɛ kä ŋot dɛ ci̱ kɔn ɛliŋ.
text_en: Time is something that is all around us, and affects everything we do, yet is difficult to understand.

text: Thaak nɛy tëë ci̱ jɛ riali̱kä kɛ ŋäc dɛ kɛ ji̱ luak kuɔth, ji̱ ŋäcä ŋɔaani̱ kɛnɛ tanyti̱i̱thni̱ kɛ kɔr runi̱ ti̱ bathdɔɔri̱.
text_en: Time has been studied by religious, philosophical, and scientific scholars for thousands of years.

text: Ci̱ kɔn ɛ je̱k ɣɛn ɣöö thaak tëë guäthni̱ ɛtookɛ ni̱ kä guäth ɛ bi̱ be̱n kɛɛ täämɛ ɛwä.
text_en: We experience time as a series of events passing from the future through the present to the past.

text: Thaak bä ɛ ɣöö ta̱a̱ in päär kɔn duɔ̱r kɛ jɛ guäthni̱
text_en: Time is also how we compare the duration (length) of events.

text: De̱ri̱ ta̱a̱ i  wä kɛɛ thaak bil kɛ ta̱a̱ in guic i̱ jɛ kɛ jɛ mi̱ locɛ rɔ kɛ wiälɛ. Ɣɛn duɔ̱r mi̱ locrɔ ɛ mi̱ wiäl kä wiäl ni̱ kä t ŋuan.
text_en: You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.

text: Kɔmpi̱ätɛrni̱̱ ɣɛn pe̱k ɛ thiäkɛ  la̱t kɛkɛ ni̱ la̱t ti̱ ce̱t kɛ rial bidi̱önii̱kä kɛnɛ thurɛni̱.
text_en: Computers today are used to manipulate pictures and videos.

text: Ɣɛn lät ni̱ kä ɣöö baa ŋɔak jaa ruac ce̱t kɛ raan agɔa la̱t kɛ jɛ kä kɔmpi̱ätɛrni̱, kä ta̱a̱ ɛ lɛl kɛ ni̱ ŋɔak kä ruac kɛ jɔw kä kompi̱ätɛr wëëkɛ mi̱ re̱p ɛ ni̱ rɔɔdɛ kä te̱lɛbi̱cɔni̱ kɛnɛ pilimni̱.
text_en: Sophisticated animations can be constructed on computers, and this kind of animation is increasingly being used in television and films.

text: Diit laa jɔw diɛn laa kua läth kɛ kä kɔmpi̱ätɛrni̱ kɛ ɣöö baa jɔw kulɛ mat kɛɛl agɔaa.
text_en: Music is often recorded using sophisticated computers to process and mix sounds together.

text: Kɛ pe̱k mi̱ ci̱ wä ni̱kɛ pe̱k rui ti̱ bathadɔɔri̱ ti̱ wal bäŋuan ɛwa kä bathdɔɔri̱ ti̱ jiɛn däŋ rɛw, Caa ŋäth ɣɛn ɣöö nɛy tin caa we̱c in cɔal Nie̱w dhi̱i̱laan jac kɛ nɛy ti̱ cɔali̱ ji̱ Maöri̱ ti̱ laa kak kɛ dit mi̱ cɔali̱ Maöth.
text_en: For a long time during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed the first inhabitants of New Zealand were the Maori people, who hunted giant birds called moas.

text: Ɣɛn  ta̱a̱ ɣëë caa lat jɛ ni̱ wal lat kɛ jɛ i̱ kɛn ji̱ Maöri̱ kɛn ɣo̱nh kɛ kä pöli̱ni̱thia kɛɛ böötni̱ ti̱ ŋuan ka̱ cuu kɛn Nie̱w Dhi̱i̱lɛ̈ɛ̈n naŋ ka ji Möriöri̱,kä cuu kɛnɛ jak kä gua̱th  pi̱thä.
text_en: The theory then established the idea that the Maori people migrated from Polynesia in a Great Fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori, establishing an agricultural society.

text: Kä i̱nɔ,tëë kɛ dup ti̱ bo̱o̱r ti̱ ti̱ lat ɣöö i̱ ji̱ mi̱riöri̱ ikɛ kɛn ji̱ we̱c in di̱i̱t ni mi̱riöri̱ tin ci̱ ɣöth kä Ni̱e̱w Dhi̱i̱lɛɛn ɛwä ka̱ dhuɔ̱ɔ̱l Cathäm kä cuu kɛn wä të kɛ ciɛŋ kiɛn.
text_en: However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture.

text: Tëë kɛ do̱r mi̱ dɔ̱ŋ kä dhuɔ̱li̱ Cathäm kɛn kɛ ji̱ Maöri̱ tin ci̱ ɣöth kä Nie̱w Dhi̱i̱lɛɛn.
text_en: There was also another tribe on the Chatham islands these were Maori who migrated away from New Zealand.

text: Cɔɔl kɛn rɔ̱ɔ̱riɛn  ji̱ Möri̱öri̱ ɣɛn thɔ̱ŋɛ mi̱i kɛ tha̱a̱ŋ kiɛn tin lo̱kɛ kɛ thuɔ̱k dɛ kɛn ji̱ Möriöri̱ cua kɛ juɔc raar.
text_en: They called themselves the Moriori there were a few skirmishes and in the end, the Moriori were wiped out

text: Tha̱a̱ŋ nath tëë caa rɔ̱ cuɔt ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ kɔr runi̱ ti̱ kur ti̱ ŋuan cuu kɛn nɛy luäk kɛ kui̱c bumä da kɛnɛ lua̱ŋda kɛ pe̱k ɣëë te̱e̱ nɛy kɛ rik kɛnɛ tin ka̱n luäŋ kɛ la̱tni̱.
text_en: Individuals who had been involved for several decades helped us appreciate our strengths and passions while candidly assessing difficulties and even failures.

text: Kä min liŋ kɔn naath kɛl kɛɛli̱ min lät kɛn kɔn nyin kiɛn, nyin ji̱ dhɔaariɛn, kɛnɛ nyin lätni̱  kiɛn.bi̱ kɔn ŋäc mi̱ gɔaa je̱k kɛ tëë wal tëë ci̱ kɛn kɛ la̱t kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ ciɛŋ ni̱i̱ kɛ  ram in ci̱ mi̱ gɔa la̱t kɛ ta̱a̱ la̱t  diɛn kiɛ rami̱ ci miji̱äk lät kɛ ta̱a̱ la̱t  in yiaan kɛ ni̱ rɔ̱.
text_en: While listening to individuals share their individual, family, and organizational stories, we gained valuable insight into the past and some of the personalities who influenced for good or ill the culture of the organization.

text: Kɛ kɔr kä min wä naath kɛ lie̱ŋ /ci̱  tin la̱t kɛ ɛ naath kɛ ta̱a̱ ciɛŋä diɛn /caa kɛ rany thi̱n jɛn luäkɛ naath kä tɔt kɛ guäth in pɛn kɛ thi̱n rɛy la̱t diɛn.
text_en: While understanding one’s history does not assume understanding of culture, it does at least help people gain a sense of where they fall within the history of the organization.

text: Min wä naath kɛ mi̱ rial kɛ tin ci̱ gɔw i̱kä kä baa tin ci̱ naath gɔw thi̱n ŋa̱c,bi̱ ramɔ kiɛ nɛy diaal tin lätkɛ nɔmɔ ŋɔak je̱k ti̱ te̱ ni̱ rɛcɔ  ce̱t kɛ tin yiaan kɛ rɔ̱,kɛ tin go̱o̱r kɛn lät ni̱ diɛn kɛnɛ tin kɔ̱ŋ tin jak kɛn kä bi̱ kɛn nɔmɔ la̱t.
text_en: While assessing the successes and becoming aware of failures, individuals and the whole of the participating persons discover more deeply the values, mission, and driving forces of the organization.

text: Kɛ jɛn cäät  ɛmɛ,kɛ car jɔk kä ciɛŋ tin te̱kɛ ram in lät ta̱a̱jiɛɛr kɛnɛ tin gɔw tin cɛ je̱k luäkɛ naath kɛ ɣöö bi̱kɛ  lɔar kɛ gër riɛn kɛnɛ wä diɛn kɛ luäk kuthni̱.
text_en: In this instance, recalling previous instances of entrepreneurial behavior and resulting successes helped people to be open to new changes and new direction for the local church.

text: Kɛn ti gɔw tɔ̱tɔ̱ni̱ ci̱ kɛn dual in te̱e̱ naath jakä kuiy kä cɛ naath jakä te̱kɛ ŋa̱th kɛ ta̱a̱ ciɛɛŋa̱ min bi̱ rɔ gɛr  min bi̱ be̱n nhiam.
text_en: Such success stories lessened the fears of change, while creating positive inclinations toward change in the future.

text: Ca̱r mi rɔ̱ŋ labɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱r la moocɛ kɛ pek ɛ thia̱k kä labɛ cäätni ti ŋuan kiɛ pɛl ti gööl la matdɛ kɛ ɣöö bɛɛ luɔt duɔ̱rä kulɛ jek.
text_en: Convergent thinking patterns are problem solving techniques that unite different ideas or fields to find a solution.

text: Ɛn ɣöö bi ca̱ru la̱th kä duɔ̱ɔ̱r ɛ pɛ̈th, kɛ ca̱r mi rɔ̱ŋ, kɛ pääri ŋɔani mi rɔ̱ŋ, kä bi min jɔc nɛn, kä bi ta̱a̱ in dɔ̱ŋ in deri lätni jɛ tim, kä bi lääri ti gööl ruɔ̱ɔ̱l.
text_en: The focus of this mindset is speed, logic and accuracy, also identification of facts, reapplying existing techniques, gathering information.

text: Min bumni jɛn ɛ lɔ̱ŋ kä ɣöö bi ca̱ru la̱th kä duɔ̱ɔ̱r: ɛ ɣöö bi jäkdɛ kɛl mal jek. La go̱o̱rɛ jɛ bi car ni rɛw, min gɔaadɛ kɛnɛ min jiääkdɛ.
text_en: The most important factor of this mindset is: there is only one correct answer. You only think of two answers, namely right or wrong.

text: Dup cärä te kɛn kɛ mat kɛ ta̱a̱ luäŋädu kɛ ɣöö deri pek duɔ̱ɔ̱rä kiɛ luɔt rikä mal jek kɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p mi lot rɔ.
text_en: This type of thinking is associated with certain science or standard procedures.

text: Nɛy tin cär i̱ nɛnɛ tekɛ kɛ ca̱r mi rɔ̱ŋ, dee kɛn ca̱a̱p duɔ̱ɔ̱rä mal tit, dëë cio̱o̱kdɛ mal jek kɛnɛ ɣöö dee kɛn ɣɔ̱ɔ̱ni tanytithni luäŋ.
text_en: People with this type of thinking have logical thinking, are able to memorize patterns, solve problems and work on scientific tests.

text: Naath kɛ kɛn tin ŋa̱c kɛ ŋɔak ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛ länykɛ tin kɔ̱kiɛn kɛ ŋäc cärä raam in dɔ̱diɛn.
text_en: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others.

text: Mi̱ lotni̱ ɣöö de̱e̱ kɔn ɛ ŋa̱c i̱ ɛŋu tuɔk ɔ kä le̱y tin kɔ̱ŋ, min göör kɛn ɛ kiɛ min nhɔk kɛn ɛ.
text_en: That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire.

text: Ɣɛn rɛy luäŋä nɛmɛ, ŋäc kɛ min göör ram in dɔ̱ŋɛ i̱ bɛ la̱t ɛ mi̱ gɔaa. Jakɛ kɔn kä bi̱ kɔn tin gör kɛ la̱th lät.
text_en: Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions.

text: Ce̱t kɛ mi̱ ci̱ raan nɛn tiathɛ wärnyin thuɔ̱rbiɛɛl, biɛ naŋ ce̱t kɛ ɣöö i̱ go̱o̱rɛ ni̱ na̱ŋ thuɔ̱rbiɛɛl rami̱ dɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger’s car.

text: Jɛn de̱e̱rɛ go̱ri̱ baa  luk kɛ dup ti̱ gööl mi̱ cɛɛ kiyni̱ thuɔ̱rbiɛɛlɛ bath kä ɛ thurbilɛ ɣɛn min go̱rɛ ɣöö bɛ tiath.
text_en: He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.

text: MRI jɛn lätɛ kɛ ta̱a̱ Pi̱i̱dhikä mi̱ cɔali̱ nukliɛr maknɛt rɛthonanthɛ (NMR),mi̱ cua je̱k kɛ ruɔ̱n 1930 ɛ rami̱ cɔali̱ Pɛlik Bilok (lätɛ kä jamɛ duŋ Ithtanpuɔd) kɛnɛ Ɣe̱d-wäd Purthël (min te̱ kä jamɛ Harbad).
text_en: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University).

text: Ɣɛn rɛy jɔaw ɛ di̱i̱t ɛmɛ, makanti̱th kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ rɛdiöwä kɛn jak kɛn atɔm kä bɛ ŋuni̱ jɔw rɛdiöwä mi̱ tɔt.
text_en: In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals.

text: Kɛ ruɔ̱n 1970, Raymɔn Damadian mi̱ däktöör kä tanyti̱i̱th cuɛ be̱n nhial kɛ ta̱a̱ in dëë jɔw mɛkanti̱i̱thä jakä mi̱ dëë moc naath I̱ lacɛ kɛ jɛ due̱l wa̱l
text_en: In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis.

text: Kɛ kɔr run da̱ŋ ŋuaan cua gua̱n jua̱th in nhiam rialikä min la ram in nhiam kä jɛn guäth MRI ɛmɔ
text_en: Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI.

text: Kɛ ruɔ̱n 1977,däktör ni̱ Damadian cuë la̱t pua̱ny  MRI in nhiam la̱t min cuë cɔli̱  "mi̱ bumbum".
text_en: In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first “whole-body” MRI scanner, which he called the ”Indomitable”.

text: Jɛn ta̱a̱ ruac ɛmɛ jakɛ thaak kä bɛ ŋɔak riali̱kä kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ in ŋuɛckɛ ni̱ kɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others.

text: Luäkɛ gaat duël gɔ̱rä ɣɛn ɣöö bi̱kɛ lät kɛ lät diɛn kä bi̱kɛn la̱t lääri̱ rialikä bä.
text_en: It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information.

text: Min dɔ̱ŋ, tëëkɛ kɛ ti̱ tɔatni̱ ti̱ dëë thaakni̱  lät mi̱ gɔaa pën. (Bremer,1998).
text_en: In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998)

text: Ɣɛn läth lät ɣintɛrnɛtka̱ jɛnɛ wɛb ɣɔaa kɛɛliw luäkɛ gaat duël gɔ̱rä kɛ ɣöö bi̱ kɛn lää ɛje̱k gua̱thni̱ diaal.
text_en: The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times.

text: Gaat duël gɔ̱rä bä de̱e̱ kɛn thi̱e̱cni̱ thöp  nɛy tin nyuɔ̱thkɛ kɛ ŋɔaani̱ guäthni̱ diaal kä de̱e̱ kɛn je̱kni̱ kiɛn je̱k kɛ pɛ̈th ɛci̱ maa ɣöö de̱e̱kɛn lip ni̱ kilɛth in guic naath rɔ̱ɔ̱kiɛn thi̱n.
text_en: Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.

text: Ɛn ta̱a̱ ŋi̱i̱cä mɛ thia̱kɛ jɛn moocɛ naath kɛ min go̱o̱r raan ɛ. Thiɛlɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p mi̱ gɔa mi̱ la duŋ ŋi̱i̱cä.
text_en: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn.

text: Ɛ puc thiɛlɛ mi̱ gɔa mi̱ dëë ŋa̱c. Ŋi̱i̱c jɛn lät kɛ jɛ kɛ ŋä kam raam in ŋiäckɛ kɛnɛ ŋäcni̱ min caa ŋun.
text_en: In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented.

text: Ŋa̱c dan kɛ pe̱k ɛmɛ kɛ ɣöö i̱ lät niɛ kä rɔa kɛnɛ lär lär kä tin la nyin ŋi̱i̱cä tin laa nyuɔ̱thkɛ rɛy TV ni̱ jɛn latdɛ jɛ jɛn nɛmɛ.
text_en: Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point.

text: Nɛɛkɔn ti̱ ŋuan ci̱ kɔn rɔ̱ je̱k guic kɔn TV mi̱ lärkɔn kɛ ta̱a̱ in de̱e̱ kɔn te̱e̱ ŋäc mi̱ gɔaa kä duɔ̱r kä/ ci̱ kɔn kɛ wa̱a̱ läth lät kiɛ /ci̱ kɔn rɔ̱ läth thi̱n ɣɛn ŋäc ɛmɔ.
text_en: So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge.

text: /Cȋ kɔn thurbil de̱e̱ la̱t,kiɛ de̱e̱ kɔn pi̱w ti̱ pɛn la̱t jɔk ciëŋ dan, wä kä Përu kɛ kui̱c kä ɣöö de̱e̱ kɔn duɔth kä tëë wal cëtkɛ duël tëë caa täth kiɛ de̱e̱ kɔn duël ji̱ thie̱kä dan duëlkiɛn nyɔk kɛ lätni̱.
text_en: We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.

text: De̱e̱ tɛthlɔac wä kä andɛrthi̱i payba optik cabɔl min la duŋ Yurɔp ɛla bröödban tha̱tɛlait, Gi̱ri̱i̱nlɛn jɛn caa moc kɛɛ ɣintɛrnɛt agɔa kä tëë nɛy ti̱ cuɔp kɛ 93% ti̱ je̱k ɣintɛrnɛt.
text_en: Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access.

text: Ho̱tɛlu kiɛ gua̱th in ci̱ jac (mi̱ cie̱ŋi̱ due̱l ja̱a̱li̱ kiɛ due̱l mi̱ private) jɛn de̱rɛ te̱ kɛɛ WIFIkiɛɛ ɣintɛrnɛt mi̱ caa pith  kɛɛl kɛɛ PC,kɛn duël diaal  te̱kɛn kɛ ŋua̱a̱th ɣintɛrnɛtkä kiɛ gua̱a̱th mi̱ te̱e̱ kɛɛ WIFI duŋ nɛɛni̱ diaal.
text_en: Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi.

text: Cetkɛ min ca lat nhial, cäŋ ni min ciöt i̱ "Eskimo" ŋotdɛ kɛ mi nhɔak kɛ jɛ kä United States, ŋotdɛ kɛ mi guɛc kɛ jɛ ɛ la riet mi jiääk ɛ nɛy ti ŋuan ti /ci la ji̱ U.S. ji̱ Arctic, cet kɛ Canada.
text_en: As mentioned above, though the word "Eskimo" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada.

text: Cäŋ ci ciöt ɛmɔ liŋ kä ji̱kɛ tin la ji̱ Greenland, lotdɛ rɔ kɛ ɣöö dëë ruacdɛ päl ɛ nɛy tin la jur.
text_en: While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners.

text: Ji̱ dhɔaar in cɔali Greenland cɔalkɛ rɔ̱ i̱ Inuit kä Canada kɛnɛ Kalaalleq (mi ŋuankɛ Kalaallit), mi cɔali raan Greenland, kä Greenland.
text_en: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

text: Kraim, kɛnɛ ciaŋ jiäk kä nɛy tin /ci maa gaat wec kɛn dial, /caa ŋäc kä rɛy Gri̱i̱nland. Amäni̱ rɛy rɛ̈kni̱, thiɛlɛ kɛ "gua̱th ti̱ tuɔ̱r tuɔ̱ɔ̱r."
text_en: Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no "rough areas."

text: Jiɔm in kɔ̱c dɔ̱ŋ ɛ jɛn da̱a̱ riɛk in bɛc kä kɛn tin kän rɔ riali̱kä bi̱kɛ bɛ̈cdɛ jek.
text_en: Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face.

text: Mi̱ ci̱i̱ Gri̱i̱nland gui̱l kɛɛ thi̱thɔn kɔa̱c ( ŋäcni̱ jɛ ɛn ɣöö bi̱ kɔa̱cdɛ rɔ rëp, kɛ wädu kɛ wä nhiamdɛ), ro̱ŋ ɣöö deri̱ rɔ röm bieyi̱ kɔa̱c ti̱ ŋuan.
text_en: If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing.

text: Jɛn ni̱n tin bär ni̱ kɛn dëë kɛn riɛk nööŋ kɛ ta̱a̱ kä ɣöö dak niën kɛnɛ dërɛ puɔ̱ny ran moc riɛk.
text_en: The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues.

text: Kɛɛ tɔ̱t, tidrɔ bä kɛɛ jɛn nyi̱i̱th Nɔrdik. Cäŋni̱ min /ci̱ kɛn juey jääl kä naath , dëë kɛn ciaaŋdu ya̱r.
text_en: During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating.

text: Kɛ gua̱a̱th ee ci̱ ikɔnɔmik duŋ Thɛn Pra̱nthi̱ithkö ro̱ŋ kɛ bɛ ja̱a̱l bɛr wi̱i̱c muɔ̱ɔ̱n, jɛn caa ikɔnɔmikdiɛn jak kä di̱t rɛydɛ.
text_en: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified.

text: Kɛn thɛktɛrni̱ tin di̱tni̱kɛn tin muɔckɛ naath lät kɛ lät ji pröpɛcinal, ta̱a̱jiɛɛr, kɛnɛ tied ja̱a̱li̱
text_en: The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism.

text: Kɛ ta̱a̱ in ŋa̱c kɛ jɛ ni̱ ciaŋ kɛ kui̱c tuaari̱, pilimni̱, ruaacni̱ tin caa gɔ̱r kɛnɛ ka̱lcier min ŋa̱c kɛ ci̱kɛn rɛk kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ in jɔc kɛ jɛ jakä ɣöö baa ŋa̱c wi̱i̱cmuɔ̱n kɛliw.
text_en: Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world.

text: Thɛn Pra̱nthi̱thkö cua jɛ la̱t kɛ ta̱a̱ mi̱ röŋ cetkɛ ɣo̱teeli̱ ti̱ ŋuan kɛ kui̱c ja̱a̱li̱,thukni̱ miëth, kɛnɛ gua̱th ma̱a̱tni̱ ti̱ bäl gɔɔydiɛn.
text_en: San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities.

text: Thɛn Pra̱nthi̱thkö ɛ jɛn gua̱a̱th kɛl mi̱ gɔa ɛlɔ̱ŋ bä rɛy wec kä lot rɔ kɛɛ kudhi̱i̱n Ji Ecia: Ji Köria,Ji thailand, Ji India, kɛnɛ Ji Japan.
text_en: San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.

text: Wä ran Ja̱l kä Walt Di̱thnɛy Wääl cerɛ ni kɛ wä ja̱l gua̱th palä Kuɔth kä dhör Ji mɛrkɛm ti̱ ŋuan.
text_en: Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families.

text: Jɛn "ti̱pi̱kɔ̱l" ŋui̱l ɛmɔ kɔn naath wä ni̱ kɛ ruëynhial kä Tiaar Ria̱ynhiali̱ wi̱i̱ni̱ ti̱ gööl rɛy Örlando, ja̱l kɛɛ ba̱th mi̱ te rɛydɛ kɛ Di̱thnɛy Ɣo̱teel, la yiɛn juɔk ɛ naŋ ɛ kän yiɛn kuak Di̱thnɛy päl, kä bia cuu luny jɔk.
text_en: The "typical" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home.

text: Tekɛ ti̱ ŋuani̱kɛn ti̱ gööl ti̱ caa pëkdiɛn luäŋ, duundɛ ɣöö cɛ duɔth ɛ la min lot nɛy ti̱ ŋuan ɛ mi̱ lat kɛn ɣöö " wä nath kä Di̱thnɛy Wääl".
text_en: There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of "going to Disney World".

text: tikɛtni̱ ti̱ ŋuanikɛn laa kɛ laa kɔakɛ rɛy-jɔam kä wɛbɛaitni̱ tin ko̱k kɛ ramin ŋuan yio̱kɛ cetkɛ eBɛy kiɛ Krɛgli̱th laa lät kɛ thi̱n kɛ tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni̱ kɛɛ park-uppɛr ti̱ketni̱ kɛ ni̱n ti̱ ŋuan.
text_en: Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets.

text: Ɛ cäŋ ni̱ mɔ la̱t kɛ jɛ inɔ ni̱ ciaŋ, /ci Di̱thnɛy ɛ nhɔk: kɛn ti̱kɛtni̱ /cikɛ ti̱ dee kɔak ɛ nɛy ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable.

text: Wä ja̱l kɛnɛ nien raar thaar kaŋ kaŋä kä Grand Canyon go̱rɛ wargak ja̱l min la wä kɛ naath rɛy cieŋ.
text_en: Any camping below the rim in Grand Canyon requires a backcountry permit.

text: Wargakni tin ka̱mkɛ naath kɛ wä nath kä lo̱o̱l ɛmɔ dak kɛn kɛ ɣöö dëë  kulɛ gaŋ, kä bɛ lɔar ni kɛ cäŋ in nhiam kä pay, päth ŋuaan ɛ ŋot ti wëë kä tuk paay in dɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month.

text: Kɛ kuic ɛmɔ, wargak in bi ja̱l kɛ naath kɛ wädiɛn rɛy ciëŋ kɛ cäŋ ɛ lot rɔ mɔ kɛ Pay Dhieec la tëë thi̱n kɛ cäŋkä 1 kä Pay Kɛl.
text_en: Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan.

text: Gua̱a̱th kɛ kui̱ dho̱ri tin ŋa̱ckɛ ɛ lɔ̱ŋ, ce̱tkɛ Tɔ̱ɔ̱r Bright Angel min thieek kɛ Phantom Ranch, ca kɛ thieŋ ɛ nɛy tëë ci thiec kɛ cäŋ in nhiam mi lotni ɣöö ca kɛ lɛp ɛ la ti ca käp.
text_en: Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations.

text: Wargakni ja̱l tin ca rialikä kɛ kui̱ ja̱a̱li tin bëë ben gue̱l ca kɛ jakä ti tɔt, la ka̱mkɛ ni kɛ nɛy tin ci ben kɛ nhiam.
text_en: There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

text: Wä kä Thɔth Apri̱ka kɛ thurbil ɛ duɔ̱p mi̱ gɔa ni̱ jɛn mi̱ dëri̱ lɛ guic ni gɔɔy wëc kɛnɛ ɣöö dëri̱ lɛ ja̱l kɛ dup tin laa jäl kɛ naath ɛ /ci maa dup ja̱a̱li̱ .
text_en: Entering Southern Africa by car is an amazing way to see all the region's beauty as well as to get to places off the normal tourist routes.

text: Deri̱ mi̱ cetkɛ nɔ la̱t kɛ jɛn thurbil in nɔrmɔl mi̱ ci̱ rɔ riali̱kä a gɔa duundɛ 4x4 ɛ jɛn min lotrɔ kɛnɛ ɣöö gua̱th ti̱ ŋuan laa cup naath thin kɛ thuɔ̱rbiɛli̱ 4x4 ti̱ te ciökiɛn nhial.
text_en: This can be done in a normal car with careful planning but a 4x4 is highly advised and many locations are only accessible with a high wheel base 4x4.

text: Ŋäc ni̱ jɛ min riali̱rɔkä ɛn ɣöö cäŋni min Jɔk Apri̱ka pälɛrɔpiny /ci̱kɛ kɛn wi̱i̱cdial tin thiëk.
text_en: Keep in mind while planning that although Southern Africa is stable not all neighboring countries are.

text: Tin laa görkɛ kä bi̱dha kɛnɛ yio̱w te kɛn kɛ dääk kä wëc ɔ kɛnɛ wëc ɔ kä lëëny kɛn rɔ kɛ ŋua̱a̱th in bi̱i̱ thi̱n.
text_en: Visa requirements and costs vary from nation to nation and are affected by the country you come from.

text: Te wëc ɔ kɛɛ ŋuɔ̱tkɛ bä ti̱ ci̱ cäät kɛ wi̱i̱c tin kɔ̱ŋ ti̱ go̱o̱rjɛ i̱ bi̱ te kɛ kuak imärjɛnthi̱ rɛy thuɔ̱rbiɛl.
text_en: Each country also has unique laws requiring what emergency items need to be in the car.

text: Bi̱ktöria po̱l ɛ rɛk kä tha̱a̱ŋ kui̱c caam kä Dhi̱mbabwi, min te kam këëyä kä Li̱biŋtɔn, Dha̱mbia, kɛnɛ thieek Bɔt-ithwana.
text_en: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana.

text: Jɛn rɛk tee niɛ kä jɛn gëkädɛ jɛn po̱l, kä kɛ kɛn tin di̱t tim bɛ̈r kɛ naath, duundɛ jɛn gua̱th ja̱a̱li̱ mɛ ŋa̱ckɛni̱ jɛ mɛ no̱ŋɛ ti̱ ŋuan nɛy tin go̱o̱r ni̱ adbencɛr kɛnɛ nɛy tin bä kɛ guëc kɛ gua̱a̱th mi̱ bäär.
text_en: The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay.

text: Kɛ kɛn rɛy ni̱ni̱ nhieli̱ (Paywälkɛl ɛ wä kä Paydiɔ̱k), bi̱ pi̱w bɛn nhial kä bi̱ po̱l cuu laa mi̱ bɛɛr gɔɔydɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic.

text: Ga̱ckɛ ni̱ jɛ ɛn ɣöö bi̱ lua̱a̱k mi̱ wi̱i̱ kubri̱ ŋok kiɛ mi̱ wi̱i̱ ja̱l gekädɛ min thiëk kɛɛ jɛn Po̱l.
text_en: You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls.

text: Kɛ ɣöö nɔ bä, ɛn jɛn gua̱a̱thdɛ kä ɣöö ci̱ pi̱w ben nhial ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛ la ɣöö bi̱ guecdu kɛ po̱l puɔnydɛ laa mi̱ /ci̱ jɔc-kɛ kui̱c pi̱i̱ni̱ dial!
text_en: On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!

text: Kɔa̱k kunya̱ Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 dɔ̱ŋ dërɛ laa jɛn gua̱a̱th kunyä min ŋa̱ckɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä jɛn Ma̱t ɛmɔ, Jɛn gua̱a̱th ee jɛk Ho̱ward kartɛr jɛ min caa riali̱kä kɛ kuɔ̱ny kua̱r rɔyal mi̱ tɔt.
text_en: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 may be the most famous of the tombs in the Valley, the scene of Howard Carter's 1922 discovery of the almost intact royal burial of the young king.

text: Mi̱ päär i̱ jɛ kɛɛ rɔyal tömni̱ ti̱ guan, kɛ ɣöö nɔ, jɛn töm Tutankhamun /ciɛ mi̱ lot rɔ kɛ gui̱l, kɛ ɣöö kuiyɛ kä ka̱nɛ biɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Compared to most of the other royal tombs, however, the tomb of Tutankhamun is barely worth visiting, being much smaller and with limited decoration.

text: ɛni rami̱ nhɔk ɣöö dërɛ ta̱a̱ ee caa yär ni̱i̱ mummy gua̱a̱th ɣɔa̱n kɛ ɣöö baa jɛ woc kä kɔpin thi̱n bɛ woc ni̱ locdu kɛ ɣöö jɔɔc ni̱ wi̱cdɛ kɛnɛ wuɔ̱kɛ kärɔ.
text_en: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.

text: Kɛn nyin ruäŋä tin gɔw tee të rɛy tömä /ci kɛn lɛ ŋot thi̱n, duunde ɣöö caa kɛ naŋ kä Mudhiam duŋ Ijip ka Kairö.
text_en: The fabulous riches of the tomb are no longer in it, but have been removed to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo.

text: Ja̱a̱l tin kuiy thaakdiɛn ŋuäni̱ ɣöö dëë kɛn ɛ wä naŋ gua̱a̱th mi̱ dɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Visitors with limited time would be best to spend their time elsewhere.
