text: Phnɔm Krɔm, kä 12km kam caam kɛnɛ jɔk Thiɛm Riip. Gua̱th palä nɛmɛ mɛ caa täth wi̱i̱c pa̱a̱m ɛ la̱t kɛ jɛ kɛ thuɔ̱k 9th thënciɛri̱ , kɛ gua̱a̱th ee ruëc
text_en: Phnom Krom, 12 km southwest of Siem Reap. This hilltop temple was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman.

text: Ta̱a̱ jɔam in jia̱k ta̱a̱dɛ min te gua̱a̱th palä kɛnɛ guëcdɛ kä jɛn Pul To̱nlɛ Thap jak ɛ köt pa̱a̱m kä mi̱ te kɛɛ luɔt.
text_en: The gloomy atmosphere of the temple and the view over the Tonle Sap lake make the climb to the hill worthwhile.

text: Mi̱ tekɛ gua̱a̱th mi̱ gui̱li̱ derɛ rɔ lot ɛlɔ̱ŋ mi̱ ci̱ mat kɛ ja̱l bo̱tdä rɛy puɔ̱l
text_en: A visit to the site can be conveniently combined with a boat trip to the lake.

text: Jɛn Aŋkör Pa̱a̱th laa gör kɛ jɛ kɛ wä gua̱a̱th palä kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ cuu pa̱a̱thpuɔtdu päl rieec mi̱ kä To̱nlɛ Thap.
text_en: The Angkor Pass is needed to enter the temple so do not forget to bring your passport along when heading to Tonle Sap.

text: Jɛruthɛlɛm ɛ jɛn kapi̱tɔl kä ɛ jɛn rɛk in di̱t ni̱ jɛn kä Ithrɛɛl, cäŋni̱ min /caa ŋic i̱ ɛ jɛn kapi̱tɔl Ithrɛɛl ɛ wi̱i̱c tin kɔ̱ŋ amäni̱ Mɛrkɛm.
text_en: Jerusalem is the capital and largest city of Israel, though most other countries and the United Nations do not recognize it as Israel's capital.

text: Ɛ jɛn wec ee wal kä kɛn wi̱i̱c Päämni̱ Ji̱ Judia min te kɛ kɛ̈k mi̱ gɔa mi̱ caa ŋa̱c kɛ kɔr runi̱
text_en: The ancient city in the Judean Hills has a fascinating history spanning thousands of years.

text: Jɛn rɛk in rɛl rɔ kä kɛn gua̱th da̱ŋdiɔk tin te kɛ rɛli̱jɔ̱n min ŋäth ni̱ ɣöö koth ɛ kɛl- Judaidhiöm, Krithtiani̱ty, kɛnɛ Ithla̱m, kɛnɛ ɛ jɛn gua̱a̱th in ŋa̱ckɛ min laa ithpi̱ri̱cual, rɛli̱jiath, kɛnɛ kalcierɔl thentɛr.
text_en: The city is holy to the three monotheistic religions - Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and serves as a spiritual, religious, and cultural center.

text: Kɛ kui̱c kä ɣöö di̱dni̱ ta̱a̱ rɛlijɔnä rɛy rɛ̈ɛ̈k, kɛnɛ jɛn ta̱a̱ kä ɣöö  te gua̱th tee ŋa̱c kɛ ni̱ wal thi̱n Rɛɛk ee Wal, Jɛruthɛlɛm ɛ jɛn gua̱a̱th ɛn nhɔk ja̱a̱l gui̱lɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä I̱thrɛɛl.
text_en: Due to the religious significance of the city, and in particular the many sites of the Old City area, Jerusalem is one of the main tourist destinations in Israel.

text: Jɛruthɛlɛm te kɛ gua̱th ɣi̱töri̱ni̱, tin nyooth ciɛŋ ee wal kɛnɛ ka̱lciɛriɛn, kɛɛl kɛnɛ gua̱th ko̱kä ti̱ biɛlbiɛɛl ti̱ ci̱ thua̱a̱ŋ, gua̱th ma̱th ca̱yni̱, kɛnɛ gua̱th miëth kuan.
text_en: Jerusalem has many historic, archeological and cultural sites, along with vibrant and crowded shopping centers, cafés, and restaurants.

text: Ekuɛdɔr go̱o̱rɛ jɛ ɛn ɣöö dee Ji wec Kuba moc kɛɛ waregak inbaitecinä ɛ ŋot kän kɛ wä rɛy Ekuɛdɔr kɛɛ tiaar ria̱ynhiali̱ tin bä wi̱i̱ni̱ tin gööl kiɛ gua̱th tin coth kɛ naath kam këyä wi̱i̱ni̱.
text_en: Ecuador requires that Cuban citizens receive an invitation letter prior to entering Ecuador through international airports or frontier admission points.

text: Jɛn warɛgak ɛmɔ bɛ kɔn ro̱ŋ kɛ guɔ̱t Mi̱ni̱thtɛr duŋ Pɔrɛn Appɛ̈ɛ̈r kä Ekuɛdɔr, kä bɛ guɔ̱t tin görkɛ thiäŋ.
text_en: This letter must be legalized by the Ecuadorian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and comply with certain requirements.

text: Ŋuɔ̱t tin görkɛ caa kɛ riali̱kä kɛ ɣöö bi ta̱a̱ in jäl kɛ naath wi̱i̱ni̱ jakä mi̱ thia̱k.
text_en: These requirements are designed to provide an organized migratory flow between both countries.

text: Gaat wec Kuba tin tekɛ gri̱i̱n kard duŋ US bikɛ wä kä Kɔnthulet Ji Ekuɛdɔr kɛ ɣöö baa kɛ kulɛ woc kä ta̱a̱ guɔ̱tni̱ tin görkɛ.
text_en: Cuban citizens who are US green card holders should visit an Ecuadorian Consulate to obtain an exemption to this requirement.

text: Pa̱thpuɔtdu bɛ yi̱k wä ŋot kɛ la̱t kɛ kɔr päthni̱ 6 ɛ wä thiam ɛ took ɛ ni̱ kä cäŋ i̱n bi̱ ja̱l kɛ ji̱. Baa tickɛt ja̱l wädu kɛnɛ lunydu jɔk/min wä kɛ ji̱ baa gör kɛ ɣöö baa pëk ja̱lu kulɛ ŋa̱c.
text_en: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay.

text: Ja̱l laa kuiy yio̱wkɛ mi̱ kɛ yiɛn buɔ̱n mi̱ di̱i̱t, kɛ kui̱c ɛ mɔ mi̱ ti̱i̱ kärca kiɛ yiɛnɛ määthdu kɛl, ɣɔ̱nɛ ɛn ɣöö bi̱ jiek kɛ nɛy ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ kä bia rɔ mat ɛ la buɔ̱n mi̱ cop ŋuaan ɛ wä kä bäkɛl kɛ ɣöö bi yio̱w tin yuɔrkɛ piny kuɛ̈ɛ̈ kä ram kɛl.
text_en: Tours are cheaper for larger groups, so if you're by yourself or with just one friend, try to meet other people and form a group of four to six for a better per-person rate.

text: Kä mi̱ /ciɛ jɛn inɔ, /cɛ ji dee dir ɛlɔ̱ŋ, kɛ ɣöö ja̱a̱l laa kɛ laa lɔamkɛ gua̱thni̱ ti ŋuan kɛ ɣöö bi̱kɛ thurbil kulɛ thiäŋ.
text_en: However, this shouldn't really be off your concern, because often tourists are shuffled around to fill the cars.

text: Cɛ jɔɔc ɛ la duɔ̱ɔ̱p mi̱ pɛ̈lkɛ ni̱ naath kɛ jɛ kɛ ɣöö kɛn ɛ kulɛ guic i̱ bi̱kɛ yuɔrni̱ yio̱w ti̱ ŋuan piny.
text_en: It seems actually to be more a way of tricking people into believing they have to pay more.

text: Lënyɛ ti̱ diaal kɛ bär nhiam Macu Pi̱ccu nɛmɛ ɛ Päm mi̱ cɛ ri̱c, kä ɛ jɛn min laa la̱thkɛ ɛ la jɔk gua̱thni̱ ti̱ guan.
text_en: Towering above the north end of Machu Picchu is this steep mountain, often the backdrop to many photos of the ruins.

text: Jɔɔc ta̱a̱ dɛ ɛ la mi̱ bum mi̱ ti̱i̱ pinydɛ, kɛnɛ ɣöö cɛ jɔkdɛ ri̱c kä bum kötdɛ, duundɛ rami̱ puɔl puɔ̱nydɛ a gɔa dërɛ jɛ luäŋ kɛ kɔr minitni̱ ti̱ 45.
text_en: It looks a bit daunting from below, and it is a steep and difficult ascent, but most reasonably fit persons should be able to make it in about 45 minutes.

text: Caa dööl car piny kɛ pëk ka̱a̱thni̱ dupni̱ ti̱ ŋuan, kä kui̱c in cɛ cuŋ ɛ pi̱c caa moc kɛ i̱thti̱i̱l kɛbɔlni̱ ti̱ kääp naath rɔ̱ kɛ kɛ̱.
text_en: Stone steps are laid along most of the path, and in the steeper sections steel cables provide a supporting handrail.

text: Lar kɛ jɛ i̱ nɛ, ɛ /ci̱ maa ɣöö dërɛ yieedu käp, ɛ bi̱ rɔ gaŋ gua̱thni̱ tin cuŋ ɛpi̱c, cetkɛ gua̱a̱th in cɛ lua̱a̱ny, dërɛ riɛk mal nööŋ kɛ pɛ̈th.
text_en: That said, expect to be out of breath, and take care in the steeper portions, especially when wet, as it can become dangerous quickly.

text: Tekɛ kaŋ-kaŋni̱ ti̱ tɔani̱ ti̱ thiëk kɛ wi̱cdɛ ti̱ la naath ɛ coth kɛ kɛ, ciɛk jɔkdiɛn ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä rill naath kɛ ɣöö ciwkɛ.
text_en: There's a tiny cave near the top that must be passed through, it is quite low and a rather tight squeeze.

text: Nen gua̱thni̱ tɔtɔ kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ leeni̱ kä jɛn Galapagɔth lot d rɔ kɛɛ bot, kɛ ta̱a̱ ee ci̱ Cha̱rl Darwin ɛ la̱t kɛ 1835.
text_en: Seeing the sites and wildlife of the Galapagos is best done by boat, just as Charles Darwin did it in 1835.

text: Baabuuri̱ ti̱ bääl 60 tin kap kɛ naath laa wä kɛ rɛy yieer Galapagɔth- took ɛ pëk di̱tdädiɛn kä nɛy ti̱i̱ 8-100.
text_en: Over 60 cruise ships ply the Galapagos waters - ranging in size from 8 to 100 passengers.

text: Nɛy ti̱ ŋuani̱kɛn laa kääp kɛn gua̱thkiɛn ɛ ŋot (kɛ ɣöö la bötni̱ laa thieŋ kɛ gua̱th runä in ŋuan naath kɛ jɛ)
text_en: Most people book their place well in advance (as the boats are usually full during the high season).

text: Go̱rɛ a gɔaa ɛn ɣöö ɛɛjɛn in buk i̱ gua̱a̱th kɛ tetdɛ ɛ ithpeciali̱th Galapagɔth kä tekɛ ŋäc mi̱ ro̱ŋ kɛɛ nɔw baabuuri̱ dial.
text_en: Be sure the agent through whom you book is a Galapagos specialist with a good knowledge of a wide variety of ships.

text: Nɛmɛ bɛ ji̱ jak kä ɣöö bi̱ min go̱o̱r lɔcdu jɛ kɛnɛ/kiɛ bi̱ tin go̱o̱r ta̱a̱ ja̱l ɛ ro̱m kɛ baabuur in bi̱ kɛ cuɔ̱ɔ̱p.
text_en: This will ensure that your particular interests and/or constraints are matched with the ship most suitable to them.

text: Ɛ ŋot kän Ji I̱thpɛɛny ni cop kɛ jɛn 16th thɛnciɛri̱, nhiam Chili̱ ruac kɛ jɛ ɛ Inka kä kɛ jɛn pëk ɛmɔ nɛy tee jiek kɛ wi̱c ni̱ Araukaniani̱ (Mapucɛ) ciɛŋ kɛn ni̱ där kɛnɛ jɔk Chili̱.
text_en: Before the Spanish arrived in the 16th century, northern Chile was under Inca rule while the indigenous Araucanians (Mapuche) inhabited central and southern Chile.

text: Kɛn Mapucɛ ɛ do̱r kɛl dör wëc tee ci̱ duɔth ɛ ruac rɔ̱, ka̱n kɛ luäŋ kɛ mat kä ruëëc ee ruac thuɔk Ji I̱thpɛɛny amäni̱ kɔr kä mee ci̱ Chi̱li̱ kumɛ jek.
text_en: The Mapuche were also one of the last independent American indigenous groups, that were not fully absorbed into Spanish-speaking rule until after Chile's independence.

text: Cäŋni̱ mee caa Chi̱li̱ ka̱m kumɛdɛ kɛ 1810 (däär köör Napo̱liönik mee ci̱ Ithpɛɛny jakä doth ɛ thiɛl kumɛ mi̱ lat kɛ kɔr runi̱ ti̱ ŋuani̱kɛn), juc I̱thpɛɛny känɛ thuɔ̱k cuu mäni̱ 1818
text_en: Although Chile declared independence in 1810 (amid the Napoleonic wars that left Spain without a functioning central government for a couple of years), decisive victory over the Spanish was not achieved until 1818.

text: Wec in cɔali Dominican Republic (Spanish: República Dominicana) ɛ wec nɛɛni tin cɔali ji̱ Caribbean min thieeŋ tha̱a̱ŋ kuec cuëëc dhɔaar in ca röm ɛ yiër min la duŋ Hispaniola, min nyuak kɛnɛ kɛɛl kɛnɛ Haiti
text_en: The Dominican Republic (Spanish: República Dominicana) is a Caribbean country that occupies the eastern half of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti

text: Ɛ /ci mɔ aa liɛt thuɔk baar in bo̱r kärɔa kɛnɛ lɔath päämni, wec puɔ̱nydɛ ɛ jɛn dhɔr in te rɛɛk ji̱ Yurɔp tëë wal kä Amɛrika, min la puɔ̱ny kɛl kä Santo Domingo.
text_en: Besides white sand beaches and mountain landscapes, the country is home to the oldest European city in the Americas, now part of Santo Domingo.

text: Nɛy tëë kɔn cieŋ wi̱c dhulä nɔmɔ kɛ Tainöni kɛnɛ Karibni. Kɛn ji̱ Karibni ruackɛ kɛ thok nɛɛni ti cɔali ji̱ Arawaka tëë ci cop kɛ jɛn gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ ni kɛ ruɔ̱n 10,000 BCE.
text_en: The island was first inhabited by the Taínos and Caribes. The Caribes were an Arawakan-speaking people who had arrived around 10,000 BCE.

text: Kɛ kɔr runi̱ ti̱ tɔt mi guur ni ben ëë bëë kɛ ji̱ Yurɔp tëë ja̱l kɛ ɣɔw kɛ ɣöö ba ŋɔak ti ŋuan ŋa̱c ɛ kɛn, cua pek nɛɛni tin cieŋ kä Tainos jakä wä piny ɛ ji̱ Spain tëë ca kɛ käp
text_en: Within a few short years following the arrival of European explorers, the population of Tainos had significantly been reduced by the Spanish conquerors

text: Kɛ ruac in ca lat ɛ Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) kam 1492 kɛnɛ 1498 ji̱ Spain tëë ca wec käp cu kɛn nɛy ti̱ 100,000 näk ti la ji̱ Taínos.
text_en: Based on Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) between 1492 and 1498 the Spanish conquerors killed around 100,000 Taínos.

text: Jardi̱n de la Uniön. Jɛn gua̱a̱th ɛmɛ la̱tkɛ ɛ la atria̱a̱m ciɛɛŋä Ji luak Kuɔth kɛ 17 thɛnciɛri̱ , kä jɛn Tëmplö de Than Diɛgö ɛ jɛn duël in ci duɔth cuŋä.
text_en: Jardín de la Unión. This space was built as the atrium for a 17th-century convent, of which the Templo de San Diego is the sole surviving building.

text: Cɛ duɔth ɛ la duël in te däär,kä tee kɛ ti̱ ŋuan ti̱ laa lätrɔ rɛydɛ, kɛ cäŋdäär kɛnɛ wäär.
text_en: It now functions as the central plaza, and always has a lot of things going on, day and night.

text: Tee kɛ gua̱th thukni̱ miëth kua̱ny ti̱ ci̱ jɛ go̱l jɛn ga̱rdɛn, kɛnɛ ɣöö kɛ cäŋdäär kɛnɛ thiaŋ laa tee kɛɛ conthɛtni̱ ti̱ /caa yio̱w tho̱p thi̱n ɛ laa la̱tkɛ ni̱ ciaŋ kä jɛn thär gadhɛbö.
text_en: There are a number of restaurants surrounding the garden, and in the afternoons and evening there free concerts are often given from the central gazebo.

text: Kallɛjɔn del Bɛdho̱ (min la duɔ̱ɔ̱p kam dueli̱ min cim naath rɔ thi̱n). Balkɔni̱ni̱ da̱ŋrɛw ti̱ te kamdiɛn kɛɛ thënti̱mi̱ti̱ri̱ ti̱i̱ 69 kärɔ̱ ɛ cieŋ min ci̱ kɛ̈kdɛ joor min ruac kɛ kui'c nho̱kä.
text_en: Callejon del Beso (Alley of the Kiss). Two balconies separated by only 69 centimeters is home of an old love legend.

text: Dëë tha̱a̱ŋ gan ji̱ jɛn i̱thtöri̱ mi̱ ci̱ cäŋ te ni̱ ji̱n kɛɛ giërëëni̱ ti̱ tɔt.
text_en: For a few pennies some children will tell you the story.

text: Dhuɔ̱ɔ̱l Böwɛn ɛ gua̱th mi̱ ŋa̱ckɛ kɛ gui̱l ca̱ŋkɛl kiɛ laath kɛɛ thuɔ̱k jokä min tekɛ ger rua̱a̱y, ɣaikiŋ, thukni̱, thukni̱ kuan, kɛnɛ ti̱ guan.
text_en: Bowen Island is a popular day trip or weekend excursion offering kayaking, hiking, shops, restaurants, and more.

text: Kɔmuni̱ti̱ nɛmɛ min ka̱n ta̱a̱ guɛl min te rɛy Hɔwɛ Thɔɔn ni̱ kɛ jiɛɛndu kä Bankuubɛr, kä dee mal cop ɛ thia̱k kɛ rɛy yieer kɛɛ takthi̱ni̱ tin laa jiɛn kä Granbi̱llɛ Aithland rɛy rɛ̈ɛ̈k Bankuubɛr.
text_en: This authentic community is located in Howe Sound just off Vancouver, and is easily accessed via scheduled water taxis departing Granville Island in downtown Vancouver.

text: Kɛ kui̱c nɛɛni̱ tin jɛk gɔɔy lätni̱ raar, wä ja̱l kam Baar kɛnɛ wec.
text_en: For those who enjoy outdoor activities, a trek up the Sea to Sky corridor is essential.

text: Wi̱thti̱lɛr (min tekɛ thaakni̱ 1.5 kɛ thurbil kɛ wä du kä Bankubɛr) jɛn ŋuan yio̱wkɛ kuɛɛ laa ɣöö ci̱ kɛkdɛ joor kɛ ta̱a̱ ŋarä duŋ O̱lympikä mëë caa la̱t thin kɛ ruɔ̱n 2010.
text_en: Whistler (1.5 hour drive from Vancouver) is expensive but well-known because of the 2010 Winter Olympics.

text: Kɛ jiɔm, bi̱ ŋar kɛ tha̱a̱ŋ ŋa̱a̱ri̱ tin ca̱a̱t naath wi̱i̱c tilicä Nhiam kä Mɛrkɛm, kä kɛ me̱y ɣɔ̱n ger ajɛlɛkä wi̱i̱ pääm.
text_en: In the winter, enjoy some of the best skiing in North America, and in the summer try some authentic mountain biking.

text: Warɛkgak la̱t baa kɔn nyuɔth kɛɛ thiam.göri̱ ɣöö dëri̱ yi̱k tekɛ warɛgak  kɛɛ nhiam kɛ ɣöö dëri̱ kulɛ tɔ̱ɔ̱c kä Thi̱rɛna.
text_en: Permits must be reserved in advance. You must have a permit to stay overnight at Sirena.

text: Thi̱rɛna ɛjɛn gua̱a̱th lɔ̱ɔ̱ŋä rɛnyjɛr min mooc naath gua̱a̱th tɔ̱ɔ̱cä kɛnɛ kuan ti̱ gɔw mi̱ waa lɔ̱äŋ wä mat thi̱n. La liöna Than Pɛdiri̱lö kɛnɛ Löth Patöth mooc kɛn ni̱ naath gua̱th tɔ̱cä mi̱ thiɛl kuan.
text_en: Sirena is the only ranger station that offers dormitory lodging and hot meals in addition to camping. La Leona, San Pedrillo, and Los Patos offer only camping with no food service.

text: Tuɔɔk ɛ ɛn ɣöö dëri̱ thiëc ka̱n kɛ wädu kä rɛy kal le̱yni̱  kä thok kal kiɛ  rɛnyjɛr kä Puɛrtö Ji̱mɛnɛdh kuɛ laa ni̱ ɣöö /ci̱ kɛn katni̱ tin laa të yi̱o̱w rɛydiɛn go̱r.
text_en: It is possible to secure park permits directly from the Ranger Station in Puerto Jiménez, but they do not accept credit cards

text: Ɣɛn la̱t  rɛy kal le̱yni̱   (MINAE) cɛ naath jakä wä kä ti̱ ŋuan rɛy paay kɛl kɛ gua̱a̱th in pay  cop kɛ ji.
text_en: The Park Service (MINAE) does not issue park permits more than one month in advance of anticipated arrival.

text: KapɛNɛt El Thöl mocɛ naath gua̱th nyuurä kɛ yi̱o̱w ti̱ 30 kiɛ yi̱o̱w 10 nyin Mɛrkɛm kɛ cäŋ kɛl baa nyin ku la̱th kä Kɔnkɔbadöpej diɛn kiɛ wargak diɛn.
text_en: CafeNet El Sol offers a reservation service for a fee of US$30, or $10 for one-day passes; details on their Corcovado page.

text: Kɛn dhuɔ̱ɔ̱li̱ Kuuk kɛɛ dhuɔ̱ɔ̱l mi̱ rɛk min te̱e̱ kɛɛl kɛɛ Ni̱e̱w Dhi̱i̱lɛn min te̱ kä Pölini̱thia. däär jɔak ɣɔaa kä bäbdiit pa̱ci̱pik.
text_en: The Cook Islands are an island country in free association with New Zealand, located in Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific Ocean.

text: Jɛn ɛ pe̱k mi̱ te̱e̱ dhuɔ̱li̱ ti̱ wäl dhie̱e̱c ti̱ caa rɔ̱ wɛ̈r piny kɛ pe̱k mi̱ naŋ yie̱r bäpdiit mi̱ de̱e̱ kuɛ̈ɛ̈nkɛ laa ki̱li̱mi̱ti̱ri̱ toi̱ kuɔ̱r.
text_en: It is an archipelago with 15 islands spread out over 2.2 million km2 of ocean.

text: Te̱ kɛn kɛ kuën thaaka̱ mɛ kɛlɔ  kɛnɛ Ɣawai,kɛn dhuɔ̱li̱ laakɛ laa guɛckɛ" ce̱tkɛ mi̱ te̱kɛn pinh Ɣawai"
text_en: With the same time zone as Hawaii, the islands are sometimes thought of as "Hawaii down under".

text: Ɛca̱ŋ ni̱ min kuiyɛ,ti̱mɛ ja̱a̱l te̱e̱ wal ta̱a̱ Ɣawai ɛŋotdɛ ɛ /ke̱nɛ ni̱ laa we̱c mi̱ te̱kɛ ho̱tɛli̱ nyin ja̱a̱li̱ kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ in dɔ̱ŋ in vaa lätni̱ jɛ.
text_en: Though smaller, it reminds some elderly visitors of Hawaii before statehood without all the large tourist hotels and other development.

text: Kɛn dhuɔ̱li̱ Kuuk thiɛlɛ kɛ rɛ̈k kue̱ laa ni̱ ɣo̱o̱ te̱kɛn kɛɛ dhuɔ̱li̱ wal dhie̱e̱c ti̱ go̱o̱l. Tin jɔc ni̱ kɛn ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛ RRarɔtɔŋa kɛnɛ Aitutaki.
text_en: The Cook Islands do not have any cities but are composed of 15 different islands. The main ones are Rarotonga and Aitutaki.

text: Wi̱i̱ni̱ tin ci̱ cop ɣɛn pëk ɛ thiäkɛ, täa̱ dhaŋ tɔ̱ɔ̱cä mi̱ gɔaa kɛnɛ cäi̱ ruɔ̱n waaŋ caa kap nhial ɛla ɣat-puɔm.
text_en: In developed countries today, providing deluxe bed and breakfasts has been raised to a sort of art-form.

text: Ni̱ thuɔ̱k nhialɛ,B kɛnɛ Bs kɛ thuɔ̱k dɛ ko̱o̱ŋ kɛn kɛ kui̱c gua̱thni̱ da̱ŋ rɛw.. kuak tɔ̱ɔ̱ca̱ kɛnɛ cai̱ ruɔ̱nwaaŋ.
text_en: At the top end, B&Bs obviously compete mainly on two main things: bedding and breakfast.

text: Kɛ gua̱thdɛ kɛ pe̱k gɔɔya̱ dɛ. la̱t mi̱ cie̱ nɔmɔ raɛn bɛɛ go̱r ɣɛn ɣöö kuak tɔ̱ɔ̱cä  tin gɔw ni̱kɛn ɛlɔ̱ŋ, dɔ̱ŋ ɛmi̱ la̱tkɛ kɛ te̱t kiɛ dhaŋ mi̱ gɔa mi̱ ci̱ gua̱thdɛ wä.
text_en: Accordingly, at the finest such establishments one is apt to find the most luxurious bedding, maybe a handmade quilt or an antique bed.

text: Ca̱y ruɔ̱n waaŋ mat ɛ kɛ thin mäni̱ tin laa tɛɛth lɔc nath kɛ kɛ kiɛ kuan neeni̱ tin nyuɔ̱ɔ̱r kɛ naath.
text_en: Breakfast may include seasonal delights of the region or the host's speciality dish.

text: Jɛn ta̱a̱ in caa lätni̱jɛ dërɛ laa ta̱a̱ kɛ kui̱c ɣi̱tori̱ni̱ wecdiɛn kɛ la̱t jiɛn ti̱ gɔw, gua̱th in laa rial kɛ tet nath i̱ kä thi̱n kɛnɛ gua̱a̱th ket mi̱ caa täth.
text_en: The setting might be an historic old building with antique furnishings, manicured grounds and a swimming pool.

text: Mi̱ naŋi̱ thurbilu kä wä wi̱i̱ ja̱l gua̱a̱th mi̱ na̱n ɛ nhök mi̱ kä raan jɛn kä rɔa.
text_en: Getting into your own car and heading off on a long road trip has an intrinsic appeal in its simplicity.

text: Ɛ /ci̱ maa ta̱a̱ thuɔ̱rbiɛli̱ tin di̱t, kä dɔ̱ŋ mi̱ ci̱ ta̱a̱ ger thuɔ̱rbiɛl ŋa̱c kɛnɛ ci̱ ŋuɔ̱tkɛ ga̱c.
text_en: Unlike larger vehicles, you are probably already familiar with driving your car and know its limitations.

text: Mi̱ ci̱ tɛn yiath piny gua̱a̱th raami̱ dɔ̱ŋ kiɛ cäŋ ɛ rɛy rɛ̈ɛ̈k mi̱ tɔt kiɛ mi̱ di̱i̱t dërɛ nöŋ guëël ti̱ /ci̱ rɔ lot.
text_en: Setting up a tent on private property or in a town of any size can easily attract unwanted attention.

text: Ɛ ciɛk, na̱ŋdu kɛ thurbilu ɛ jɛn duɔ̱p in röŋ kɛ wä ja̱l duundɛ ɣöö kɛ ɣöö ciɛ mi̱ lätrɔ ni̱ ciaŋ ci̱ thia̱k ni̱ "tɔ̱ɔ̱c raar".
text_en: In short, using your car is a great way to take a road trip but seldom in itself a way to "camp".

text: Tɔ̱ɔ̱c raar kɛ thurbil laa lot ɛ rɔ mi̱ ti̱i̱ kɛɛ Miniban, SUV, Sidan kiɛ I̱thtecin Wagɔn min tekɛ kɔami̱ tin laa tɔ̱a̱a̱ckɛ.
text_en: Car camping is possible if you have a large minivan, SUV, Sedan or Station Wagon with seats that lay down.

text: Tha̱a̱ŋ ɣo̱teeli̱ tekɛn kɛ ta̱a̱ ciɛŋni tee wal kä run tee ŋot baabuur raar duŋ i̱thti̱i̱mä kɛnɛ ka̱p nath kɛ rɛy bäbdiit; ɛ ŋot ko̱r wecmuɔ̱ɔ̱n in rɛwdɛ, kɛ jɛn 19th kiɛ tuk 20th thenciɛri̱ni̱.
text_en: Some hotels have a heritage from the golden age of steam railways and ocean liners; before the Second World War, in the 19th or early 20th centuries.

text: Kɛn ɣo̱teeli̱ tɔ̱tɔ̱ ci̱ kɛ kɔn ria̱ŋ ɛ lɔ̱ŋ kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ gäcä kɛ ni̱n tee kɔn, kä ni̱ ciaŋ laa tekɛ kɛ gua̱th mieth ti̱ gɔw kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ ŋa̱a̱ri̱ wa̱r.
text_en: These hotels were where the rich and the famous of the day would stay, and often had fine dining and nightlife.

text: Jɛn ta̱a̱ läth bieyni̱ mee wal, kɛ thiɛl kuakni̱ tin rial ciaaŋi̱kä, kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ ciɛɛŋä dɔŋni̱ mi̱ gɔaa bikɛ jek kä ciɛŋkiɛn.
text_en: The old fashioned fittings, the lack of the latest amenities, and a certain graceful agedness are also part of their character.

text: Cäŋni̱ min kɛɛ nyin ji̱kiɛn gua̱thni̱ ti̱ ŋuan, Tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni̱ La kɛn kua̱r wec tin ci̱ bën guëël laa nyuur kɛnɛ nɛy tin luɔ̱thkɛ.
text_en: While they are usually privately owned, they sometimes accommodate visiting heads of state and other dignitaries.

text: Jääl mi̱ tekɛ yio̱w ti̱ ŋuan dërɛ ja̱l wecmuɔ̱ɔ̱n kɛ rieynhial lɛ ɣɔ̱n, Mi ci̱ ŋɔa̱a̱ŋ kɛ ciaaŋ rɛy ɣöteeli̱ ti̱ti̱.
text_en: A traveller with piles of money might consider a round the world flight, broken up with stays in many of these hotels.

text: Ta̱a̱ ji nyuurä ja̱a̱li̱ min laa 6 min la makämɛ min no̱o̱ŋ ja̱a̱l kɛnɛ ji wec gua̱th kɛl rɛy rɛkni̱ tin wä kɛn kɛ gui̱l.
text_en: A hospitality exchange network is the organization that connects travelers with locals in the cities they are going to visit.

text: Mi̱ mät i̱ rɔ kɛ jɛn buɔ̱n ɛ mɔ laa go̱o̱rkɛn ɣöö bi̱i̱ warɛgak thiäŋ rɛyjɔam; cäŋ ni min tha̱a̱ŋ buni̱ ŋunkɛn kiɛ go̱o̱r kɛ ɣöö warɛgakni̱ ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ nyuɔthkɛ.
text_en: Joining such a network usually just requires filling out an online form; although some networks offer or require additional verification.

text: Laa li̱th nɛɛni̱ tin laa nyuur naath ɛ ŋuɔnkɛ kɛɛ warɛgak kɛnɛ/kiɛ kɛ rɛy jɔam, tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni̱ kɛnɛ nɛy tin dee luɔtdiɛn thiëc kä kɛ kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ gɔyädiɛn kä ja̱a̱l tin kɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: A listing of available hosts is then provided either in print and/or online, sometimes with references and reviews by other travelers.

text: Köctha̱piŋ tuɔ̱k jɛ kɛɛ Paykɛl 2004 kɛ kɔr kä mee ci̱ ramkɛl mi̱ laa gɔ̱ɔ̱r ta̱a̱ la̱t kɔmputɛrä ni̱ Ka̱thɛy Pɛntɔn köt ria̱ynhial mi̱ kuiy yio̱wkɛ jek mi̱ wä kä Aithland duundɛ ɣöö känɛ gua̱a̱th mi̱ ciëŋɛ thi̱n wä jek.
text_en: Couchsurfing was founded in January 2004 after computer programmer Casey Fenton found a cheap flight to Iceland but did not have a place to stay.

text: Cuɛ warɛgak ja̱k kɛ rɛy jɔam mi̱ wä kä gaat  duel gɔrä kä jam in te wi̱c kä cu nɛy ti̱ ŋuani̱kɛn rɔ lar kɛ ɣöö dëkɛn ɛmoc kɛ gua̱a̱th nyuurä baaŋ.
text_en: He emailed students at the local university and received an overwhelming number of offers for free accommodation.

text: Ɣɔ̱thteli̱ kɛ tukdɛ laa te ni̱ ni̱ guɛ̈tni̱ thi̱n - tin la ja̱a̱l tin te kɛ run ti̱ jiɛnrɛwni̱ - duundɛ ɣöö gua̱thni̱ ti̱ ŋuan dëri̱ jääl mi̱ ci̱ del jɛk bä.
text_en: Hostels cater primarily to young people – a typical guest is in their twenties – but you can often find older travellers there too.

text: Dho̱r kɛnɛ gaat bum nendiɛn, duundɛ ɣöö tha̱a̱ŋ ɣɔ̱thtɛli̱ laa nhɔk rɛy dueli̱kiɛn
text_en: Families with children are a rare sight, but some hostels do allow them in private rooms.

text: Jɛn rɛk Bɛijiŋ kä Caina baa jɛn gua̱a̱th in la̱t kɛɛ Ŋa̱a̱ri̱ O̱lympik thin kɛ Jiɔm kɛɛ 2022, min bi̱ jɛ jakä ɣöö baa jɛn wec in ci̱ pɛ̈th kɛ ɣöö bɛɛ O̱lypik tɔa̱t kɛnɛ jiɔm la̱t.
text_en: The city of Beijing in China will be the host city of the Olympic Winter Games in 2022, which will make it the first city to have hosted both the summer and winter Olympics.

text: Bɛijiŋ bɛɛ theri̱mɔ̱ni̱ min lɛ̈pjɛ kɛnɛ ga̱kdɛ la̱t kɛnɛ ŋa̱a̱ri̱ tin la̱t kɛ rɛy luaak.
text_en: Beijing will host the opening and closing ceremonies and the indoor ice events.

text: Ŋa̱a̱ri̱ tin ca̱a̱t kɛ naath wi̱i̱c tilicä tin kɔ̱ŋ baa kɛ la̱t gua̱a̱th ca̱a̱tdä kä Taidhi̱cɛŋ, min tekɛ pëk mi̱ 220 km (140 miles) kɛnɛ Bɛijiŋ.
text_en: Other skiing events will be at the Taizicheng ski area in Zhangjiakou, about 220 km (140 miles) from Beijing.

text: Duel palä ti̱ guan la kɛn ɛ te kɛɛ pɛthti̱bɔl Run kä run ɛ took ɛ ni kɛ Paywälkɛl bɛ wä thuɔ̱k ni̱ kɛ där Paayŋuaan, min tekɛ dääk dueli̱ pali̱kiɛn kɛ kui̱c kalɛndɛrni̱kiɛn tin tekɛ dääk.
text_en: Most of the temples do have an Annual festival starting from November end to Mid of May, which varies according to each temple's annual calendar.

text: Gua̱th pali̱ ti̱ ŋuan laa lät kɛn ŋar ɛmɔ ɛ la pal kɛ kui̱c kä ɣöö mi̱ ci̱ ruɔ̱n thuɔ̱k kiɛ cäŋ däpä kuɔthdiɛn kiɛ ta̱a̱ ŋa̱a̱ri̱ tin kɔŋ tin laa nyin gua̱th palä.
text_en: Most of the temple festivals is celebrated as part of temple's anniversary or presiding deity's birthday or any other major event associated with the temple.

text: Pɛthtibɔl duŋ gua̱th palä Kɛrala ɛ mi̱ gɔaa guëcdɛ ɛ lɔ̱ŋ, laa tekɛ kɛ guɔ̱r mi̱ caa biɛl gua̱thni̱ ti̱ ŋuan, pua̱a̱t thuɔmni̱ gua̱th palä, kɛnɛ ŋa̱a̱ri̱ tɛthä lɔaac.
text_en: Kerala's temple festivals are very interesting to see, with regular procession of decorated elephants, temple orchestra and other festivities.

text: Ɛn Wääli̱th Pɛ̈ɛ̈r (min cɔalkɛ ni̱ ciaŋ i̱ Ɛ̈kpöthi̱cin wecmuɔ̱ɔ̱n, kiɛ ɛ thia̱k  Ɛkpö) ɛ jɛn pɛthti̱bɔl matdä wi̱i̱cni̱ ti̱ gööl kɛ ta̱a̱ kuurä kɛnɛ thaany.
text_en: A World's Fair (commonly called World Exposition, or simply Expo) is large international festival of arts and sciences.

text: Wi̱i̱c tin bä thi̱n laa nööŋkɛn nyin kuurädiɛn kä nyooth kɛn ta̱a̱ rikni̱wecmuɔ̱ɔ̱n kiɛ ta̱a̱ ciɛŋä wecdiɛn kɛnɛ lätkiɛn tee wal.
text_en: Participating countries present artistic and educational displays in national pavilions to showcase world issues or their country's culture and history.

text: Ho̱ti̱ka̱lciɛr Ɛ̈kpöthi̱cini̱ Wi̱i̱cni̱ ti̱ gööl laa la̱t kɛ kɛ ɛ la ti̱ bäl gɔɔydiɛn tin nyuɔthkɛ ta̱a̱ gaaki̱, bötani̱kɔl ga̱rdɛn kɛnɛ tin kɔ̱ŋ tin laa la̱tkɛ kɛ jiɛn.
text_en: International Horticultural Expositions are specialised events which showcase floral displays, botanical gardens and anything else to do with plants.

text: Cäŋni̱ mee lat jɛ i̱ dee kɛ laa la̱t ni̱ run ka̱ run ( cɛ jɔɔc ɛn ɣöö la kɛn ɛ jäny wi̱i̱cni̱ ti ŋuan ), mi̱ caa wä la̱th lät /cɛ laa lap a jɛn gua̱a̱thdɛ.
text_en: Although in theory they can take place annually (so long as they are in different countries), in practice they are not.

text: Kɛn ŋa̱a̱ri̱ ti̱ti̱ laa la̱t kɛ kɛ kɛ kɔr päthni̱ da̱ŋdiɔ̱k kiɛ bäkɛl, kä laa ŋarkɛ kɛ mi̱ di̱i̱t mi̱ tekɛ 50 hectares ɛ wä nhiam.
text_en: These events normally last anywhere between three and six months, and are held on sites no smaller than 50 hectares.

text: Tekɛ pɔmatni̱ pilimä ti̱ ŋuan tee laa lät kɛ naath kɛ run tee ci̱ wä, Min caa pa̱a̱r 35 mm pilim (36 kɛnɛ 24 mm ɛ wä piny) ɛ jɛn min ŋackɛ nji jɛ ɛ lɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: There are many different film formats that have been used over the years. Standard 35 mm film (36 by 24 mm negative) is much the commonest.

text: Kä jɛn thia̱k ɣöö dee mal thieŋ mi̱ cɛ thuɔ̱k, kä laa bee raar ɛ la mi̱ jɔc ɛ lɔ̱ŋ ɛ dëë pa̱a̱r ni̱ jɛn kɛnɛ  DSLR mɛ thia̱k ɛ.
text_en: It can usually be replenished fairly easily if you run out, and gives resolution roughly comparable to a current DSLR.

text: Tha̱a̱ŋ pɔmatdä pilimä kamɛrakä  min te däär laa lätdɛ kɛɛ 6 kɛnɛ 6 cm pɔmat, kɛ gua̱a̱thdɛ min thuɔ̱k ɛ 56 kɛnɛ 56 mm ɛ wä piny.
text_en: Some medium-format film cameras use a 6 by 6 cm format, more precisely a 56 by 56 mm negative.

text: Nɛmɛ rëëp ɛ jɔacdɛ ni̱ kä ti̱ cop ŋuaan kä jɛn mɔ te kɛɛ 35 mm ɛ wä piny kä baŋ (3136mm2 kɛɛ 864)
text_en: This gives resolution almost four times that of a 35 mm negative (3136 mm2 versus 864).

text: Ta̱a̱ lëëni̱ dɔaar ɛ kɛl kä tin bum ta̱a̱diɛn kä nɛy tin laa thuur ŋɔak, kä go̱o̱rɛ mat maŋni̱ kɛ liëp bitdä, kɛ ɣöö mi̱ ŋäc raan luɔtdɛ kɛnɛ kuak ti̱ gɔw.
text_en: Wildlife is among the most challenging motifs for a photographer, and needs a combination of good luck, patience, experience and good equipment.

text: Thuɔ̱r lëëni̱ dɔaar gua̱thni̱ ti̱ ŋuan /caa jɛ laa guɛckɛ ɛ la mi̱ thuɔ̱k, duundɛ cetkɛ ta̱a̱ thurä kɛɛ liw , thur dërɛ pa̱a̱r ni̱ kɛɛ riëët ti̱ cop ki̱thni̱.
text_en: Wildlife photography is often taken for granted, but like photography in general, a picture is worth a thousand words.

text: Thuɔ̱r lëëni̱ dɔaar gua̱thni̱ ti̱ ŋuan laa go̱o̱rɛ tɛlɛpötö lɛni̱ mi̱ bäär, cäŋni̱ min tekɛ ti̱ go̱o̱r lɛni̱ ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ cetkɛ diit ti̱ guan kiɛ muɔl piɛny ti̱ tɔatni̱.
text_en: Wildlife photography often requires a long telephoto lens, though things like a flock of birds or a tiny creature need other lenses.

text: Lëy ti̱ ŋuani̱kɛn tin laa jek kɛ wi̱c laa bum jekdiɛn, kä jɛn rɛk lëëni̱ nɔmɔ tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni̱ laa tekɛ ŋuɔ̱t kä thurɛni̱ tin naŋkɛ kɛ kui̱c kä baa kɛ wä nyuɔth.
text_en: Many exotic animals are hard to find, and parks sometimes have rules about taking photographs for commercial purposes.

text: Lëy duaar dɔ̱ŋ dëë kɛ dual kiɛ dëë kɛ ŋɛ̈ɛ̈ny. Jɛn gua̱th ciɛŋä dërɛ kɔa̱c, leth, kiɛ mi̱ ciɛ jɛn dëë ciaŋdɛ bɛ̈c.
text_en: Wild animals might either be shy or aggressive. The environment might be cold, hot, or otherwise hostile.

text: Jɛn wi̱cmuɔ̱n teekɛ thuk ti̱ gööl ti̱ bääl 5,000, kä ti̱ bääl jiɛnrɛw ruac nɛy ti̱ cop baathdɔɔri̱ ti̱ 50 kiɛ bääl nɛy tin ruac kɛ kɛ pëk ɛ mɔ.
text_en: The world has over 5,000 different languages, including more than twenty with 50 million or more speakers.

text: Riëët tin caa gɔa̱r piny laa mal ɛ liɛŋ kɛ ni kɛ riëët tin lat kɛ ni kɛ, bä. Nɛmɛ laa lab a jɛn gua̱thdɛ kä ti̱i̱t gua̱thni̱ ciɛgä tin laa bum läriɛn kɛ liëŋdiɛn gua̱thni̱ ti̱ ŋuan
text_en: Written words are often easier to understand than spoken words, also. This is especially true of addresses, which are often difficult to pronounce intelligibly.

text: Wi̱i̱c ti̱ ŋuan gua̱thni̱kiɛn dial ŋäckɛn ruac kɛ thok Iŋlic, kɛnɛ kɛ gua̱th ti̱ ŋuan biɛ yik ŋa̱c ɛn ɣöö bi̱ thiɛl ŋäcä- cetkɛ rɛy guɛ̱tni̱
text_en: Many entire nations are completely fluent in English, and in even more you can expect a limited knowledge - especially among younger people.

text: Kulɛ met nɛn, mi̱ wi̱i̱ , Ji Mancuna, Ji Böthtɔn, Ji Jamaika kɛnɛ Ji thydnɛythaidɛr nyurkɛ geekni̱ tharbedä mi̱thkɛ kä thuk miëth kä Tɔro̱ntö.
text_en: Imagine, if you will, a Mancunian, Bostonian, Jamaican and Sydneysider sitting around a table having dinner at a restaurant in Toronto.

text: Lät kɛn dɔaal kam ni̱ kiɛn kɛ kui̱c ɣi̱thtɔri̱ni̱ gua̱thni̱ tin bä kɛ thin, lat kɛn kɛ kɛ thuk ti̱ gööl kɛnɛ thokdiɛn kɛn guëtni̱.
text_en: They're regaling each other with stories from their hometowns, told in their distinct accents and local argot.

text: Kök kua̱n kä thuperma̱rkɛtni̱ tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni̱ ɛ jɛn duɔ̱p in thia̱k kökdɛ mi̱ dëë mi̱th kɛ raar. Mi̱ thiɛlɛ gua̱th mi̱ thät kɛ raan, laa thiɛl ɛ gua̱a̱th mi̱ dɔ̱ŋ ɛ ni̱ kuän mi̱ ci̱ tuak.
text_en: Buying food in supermarkets is usually the cheapest way to get fed. Without cooking opportunities, choices are however limited to ready-made food.

text: Kɛ ta̱a̱ mi̱ rëëprɔ thuperma̱rkɛtni̱ läthkɛn gua̱th ti̱ ŋuani̱kɛn piny kɛ kui̱c kuan ti̱ ci̱ tuak. Tha̱a̱ŋkiɛn la kɛn maikröwɛb ɛ tho̱p kiɛ tha̱a̱ŋkiɛn baa kuän thɔl.
text_en: Increasingly supermarkets are getting a more varied section of ready-made food. Some even provide a microwave oven or other means to heat food.

text: Tha̱a̱ŋ wi̱i̱cni̱ kiɛ thukni̱ ti̱ gööl laa te kɛ thuk miëth ɛ cäŋ ɛ kɛl rɛydɛ, ni̱ ciaŋ /cɛ laa di̱tdɛ kä laa kui̱y yio̱wkɛ.
text_en: In some countries or types of stores there is at least one on-site restaurant, often a rather informal one with affordable prices.

text: Lätni̱ jɛ kä kap kɔpi̱dɛ jɛn warɛgak pɔli̱thi̱kädu kɛnɛ kɔ̱ntakni̱ incuärɛr duŋdu kɛ rɔ kɛɛl.
text_en: Make and carry copies of your policy and your insurer's contact details with you.

text: Go̱o̱rɛ ɣöö bɛɛ jɛ nyoth jɛn e-mail addrɛth duŋ incuärɛrkä kɛnɛ nämbär ja̱a̱thädɛ kɛ kui̱c kä ɣöö dëri luäk kɛ cär/kɛnɛ ɣöö dee ji̱ nhök ja̱l kɛnɛ ɣöö mi̱ go̱o̱ri̱ duɔ̱ɔ̱r.
text_en: They need to show the insurer's e-mail address and international phone numbers for advice/authorizations and making claims.

text: Läthni̱ kɔpi̱ mi̱ dɔ̱ŋ rɛy kuakni̱ku kɛnɛ rɛyjɔam (jäkni̱ jɛ kä rɔ kɛɛ e-mail, kiɛ tɔ̱wɛ kä klɔɔd")
text_en: Have another copy in your luggage and online (e-mail to yourself with attachment, or stored in the "cloud").

text: Mi jäli̱ kɛɛ laptɔp kiɛ tablɛt, tɔ̱w kɔpi̱ rɛydɛ kiɛ di̱thk ( mi̱ dee jek ɛ thiɛl intɛrnɛt).
text_en: If traveling with a laptop or tablet, store a copy in its memory or disc (accessible without the internet).

text: Ɛ nyɔk bä tho̱bni̱ kɔpi̱ pɔli̱thi̱/kɔntrak ramin jäl yiɛn kɛɛl kɛnɛ ji maarä kiɛ mäthni̱ tin ci̱ duɔth ciäŋ tin nhɔk ɣöö dee ji̱ luäk.
text_en: Also give policy/contact copies to traveling companions and relatives or friends back home willing to help.

text: Muuth ( min laa cɔalkɛ bä i̱ ëlk) /ci̱kɛ ti̱ ca̱l ta̱a̱ köör, duundɛ la kɛn rɔ laa gaŋ mi̱ caa kɛ ŋuɔ̱k ko̱r.
text_en: Moose (also known as elk) aren't inherently aggressive, but will defend themselves if they perceive a threat.

text: Gua̱a̱th in gui̱c naath ɛ i̱ muuth /ciɛ mi̱ dëë naath näk, dëë kɛn jɛ ɣɔ̱n ɛn bi̱ rɔ thieek ni̱ kɛ jɛ kä dëë kɛn rɔ la̱th rɛy rikä.
text_en: When people don't see moose as potentially dangerous, they may approach too closely and put themselves at risk.

text: Mäthni kɛ kɔaŋ kɛ tiit.Kɔaŋ yärɛ naath kɛ dup ti gööl,min bum ni jɛn ɛ ɣöö ŋäcni pek mäthdu.
text_en: Drink alcoholic drinks with moderation. Alcohol affects everyone differently, and knowing your limit is very important.

text: Ma̱th kɔaŋ mi̱ di̱i̱t yärɛ cuäny ran kɛnɛ wäŋkɛ kä no̱ŋɛ lia̱a̱. Jiääkdɛ min di̱i̱t ɛ mäth kɔaani̱ tin /caa nhɔk ɛ kumɛ.
text_en: Possible long term health events from excessive drinking can include liver damage and even blindness and death. The potential danger is increased when consuming illegally produced alcohol.

text: Koaaŋ tin la̱tkɛ kɛ piny ɛ thiɛlɛ kumɛ ŋääc jiäk kɛn kä no̱ŋkɛn naath lia̱a̱ mi thia̱k.
text_en: Illegal spirits can contain various dangerous impurities including methanol, which can cause blindness or death even in small doses.

text: Ne̱e̱ni̱ waŋ de̱e̱ kök diɛn kuɛ̱̈ɛ̱̈ ro̱l midɔŋ,cetkɛ röl tin te̱ kɛ yio̱w ti tɔt guäth tin kuiy yio̱w tin la̱tkɛ naath thin.Bum ni jek waŋ.
text_en: Eyeglasses can be cheaper in a foreign country, especially in low-income countries where labour costs are lower.

text: Go̱r ɣöö baa wäŋku thɛm mi ti̱i̱ ce̱ŋ kä ti̱i̱ kɛ nɛy ti̱ de̱e̱ due̱l wälu yuɔr piny,kä bi̱ cu jääl kɛ wargak duël wälu.
text_en: Consider getting an eye exam at home, especially if insurance covers it, and bringing the prescription along to be filed elsewhere.

text: Tin di̱t kökdiɛn kä te thi̱n rɛy dho̱ri tɔ̱tɔ̱ deekɛ tekɛ rik da̱ŋ rɛw; tha̱a̱ŋkiɛn deekɛ thiɛl luɔt, kä tin nööŋkɛ wi̱i̱ni ti gööl dee kökdiɛn di̱t ɛlɔ̱ŋ mi leny ni kök kuakni tin te wi̱c ni wen.
text_en: High-end brand-name frames available in such areas may have two problems; some may be knock-offs, and the real imported ones may be more expensive than at home.

text: Bun ɛ kɛl kä tin kɔakɛ.De̱ri gua̱th bunä ti gööl  je̱k gua̱a̱th ciɛŋkädu.
text_en: Coffee is one of the world's most traded commodities, and you can probably find many types in your home region.

text: Tëëkɛ dup ti ŋuan ti mathkɛ bun wi̱i̱ muɔ̱ɔ̱n ti lotrɔ̱ kɛ ɣöö dëë ŋa̱c.
text_en: Nevertheless, there are many distinctive ways of drinking coffee around the world that are worth experiencing.

text: La naath ɛ ŋar kɛ kaac yie̱r wi̱i̱ po̱mkä guäth in ci yiër thia̱a̱ŋ kɛ pi̱w.
text_en: Canyoning (or: canyoneering) is about going in a bottom of a canyon, which is either dry or full of water.

text: Ŋa̱a̱ri ti ce̱tkɛ kët yiër, köt päämni̱ kɛnɛ ka̱c go̱o̱rkɛn ŋi̱i̱c mi tɔt kiɛ buɔ̱m pua̱a̱ny kɛ tukdiɛn.(/ci kɛn päär kɛ köt päämni̱ ti di̱i̱t,kët mi wëë ni piny yiër elɔ̱ŋ ki̱ɛ rami̱ ŋar rɛy talackä)
text_en: Canyoning combines elements from swimming, climbing and jumping--but requires relatively little training or physical shape to get started (compared to rock climbing, scuba diving or alpine skiing, for example).

text: Jäl rɛy ruɔ̱p ɛ mi la̱tkɛ guäth mi̱ na̱n kɛ ciëŋ, la raan ɛ wä ja̱l rɛy gua̱thni ti gööl.
text_en: Hiking is an outdoor activity which consists of walking in natural environments, often on hiking trails.

text: Jäl rɛy ruɔ̱ɔ̱p kɛ cäŋdäär tëë kɛ käth mi̱ di̱i̱t mi̱ de̱e̱ ran ɛ ja̱l.
text_en: Day hiking involves distances of less than a mile up to longer distances that can be covered in a single day.

text: Nɛy ti̱ caa ŋiääc ɛ määth kɛ jäl rɛy ruɔ̱ɔ̱p go̱rkɛn rialikä mi tɔt rɛy ja̱liɛn.
text_en: For a day hike along an easy trail little preparations are needed, and any moderately fit person can enjoy them.

text: Dho̱r ti̱ te̱ kɛ gaat ti̱ tiatni̱ go̱rkɛn riali̱kä mi̱ gɔa, duŋdɛ ɣöö mi la̱t jɛ raar duel thiɛlɛ mi de̱e̱ gaat je̱k amäni gaat duël gɔ̱rä.
text_en: Families with small children may need more preparations, but a day outdoors is easily possible even with babies and pre-school children.

text: Rɛy wi̱i̱cni̱ ti gööl te̱ muktäbni ti cop 200 ti lät la̱t ɛmɛ thi̱n, riwdiɛn cuŋ kɛn kä rɔ̱diɛn.
text_en: Internationally, there are nearly 200 running tour organizations. Most of them operate independently.

text: Ɛn Ŋar wuurä wi̱i̱ muɔ̱ɔ̱n, ala Wuɔ̱r Ŋarä mi gɔa tëë kɛ nɛy ti ŋuan ti wur thi̱n kä däwläni da̱ŋ ŋuaan.
text_en: The Global Running Tours successor, Go Running Tours networks dozens of sightrunning providers on four continents.

text: Duɔ̱p wurkä min te kä Barcelona kɛnɛ Copenhagen, caa kɛ röm kɛnɛ duɔ̱p mi̱ te̱ kä Prague kene wi̱i̱c tin kɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: With roots in Barcelona's Running Tours Barcelona and Copenhagen's Running Copenhagen, it was quickly joined by Running Tours Prague based in Prague and others.

text: Tëë kɛ ti ŋuan ti̱ lotrɔ̱ kɛ ŋa̱c ɛ ŋot ja̱l ɛn wi̱i̱ thi̱n kiɛ rɛy ja̱l ɛn ti̱i̱ thi̱n.
text_en: There are many things you have to take into consideration before and when you travel somewhere.

text: Mi̱ ti̱i̱ rɛy ja̱l, ŋäcni jɛ ɛn ɣöö bi̱ ŋɔak ti̱ ŋuan te̱kɛ dääk a /ci ma "ta̱a̱ ciëŋ in bi̱i̱ thi̱n". Ciaŋ nath, miäth ɛn bi cam rɛy we̱c ɛmɔ, ŋuɔ̱t, ŋuan thurbiɛli, guäth lɔ̱ŋä, thok ɛn ruac kɛ naath bɛ te dääk mi̱ di̱i̱t kɛ ji̱.
text_en: When you travel, expect things not to be like they are "back home". Manners, laws, food, traffic, lodging, standards, language and so on will to some extent differ from where you live.

text: Nɛmɛ ɛ kɛl mi lotrɔ kɛ ta̱a̱ rɛy cäri̱ ran kɛ ɣöö cɛ ji̱ bi moc ga̱a̱c mi̱ di̱i̱t kɛ tukdiɛn ɛ de̱rɛ ciandu nyon.
text_en: This is something you always need to keep in mind, to avoid disappointment or perhaps even distaste over local ways to do things.

text: Muktäb ja̱l tëë thi̱n ni̱kɛ ruɔ̱n bathdɔɔr ɛn wäl bäŋuandiɛn. Muktäb ja̱l gɔa ɛ kä nɛy ti̱ wëë röli ti tok kɛn ni wä thi̱n.
text_en: Travel agencies have been around since the 19th century. A travel agent is usually a good option for a journey which extends beyond a traveller's previous experience of nature, culture, language or low-income countries.

text: Nɛy ti ŋuan nhɔk kɛn ɣöö bikɛ thurbil jur ɛŋot guäth jiɛnkädɛ,tëë kɛ naath ti̱ latni̱ pek yio̱ni kɛnɛ guäth ɛn bi̱ jäl guut thi̱n.
text_en: Although most agencies are willing to take on most regular bookings, many agents specialise in particular types of travel, budget ranges or destinations.

text: Go̱r ɣöö bi kuanyni rami̱ bi jur kä thurbil ɛn bi jälkɛ jɛ.
text_en: It can be better to use an agent who frequently books similar trips to yours.

text: Ŋäcni̱ tin la̱tkɛ ɛ naath tin la̱a̱t guäth thurbiɛli guäth in la kɛn läärikiɛn ɛ tho̱p kɛ jɛ.
text_en: Take a look at what trips the agent is promoting, whether on a website or in a shop window.

text: Mi̱ go̱o̱ri̱ ɣöö bi̱ ta̱a̱ we̱cmuɔ̱ɔ̱n ŋa̱c kɛnɛ cɛŋ nath amäni tin tuɔɔk thi̱n tëë kɛ dup ti̱ deri̱ jɛ la̱t kɛ jɛ.
text_en: If you want to see the world on the cheap, for necessity, lifestyle or challenge, there are some ways to do that.

text: Tëë kɛ dup da̱ŋ rɛw ti̱ de̱ri̱ la̱th lät gua̱a̱th in jäli̱ kɛnɛ ɣöö bi̱ yio̱ku tit rɛy ja̱lu.
text_en: Basically, they fall into two categories: Either work while you travel or try and limit your expenses. This article is focused on the latter.

text: Nɛy tin go̱r ɣöö de̱e̱ kɛn cɛŋ tin naŋ yio̱w ti̱ ŋuan päl kɛ ɣöö bi pek yio̱nikiɛn loc guäthdiɛn,tëë kɛ duɔ̱p mi caa rialikä kɛ kuidiɛn.
text_en: For those willing to sacrifice comfort, time and predictability to push expenses down close to zero, see minimum budget travel.

text: Latkɛ jɛ ɛn ɣöö ja̱a̱l /ci kɛnɛ kue̱l, /ci kɛn lät ti̱ caa nhɔk ɛ kumɛ lät, /ci̱ kɛn li̱m kä /ci kɛn naath mɛt kɛ ka̱a̱cni̱ kɛ kui̱ kä mi gɔa mi de̱e̱ kɛnɛ je̱k.
text_en: The advice assumes that travellers do not steal, trespass, participate in the illegal market, beg, or otherwise exploit other people for their own gain.

text: Muktäb ja̱a̱li ɛjɛn gua̱a̱th in nhiam min thuɔlkɛ naath thi̱n mi ci cop kä mataar kiɛ gua̱a̱th thurbiɛɛli.
text_en: An immigration checkpoint is usually the first stop when disembarking from a plane, a ship, or another vehicle.

text: Guäthni kɔ̱kiɛn,laa thuɔlkɛ naath rɛy gatɔar ɛ tëë jäl.Kä inɔ bi̱i̱ wargakni̱ jälu cu rɔm kɛ te̱tdu kɛ guäth in kɔtdi gatɔr ɛmɔ.
text_en: In some cross-border trains inspections are done on the running train and you should have valid ID with you when boarding one of those trains.

text: Rɛy gatɔri tin laa ja̱l kɛ wäär la gëër wargakni jäl nath ɛ thɔl kɛ ɣöö ca niän ran bi̱ lɛ ya̱r.
text_en: On night sleeper trains, passports may be collected by the conductor so that you do not have your sleep interrupted.

text: Gɔ̱ɔ̱r ciöötni piny ɛ kɛl mi̱ bum kä lät wargakni ja̱l. Röli tin kɔ̱ŋ baa ciötdu gɔ̱a̱r piny kɛ nhiam amäni guäth ciɛŋkädu bi̱ wargak ja̱l kulɛ je̱k.
text_en: Registration is an additional requirement for the visa process. In some countries, you must register your presence and address where you are staying with the local authorities.

text: Nɛmɛ go̱o̱rɛ wargak mi bi thiäŋ rɛy kal kumɛ kiɛ kä muktäb ji̱ ja̱l.
text_en: This might require filling out a form with the local police or a visit to the immigration offices.

text: Rɛy wi̱i̱cni̱ ti ŋuan ti̱ te̱ kɛ ŋuɔ̱t mi ce̱tkɛ nɛmɛ, laa ciöt nath ɛ gɔ̱a̱rkɛ piny ɛ nɛy tin jur duel ja̱a̱li̱ (thi̱ecni̱).
text_en: In many countries with such a law, local hotels will handle the registration (make sure to ask).

text: Tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni̱ nɛy tin cie̱ŋ raar duëli ja̱a̱li ɛkɛn laa ciöötkiɛn ɛ gɔ̱a̱rkɛ piny. Nɛmɛ no̱o̱ŋɛ kui̱c ŋuɔ̱tni̱ kä nɛy ti̱ ŋuan.Thiecni̱ kɛ nhiam.
text_en: In other cases, only those staying outside of tourist accommodations need to register.  However, this makes the law much more obscure, so find out beforehand.

text: La̱a̱t duëli kɛ nɛy tin laa duël ɛ thur kä lätkɛn kɛ.Ta̱th duëli no̱o̱ŋɛ yio̱w kä nɛy tin nhɔakɛ nën duëli̱ tɔ̱tɔ̱.
text_en: Architecture is concerned with the design and construction of buildings. The architecture of a place is often a tourist attraction in its own right.

text: Duël ti ŋuan caa kɛ täth ɛ gɔa kä gɔa nëndiɛn gua̱thni̱ diaal.
text_en: Many buildings are quite beautiful to look at and the view from a tall building or from a cleverly-positioned window can be a beauty to behold.

text: Läät duëli̱ te kɛn kɛ la̱t ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ kä kumɛ ce̱tkɛ la̱t caari, la̱t jäthkä, lätni wec mi gɔa, riali wec ikä kɛnɛ kuak tin kɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Architecture overlaps considerably with other fields including urban planning, civil engineering, decorative arts, interior design and landscape design.

text: Thiɛlɛ gua̱a̱th mi te̱ kɛ thuukni̱ kɔaŋ kɛ wäär rɛy we̱c Pueblos kɛ ɣöö ŋot wecdiɛn /känɛ ni̱ cop ɛgɔa duŋdɛ ɣöö te̱ kɛn kä Albuquerque kiɛ Santa Fe.
text_en: Given how remote many of the pueblos are, you won't be able to find a significant amount of nightlife without traveling to Albuquerque or Santa Fe.

text: Guäth ŋa̱a̱ri tin caa lat kɛ nhiam, kɔkɛn ti̱ maathkɛ kä riwdiɛn no̱o̱ŋkɛn ciööt ti gööl (guäth tin di̱t te kɛn kä Albuquerque kɛnɛ Santa Fe).
text_en: However, nearly all of the casinos listed above serve drinks, and several of them bring in name-brand entertainment (primarily the large ones immediately surrounding Albuquerque and Santa Fe).

text: Ŋäcni jɛ ɛn ɣöö guäth kɔaaŋni ti tɔt ci kɛn rɔ̱ lot kɛ jäl mi bi̱i̱ guäth mi dɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Beware: small-town bars here are not always good places for the out-of-state visitor to hang out.

text: Wec Northern Mexico tëë kɛ riɛk nɛɛni̱ ti gɛ̈rkɛ thurbiɛɛli̱ ɛ cikɛ maath kɛ kɔaaŋ, kä kɔaaŋ ɛti kɔkɛn kɛ rɛy wi̱i̱c tin tiɛtni̱.
text_en: For one thing, northern New Mexico has significant problems with drunk driving, and the concentration of intoxicated drivers is high close to small-town bars.

text: Ŋɔak ti̱ ca thuɔ̱r puɔ̱ɔ̱ny duëël kɛnɛ gɔ̱a̱a̱r ti te puɔ̱ɔ̱ny duëël cɔalkɛ kɛ i̱ thurɛni̱.
text_en: Unwanted murals or scribble is known as graffiti.

text: Cäŋni mɔ kɛ nyin rɛ̈ɛ̈k ɔ, car nɛy ti ŋuanɛ ikɛ ŋuɛ̈tni̱ i̱ kɛ kɛn lät la̱t mi ce̱tkɛ nɛmɛ.
text_en: While it's far from a modern phenomenon, most people probably associate it with youth vandalizing public and private property using spray paint.

text: kɛ gua̱a̱th ɛmɛ ca guäth rialikä kɛ kui̱ thurɛni tɔ̱tɔ̱, kɛ ɣöö nyoothkɛn ca̱r mi gɔa ka ŋuɛ̈tni.
text_en: However, nowadays there are established graffiti artists, graffiti events and "legal" walls. Graffiti paintings in this context often resemble artworks rather than illegible tags.

text: Yori̱ dëëp ɛ kɛl mi göörkɛ ŋäcdɛ ɛ nɛyti ŋuan.
text_en: Boomerang throwing is a popular skill that many tourists want to acquire.

text: Mi go̱ri ɣöö bi yori̱ dëëp mi̱ bi̱ luny te̱tkädu ŋäc, go̱r de̱p mi bäär mi rɔ̱ŋ kɛ wä amäni luny jɔk.
text_en: If you want to learn throwing a boomerang that comes back to your hand, make sure you have a suitable boomerang for returning.

text: Yori̱ de̱pni̱ tin te ka̱ Australia /ci kɛnɛ luny jɔk kä raan. /Cɛ rɔ lot kɛ ɣöö bi rami̱ tookni jɛ kɛ ŋar gua̱a̱th mi tekɛ jiɔm ɛ yuɔr.
text_en: Most boomerangs available in Australia are in fact non-returning. It is best for beginners to not try throwing in windy

text: 'Hangi'' ɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p mi la thal kɛ miäth rɛy puɔ̱ɔ̱l mi caa mol.
text_en: A Hangi Meal is cooked in a hot pit in the ground.

text: Rɛy puɔ̱ɔ̱l ɛmɔ laa muɔckɛ jɛ kɛ pääm ti le̱th bi piny kulɛ lëth ɛ gɔa.
text_en: The pit is either heated with hot stones from a fire, or in some places geothermal heat makes areas of ground naturally hot.

text: Duɔ̱ɔ̱p ɛmɛ laa thalkɛ ni kuan rɛy ciëŋ kɛ jɛ.
text_en: The hangi is often used to cook a traditional roast style dinner.

text: Guäth  tin te̱ kä Rotorua te̱ kɛn kɛ mac mi rɔ̱ŋ kɛnɛ Christchurch, Wellington amäni̱ gua̱th tin kɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Several places in Rotorua offer geothermal hangi, while other hangi can be sampled in Christchurch, Wellington and elsewhere.

text: Ɛn caar babuur raar tëëkɛ gua̱th da̱ŋ rɛw rɛy kɛnɛ rar wec Cape in di̱i̱t: MetroPlus (Mi cɔalkɛ bä i̱ Kilɛ̈th in Nhiam) kɛnɛ Caar mi cɔali (Kilɛ̈th in Diɔ̱ɔ̱kdiɛn).
text_en: MetroRail has two classes on commuter trains in and around Cape Town: MetroPlus (also called First Class) and Metro (called Third Class).

text: Gatɔr piɛny ɛmɛ gɔa ja̱lɛ kä thiɛlɛ jɛ nɛy ti ŋuan duŋdɛ ɣöö ŋuan yio̱kɛ kä gatɔr in te̱ kä Europe.
text_en: MetroPlus is more comfortable and less crowded but slightly more expensive, though still cheaper than normal metro tickets in Europe.

text: Gatɔri diaal te̱ kɛn kɛ ji̱ duëël wa̱l ti nyuur ni jɔk gatɔaar ɛn thieek kɛ wec Cape in Di̱i̱t.
text_en: Every train has both MetroPlus and Metro coaches; the MetroPlus coaches are always on the end of the train nearest Cape Town.

text: Ɛ ɣa̱cdu /ci bath waaŋdu gua̱a̱th in ŋoo k i̱ dup röli̱ ti̱ gööl.
text_en: Carrying for others - Never let your bags out of your sight, especially when you are crossing international borders.

text: De̱ri rɔ je̱k rɛy rikä a thiɛlɛ ji ŋäc kɛ ɣöö dëë ɣa̱cdu re̱p kɛ kuak ti ca nhɔk ɛ ji̱ kumɛ kä inɔ dëë ji̱ yiɛn kä thijin.
text_en: You could find yourself being used as a drug carrier without your knowledge, which will land you in a great deal of trouble.

text: Gua̱a̱th ɛn ti̱i̱ kä thäp dëë jio̱k jakä jäl kamni nath ɛ thiɛlɛ yɛ ŋäc.
text_en: This includes waiting in line, as drug-sniffing dogs could be used at any time without notice.

text: Röl ti ŋuan thiɛlɛ kɛ pälikä kɛ duer mi ce̱tkɛ nɛmɛ. Derɛ ji̱ nööŋ yie̱n kɛ run 10 kiɛ lia̱a̱.
text_en: Some countries have exceedingly draconian punishments even for first time offenses; these can include prison sentences of over 10 years or death.

text: Ɣa̱a̱c ti̱ kän thol dëë kɛ diw kɛ ɣöö dɔ̱ŋ caa mäc buɔmni kap kɛ kɛ.
text_en: Unattended bags are a target for theft and can also attract attention from authorities wary of bomb threats.

text: Gua̱a̱th ciɛŋkädu mi̱ tëë kɛ ni̱ɛt mi̱ di̱i̱t, nyoothɛ jɛ ɛn ɣöö ci jɛ ŋic.
text_en: At home, due to this constant exposure to the local germs, odds are very high that you're already immune to them.

text: Duŋdɛ ɣöö de̱e̱ ciandu bɛ̈c mi̱ ti̱i̱ guääth mi̱ /ke̱ni̱ ŋic.
text_en: But in other parts of the world, where the bacteriological fauna are new to you, you're far more likely to run into problems.

text: Guääth in le̱th piny,niɛt la tëë raar puɔ̱ɔ̱ny ran ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä la jänyɛ raar puɔ̱ɔ̱ny ran kɛ gua̱a̱th mi ba̱a̱r.
text_en: Also, in warmer climates bacteria both grow more quickly and survive longer outside the body.

text: Rik tin te kä Delhi Belly, kä Lam Pɛ̈ɛ̈röö, ga̱m Montezuma kɛ ko̱r, kɛnɛ mäthnikɛ ti ŋuan.
text_en: Thus the scourges of Delhi Belly, the Pharaoh's Curse, Montezuma's Revenge, and their many friends.

text: Gua̱a̱th in kɔ̱c piny bi̱ jiɔm te̱kɛ dääk kä gua̱a̱th in le̱th piny kä bi̱ ci̱i̱n raan cu bɛ̈c duŋdɛ ɣöö ɛ bɛ̈c mi tɔt.
text_en: As with respiratory problems in colder climates, intestinal problems in hot climates are fairly common and in most cases are distinctly annoying but not really dangerous.

text: Mi jeli rɛy we̱c mi̱ caa tääth ɛlɔ̱ŋ kiɛ we̱c mi /käni me̱t gui̱l, ŋäcni jɛ ɛn ɣöö bi̱ ŋɔak ti gööl nɛn.
text_en: If traveling in a developing country for the first time – or in a new part of the world – don't underestimate the potential culture shock.

text: Rami jel  rɛy wi̱i̱cni̱ ti caa täth de̱rɛ ciaaŋ nɛɛni ti gööl dɔp, gua̱a̱th mi dee ciɛŋ ti kɔ̱ŋ rɔ̱ mal nyuɔ̱ɔ̱th kɛ pɛ̈th.
text_en: Many a stable, capable traveler has been overcome by the newness of developing world travel, where many little cultural adjustments can add up quickly.

text: Ce̱tkɛ kɛ ta̱a̱du mee wal,Naŋɛ kɛ ta̱a̱ rɛɛk kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ in de̱ri̱ yio̱w cam kɛ jɛ kɛnɛ miëthdu kɛ kuän kɛ wä ka̱ o̱tɛ̈li̱  tin gɔw ̱ kɛ ɣöö dërɛ ji luäk kɛ ɣöö dëri aklimataidh.
text_en: Especially in your initial days, consider splurging on Western-style and -quality hotels, food, and services to help acclimatize.

text: Cuu tɔ̱c wi̱i̱ matäbɛkä kiɛ ko̱l piɛ̈ny ŋua̱th mi̱ kui̱ci̱ le̱y tin të thi̱n.
text_en: Do not sleep on a mattress or pad on the ground in areas where you do not know the local fauna.

text: Mi̱ go̱o̱ri̱ tɔ̱ɔ̱c tuunyä,no̱o̱ŋnii̱ kɛmɛ kɔt kiɛ amɔk kɛ ɣöö bɛ ji̱ gaŋ kɛ thɔ̱ɔ̱l, jiɛ̈th kɛnɛ ti̱ ciä tɔ̱tɔ̱ni̱.
text_en: If you are going to camp out, bring a camp cot or hammock to keep you away from snakes, scorpions and such.

text: Thiäŋ  cieŋdu kɛɛ bun mi̱ gɔaa kɛ runwaŋ kɛnɛ ca̱i mi päl rɔ piny ɛla camömilɛ.
text_en: Fill your home with a rich coffee in the morning and some relaxing chamomile tea at night.

text: Mi̱ ti̱i̱ kä i̱thtɛikeecɔn,ti̱i̱ kɛ ŋua̱a̱th kɛ ɣöö dëri̱ rɔ moc ilac kä ti̱i̱ kɛ diɛgiɛ̈ɛ̈kni̱ ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ kɛ ɣöö dëri̱ mi̱ gɔaa riali̱kä.
text_en: When you're on a staycation, you have the time to treat yourself and take a few extra minutes to brew up something special.

text: Mi̱ jëki̱ rɔ ɛla ɣöö dëri̱ ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ la̱t,naŋ gua̱th kɛ ɣöö dëri̱ i̱thmuuthi̱thni̱ lät kɛ la̱t juudhä kiɛ dëri̱ kɛ blën.
text_en: If you're feeling more adventurous, take the opportunity to juice or blend up some smoothies:

text: Dɔ̱ŋ dëri̱ bɛbɛrɛc thia̱m piny ɛthia̱k mi̱ dëri̱ lɛl ɛla ca̱i ruɔ̱nwaaŋ mi̱ ci̱ lunyjɔk kä la̱tku tin wën tin laa lätdi̱.
text_en: maybe you'll discover a simple beverage that you can make for breakfast when you're back to your daily routine.

text: Mi̱ ti̱i̱ rɛɛk mi̱ tëkɛ ti̱ gööl ti̱ mathkɛ,lɛni̱ wä kä käläbni̱ kɛnɛ duel mäth tin thiëk kɛ yiɛ  tin /ke̱ni̱ mët wä thi̱n ni̱ wën.
text_en: If you live in a city with a varied drinking culture, go to bars or pubs in neighborhoods you don't frequent.

text: Kɛ kui̱c nɛni̱ tin kue̱ckɛ ta̱a̱ wal,riët kä ɣöö inpɛ̈kciööth kiɛ kɔntɛji̱ööth  te̱ kɛn kɛ dääk ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: For those unfamiliar with medical jargon, the words infectious and contagious have distinct meanings.

text: Juëy in la inpɛkciiööth no̱o̱ŋɛ pa̱thögi̱n, cëtkɛ baira̱th, bakti̱riöm, pungi̱ni̱,kiɛ pa̱rathaitni̱ tin kɔ̱kiɛn.
text_en: An infectious disease is one that is caused by a pathogen, such as a virus, bacterium, fungus or other parasites.

text: Juëy in la kɔntɛji̱öth jɛn ɛ juëy mi̱ thiäk jëkdɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ  mi̱ të raan kɛɛl kɛ ram mi̱ të kɛ juëy ɛmɔ.
text_en: A contagious disease is a disease which is easily transmitted by being in the vicinity of an infected person.

text: Ji̱ kumɛ wi̱i̱ni̱ ti̱ ŋuan la kɛnɛ  laa  go̱o̱r ɣɛn ɣöö nɛy tin ja̱a̱l tin bä wi̱c kɛnɛ ji̱ wëc tin wä wi̱i̱ni̱ tin kɔ̱kiɛn ɣɛn ɣöö dëëkɛ tuɔm kɛ kui̱c juäthni̱ ti̱ gööl.
text_en: Many governments require visitors entering, or residents leaving, their countries to be vaccinated for a range of diseases.

text: Kɛn ti̱ cië ti̱ti̱ni̱ dëëkɛ tuɔɔk kɛ wi̱c tin ci̱ raan wä thi̱n kiɛɛ wi̱i̱c tin go̱o̱r raan wä thi̱n.
text_en: These requirements may often depend on what countries a traveller has visited or intends to visit.

text: Kɛl in bumni̱ jɛn ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä Carlɔtɛ,Nhiam Karɔli̱na, ɛ ɣöö teekɛ dup ti̱ ŋuan ti̱ gɔw ti̱ dëë ji̱ cieŋ kɛ matpiny.
text_en: One of strong points of Charlotte, North Carolina, is that it has an abundance of high-quality options for families.

text: Nɛy tin ciëŋ guäthni̱ ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ,la kɛn ciaaŋ in in ci̱ kɛn ɛ nɛn kä ji̱ cieŋ ɛla min nhiam kɛ wä diɛn ɣɛn thɔ̱ŋ ɛmi̱ kɛ guël,Ja̱a̱l la kɛnɛ laa jëk ɛ thia̱k kä gɔaa mi̱ jäl kɛn kɛɛl kɛ gaat.
text_en: Residents from other areas often cite family-friendliness as a primary reason for moving there, and visitors often find the city easy to enjoy with children around.

text: Kɛ kɔr runi̱ ti̱ 20  tee ci̱ wä,ta̱a̱ ciɛŋä gan agɔa kä Carlɔtɛ aptɔɔn cɛ wä nhial ɛlɔ̱ŋ
text_en: In the past 20 years, the amount of child-friendly options in Uptown Charlotte has grown exponentially.

text: Takthi̱ni̱ /caa kɛɛ kɔt ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä Carlɔtɛ, ɛ cäŋ ni̱ min kɛ tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni̱ të kɛn kɛ luɔt.
text_en: Taxis are not generally used by families in Charlotte, though they can be of some use in certain circumstances.

text: Laa rëpkɛ yi̱o̱w nath mi̱ ci̱ nɛy da̱ŋ  rɛw bäl, kɛ jɛn kui̱c ɛmɔ dëë ta̱a̱ ko̱kä dɛ të nhial ɛ /ci̱ lapɛ ta̱a̱ in wën.
text_en: There is a surcharge for having more than 2 passengers, so this option might be more expensive than necessary.

text: Jɔk ɣɔa min cɔalkɛ Antartica ɛ jɛn gua̱a̱th min kɔ̱c ɛ lɔ̱ŋ wi̱i̱ muɔ̱ɔ̱n kɛɛliw kɛnɛ gua̱th tin thia̱k kɛ jɛ.
text_en: Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth, and surrounds the South Pole.

text: Gui̱l ja̱a̱li kɛ ɣɔw ŋuan yio̱wkɛ, kä go̱o̱rɛ pual pua̱a̱ny mi rɔ̱ŋ, la wä naath kɛ pay wäl kɛl a wä kä pay rɛw kä rɔa, kä pek kɛn kä dhuɔ̱li tin kuiynikɛn kɛ tin di̱t, Bar kɛnɛ Bar Ross.
text_en: Tourist visits are costly, demand physical fitness, can only take place in summer Nov-Feb, and are largely limited to the Peninsula, Islands and Ross Sea.

text: Tëë la̱a̱t ti ŋuan ti cop ki̱thni ti ci rɔ̱ da̱a̱k ti te wälrɛw kɛɛl gua̱thni da̱ŋ ŋuaan ti cieŋ thi̱n mi ci ɣɔw leeth; kɛ jiɔm la cieŋ ni nɛy ti tɔt thi̱n.
text_en: A couple of thousand staff live here in summer in some four dozen bases mostly in those areas; a small number stay over winter.

text: Rɛy dhulä Antartica ɛ rɛl mi ca kuɔ̱m piny ɛ tilic kɛ mi̱ti̱ri ti̱  2 kiɛ 3.
text_en: Inland Antarctica is a desolate plateau covered by 2-3 km of ice.

text: Nɛy tin ŋa̱c ɣɔw tin jäl kɛ ria̱th nhiali la wäkɛ ni däärɛ, kɛ gör ŋäcä päämni kiɛ kɛ cuɔ̱pdiɛn ni peekdɛ, min kulɛ di̱t ni jɛn ɛ lɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Occasional specialist air tours go inland, for mountaineering or to reach the Pole, which has a large base.

text: Ɣɛn Thɔth pöl Trabäth  (kiɛ Ɣa̱i̱wɛy) kɛ pëkdɛ ɛ kilimitiri̱ ti̱ 1600 kɛ pëk in bä kä MakMurdo thokdɛ  kuic yieer Röth ɛwä nikä pöölɛ.
text_en: The South Pole Traverse (or Highway) is a 1600 km trail from McMurdo Station on the Ross Sea to the Pole.

text: Jɛn ɛ i̱thnɔw  mi̱ ci̱ rɔ käp kɛɛl kɛɛ kri̱bethithni̱ tin caa thiäŋ kä caa gua̱thdiɛn moc kɛɛ bɛ̈ri̱. jɛn dëë jɛ gɛr traktɔr mi̱ ci̱ thuɔ̱k thin yɔɔ̱äckɛ kuakɛ  kɛ makanɛ mi̱ tëë kɛ ja̱th.
text_en: It's compacted snow with crevasses filled in and marked by flags. It can only be traveled by specialized tractors, hauling sleds with fuel and supplies.

text: Kɛn /ci̱kɛ pɛ̈th ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɣɛn gatɔr laa jänyɛ kɛ yɔ̱äcdɛ kɛ rɔ kɛ pääm Truäntäntaktik kɛ bëndɛ kä pääm tin tɔatni̱
text_en: These aren't very nimble so the trail has to take a long swerve around the Transantarctic Mountains to come onto the plateau.

text: Min no̱o̱ŋ riëëcni̱ ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ jiɔm ɛta̱a̱ cätcätdä gëkni̱ caari̱ ( jäl gekni̱ car) cëtkɛ ka̱a̱th.
text_en: The most common cause for accidents in winter is slippery roads, pavements (sidewalks) and especially steps.

text: Min dëri̱ lɛl ,go̱rɛ war  mi̱ dëri̱ la̱th ci̱o̱kä du mi̱ të kɛɛ thɔɔl mi̱ gɔaa. wa̱ri̱ ma̱y la lapkɛn ɛ ti̱ cätcäät rɛy i̱thnɔwä kɛnɛ ɣac, amäni̱ butni̱ jin jɔam bä dak kɛn.
text_en: At a minimum, you need footwear with suitable soles. Summer shoes are usually very slippery on ice and snow, even some winter boots are deficient.

text: Jɛn pa̱tɛn dërɛ lueŋdɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ, 5mm (1/5inch) ɛ wä nhiam, kä min la̱t kɛ jɛ kɛ jɛ dëra kuaak mi̱ kɔ̱c-kɔ̱c mi̱ kɔ̱c ɣɔw kiɛ mi̱ të tëmpërɛciɛr piny.
text_en: The pattern should be deep enough, 5 mm (1/5 inch) or more, and the material soft enough in cold temperatures.

text: Thääŋ butni̱ të kɛn kɛɛ nyuɛ̈ny kä teekɛ mi të thi̱n mi̱ laa duŋ cätcätdä kä wa̱ri̱ ti̱ ŋuan kɛnɛ butni̱ kɛ bär thäri̱kiɛn kɛnɛ thɔɔli̱kɛn.
text_en: Some boots have studs and there is studded add-on equipment for slippery conditions, suitable for most shoes and boots, for the heels or heels and sole.

text: Thär wa̱a̱ri̱ tin bärbäa̱r dëkɛ të piny kä dëkɛ diët.liɛt, grabɛl, kiɛ katdɛ (kälci̱öm kɔlɔ̱raid) jɛn laa puɔr jɛ rɛy cari̱ kɛ ɣöö ci̱ ta̱a̱ cätcätdä të thi̱n.
text_en: Heels should be low and wide. Sand, gravel or salt (calcium chloride) is often scattered on roads or paths to improve traction.

text: Jɛn ca̱a̱t in laa cät kɛɛ tilic piny wi̱i̱c päämni̱  /ci̱ɛ mi̱ gääy tuɔɔkdɛ naath; pömni̱ tin lueŋlueeŋ dëë kɛn luäŋ ni̱ min jäl ɛ määth kɛ röm, kä jɛn min ci̱ di̱tdɛ rɔ rep laa cät ɛ piny kɛ pɛ̈th.
text_en: Avalanches are not an abnormality; steep slopes can hold only so much slow, and the excess volumes will come down as avalanches.

text: Min la riɛk ɛ ɣöö i̱thnöw ɛmi̱ dɔpdɔp,jɛn görɛ mi̱ dëë jɛ tɛŋ dërɛ kulɛ pɛn piny kä mi̱ bä tha̱a̱ŋ ɣacä piny dërɛ ɣac in dɔ̱ŋ tɛŋ piny bä.
text_en: The problem is that snow is sticky, so it needs some triggering to come down, and some snow coming down can be the triggering event for the rest.

text: Tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni̱ ɛla min thuɔ̱k in tɛɛŋ ɣac ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛ cäŋ kɛ lërɛ kɛɛ i̱thnɔw,tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni̱ dëraa pɛ̈ɛ̈n i̱thnɔwä kä rɔa thääŋ gua̱thni dëka nyin ɣɔa tin laa tuɔk cëtkɛ raan.
text_en: Sometimes the original trigging event is the sun warming the snow, sometimes some more snowfall, sometimes other natural events, often a human.

text: Thul ɛ jiɔm mi̱ laa riith rɔɔdɛ mi̱ tëkɛ buɔ̱m jiɔm mi di̱i̱t mi̱ took rɔɔdɛ piny ɛ määth kuɛ lɛ wä nhial.
text_en: A tornado is a spinning column of very low-pressure air, which sucks the surrounding air inward and upward.

text: La kɛn jiɔm ti̱ di̱t ɛ no̱o̱ŋ ( ti̱ cët kɛ 100-200) kä dërɛ duɔ̱r mi̱ thiɛkthiɛk kap nhial kapɛ jɛ min wee kɛ wä nhial ɣɛn thul.
text_en: They generate high winds (often 100-200 miles/hour) and can lift heavy objects into the air, carrying them as the tornado moves.

text: La kɛn  a took cëtkɛ ti̱ ɣööŋ ti̱ bee rɛy jɔam nhial kä bi̱ kɛn cua̱ "thuɔ̱l" mi̱ ci̱ kɛn piny nyɔt.
text_en: They begin as funnels descending from storm clouds, and become "tornadoes" when they touch the ground.

text: VPN min la duŋ ran (mi̱ ci lapɛ duŋ nɛɛni̱ diaal).tin ŋuɔ̱n kɛ wiäl ŋɔani̱ kɛɛ thiathɛ kɛnɛ kuen nath amani̱ cɔmercial IP jiöpiltɛriŋ.
text_en: Personal VPN (virtual private network) providers are an excellent way of circumventing both political censorship and commercial IP-geofiltering.

text: Kɛn tëkɛ të kɛ wi̱i̱kä wɛb prɔkthi̱th kɛ dup ti̱ ŋuan.kɛn ku kɛn trapik intɛrnɛtni̱ dial pith ɛ /ci̱ lapɛ http.
text_en: They are superior to web proxies for several reasons: They re-route all Internet traffic, not only http.

text: La kɛn ta̱a̱ intɛrnɛtä mi̱ di̱i̱t kɛnɛ ti̱ gɔw laa tho̱p naath. Caa kɛ ɛnkriptɛt kä bum ɣöö dekɛ luɔm.
text_en: They normally offer higher bandwidth and better quality of service. They are encrypted and thus harder to spy on.

text: Kɛn kɔmpani̱ni̱ nyin ji̱ midia la kɛn kac ɛ kac ni̱ ciaŋ kɛɛ luɔtkä nɛmɛ bi̱ kɛn cuu wëë i̱ "gaŋɛ ni̱ cuër  rɛy jɔam".
text_en: The media companies routinely lie about the purpose of this, claiming that it is to "prevent piracy".

text: Kɛ thuɔ̱kdɛ kɔɔdni̱ nyin wëc  thiɛlɛ kɛ riɛk kɛ kui̱c kä min caa mat piny kɛ kui̱c duɔ̱rä  m tɔt kä mi̱ tɔt ɛla kɔpɛ duŋ dithkä bɛ ŋar a thiɛlɛ riɛk cëtkɛ gua̱äth in tä mee wal thi̱n.
text_en: In fact, region codes have absolutely no effect on illegal copying; a bit-for-bit copy of a disk will play just fine on any device where the original will.

text: Min la luɔtdɛ ɛ ɣöö dee kɔmpani̱ni̱ dee kɛ thöp buɔ̱m kɛ tää thu̱kni̱ kiɛn;jɛn luɔtdɔ ɛ wiäl yio̱ni̱.
text_en: The actual purpose is to give those companies more control over their markets; it's all about money spinning.

text: Kɛ ɣöö yɔ̱ät puɔɔni̱ min yɔ̱t kɛ naath cakɛ läth rɛy jɔam,Thiɛlɛ mi̱ go̱r ɣöö dëri̱ thiek kɛɛ kɔmpani̱ duŋ  tɛlɛpoona̱ kiɛ gua̱th in wi̱i̱ ja̱l thi̱n.
text_en: Because calls are routed over the Internet, you do not need to use a phone company located where you live or where you travel.

text: Thiɛlɛ mi̱ lar jɛ bä idëri̱ naŋ ni̱ nɔmbor duŋ ɣëlɛ kä min ti̱i̱ thi̱n dëri̱  intɛrnɛt duŋ thätɛlaitkä, rɛy wëc Wi̱l Cikɛn Aläthka kä dëri̱ ncmbor kuany min nyooth jɛ i̱ ti̱i̱ kä Aridhɔna min lɛp cäŋ thin.
text_en: There is also no requirement that you obtain a local number from the community in which you live; you can obtain a satellite Internet connection in the wilds of Chicken, Alaska and select a number which claims you're in sunny Arizona.

text: Kɛ tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni, bi nämbär rööl kɔk mi bi ji̱ jakä ɣöö yɔ̱a̱tkɛ ikä kɛ ja̱a̱thni PSTN. Gua̱a̱th in te nämbär thi̱n jakɛ jɛ kä thia̱k kɛ kui̱ nɛɛni tin yɔ̱a̱tkɛ ji̱ ikä ɛ kɛn.
text_en: Often, you have to buy a global number separately that allows PSTN phones to call you. Where the number is from makes a difference for people calling you.

text: Tëëkɛ kuak ti ca rialikä ti looc thuk kä rɔ̱ ɛ tookɛ kä thok kɛl a wä kä thok in dɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Real-time text translator apps – applications that are capable of automatically translating whole segments of text from one language into another.

text: Kɛn tha̱a̱ŋ kuakni ti̱ti̱ dee kɛn ruaacni loc kɛ thuk ti gööl cie kɛ ruaacni nɛɛni tin /ci li̱ŋ kiɛ tin kɔ̱ŋ wi̱i̱ muɔ̱ɔ̱n mi ci raan nyuɔ̱th kɛ tetdɛ rɛy ja̱a̱thkä dɛ.
text_en: Some of the applications in this category can even translate texts in foreign languages on signs or other objects in the real world when the user points the smartphone towards those objects.

text: Kɛn gua̱th tin la luɔc kɛ thuk thi̱n cikɛ rɔ̱ luäŋ ɛlɔ̱ŋ, ɛn täämɛ looc kɛn thuk kɛ gua̱a̱thdɛ nikä ti ŋuan kiɛ kä tɔt (kä gua̱thni ti ŋuan thiɛlɛ kɛ luɔt), ɛni ɣöö go̱rɛ guec, kɛ ɣöö dɔ̱ŋ dee kɛn la̱t ni baŋ.
text_en: The translation engines have improved dramatically, and now often give more or less correct translations (and more seldom gibberish), but some care is due, as they still may have gotten it all wrong.

text: Kuak lucä thuɔk in te thi̱n ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛ "Google Translate", mi la jak luɔ̱c thukni kä ɣöö bi rɔ la̱t gua̱a̱th mi thiɛl intɛrnet kɛ gua̱a̱th in ci raan lääri tin go̱rɛ ka̱m raar.
text_en: One of the most prominent apps in this category is Google Translate, which allows offline translation after downloading the desired language data.

text: La̱tdu kɛ kuak GPS tin nyooth gua̱a̱th in te raan thi̱n rɛy ja̱a̱thkädu derɛ la duɔ̱ɔ̱p mi thia̱k ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ rialu kɛ rɔ ikä gua̱a̱th in ci jiɛɛn wi̱i̱du.
text_en: Using GPS navigation apps on your smartphone can be the easiest and most convenient way to navigate when out of your home country.

text: Derɛ ji̱ duɔ̱th yio̱w kɛ kökdu kɛ GPS mi ji̱di̱t, kiɛ GPS mi lät kä rɔa kiɛ dëë jur kä kampani ji̱ thuɔ̱rbiɛɛli.
text_en: It can save money over buying new maps for a GPS, or a standalone GPS device or renting one from a car rental company.

text: Mi thiɛlɛ ji̱ mi wee kɛ ji̱ rɛy jɔam rɛy ja̱a̱tkädu, kiɛ mi thiɛlɛ mi luäŋɛ, la la̱t in dee lät kɛ kɛ la wä piny.
text_en: If you don't have a data connection for your phone, or when it is out of range, their performance can be limited or unavailable.

text: Gɔ̱ŋtɔli diaal cakɛ thia̱ŋ kɛ kadni ja̱a̱thkä ti ca yuɔr piny ɛ ŋot ti yiec kɛ wuɔ̱th nath ti dëë la̱th lät rɛy ja̱a̱thni tin ca yio̱wkiɛn yuɔr piny kiɛ ja̱a̱thni tin ŋa̱ckɛ.
text_en: Every corner store is filled with a confusing array of pre-paid phone cards that can be used from pay phones or ordinary telephones.

text: Kɛ ɣöö ri̱w kadni ti ŋuan gɔwkɛn kɛ yɔ̱a̱t gua̱thni ti gööl, tha̱a̱ŋkiɛn rialkɛ yɔ̱a̱t mi gɔa ikä kä wi̱i̱c ti ŋa̱ckɛ.
text_en: While most cards are good for calling anywhere, some specialise in providing favourable call rates to specific groups of countries.

text: Kɛn lät ɛ ti̱i̱ la jekɛ kɛ kɛ yɔ̱a̱t nath kɛ nämbär mi ŋa̱ckɛ ikä rɛy ja̱a̱thni diaal baaŋ ɛ thiɛl yio̱w ti go̱o̱rɛ.
text_en: Access to these services is often through a toll-free telephone number that can be called from most phones without charge.

text: Ŋuɔ̱t kɛ kui̱ thurɛkä bä wäkɛ kɛɛl kɛ lätni bidiöökä, kä wäkɛ kɛɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Rules regarding regular photography also apply to video recording, possibly even more so.

text: Mi /ca jɛ nhɔk ɛn ɣöö deri thurɛ kä duɔ̱ɔ̱r naŋ, /ci rɔ dee nyäk kɛ ɣöö derɛ ca̱ru la̱th thi̱n kɛ yiöcdu kɛ bidiöödɛ.
text_en: If just taking a photo of something isn't allowed, then you shouldn't even think of recording a video of it.

text: Mi jeli kɛ riääc ŋarä min tɔt, guicɛ ni gɔa ɛ ŋot kä ŋäcni min ca nhɔk i̱ bi wä thur kɛnɛ wargakni la̱t kiɛ wargakni nyooth jɛ ɛn ɣöö lätdi kä görkɛ.
text_en: If using a drone, check well in advance as to what you are allowed to film and what permits or additional licensing are required.

text: Köt ria̱a̱th ŋarä min tɔt gua̱a̱th mi thieek kɛ gua̱a̱th köt ria̱th nhiali kiɛ wi̱i̱ nɛɛni ti ŋuan ɛ ca̱p mi jiääk ɛlɔ̱ŋ, a /cäŋ ciɛ duer gua̱a̱th in ciɛŋi.
text_en: Flying a drone near an airport or over a crowd is almost always a bad idea, even if it's not illegal in your area.

text: Ɛn ni̱ni̱ ti̱ti̱ dakɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛn ɣöö bi raan wargak ja̱lɛ kɛ riääc nhial tɛm a /kenɛ ni gör kɛnɛ ɣöö derɛ yio̱w köt pa̱a̱r.
text_en: Nowadays air travel is only rarely booked directly through the airline without first searching and comparing prices.

text: Kɛn tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱th ɛn riääy nhial ɛ kɛl ɔ derɛ tekɛ yio̱w gööli ti ŋuan kä go̱o̱rɛ ɣöö dee raan kɔŋ thiec kä derɛ wä rɛy wɛpthaiyädiɛn rɛy jɔam min la duŋ ria̱a̱y ɛ ŋot /ke̱n raan yio̱w köt ni yuɔr piny.
text_en: Sometimes the same flight can have vastly differing prices at various agregators and it pays to compare search results and to also look at the website of the airline itself before booking.

text: Kɛ ɣöö dɔ̱ŋ /ci wargak ja̱l dee go̱r kɛ kui̱ jeli ti ciëk ciëëk wädu wi̱i̱ni ti kɔ̱ŋ ala ja̱a̱l kiɛ ran la̱t, wädu ɛn thɔ̱ŋɛ mi̱i̱ ala gat duël gɔ̱rä wec muɔ̱ɔ̱n derɛ ji̱ jakä ɣöö deri jääny a /ci ma wädu ala jääl baaŋ.
text_en: While you may not need a visa for short visits to certain countries as a tourist or for business, going there as an international student generally requires a longer stay than going there just as a casual tourist.

text: Min te thi̱n, ciaandu wi̱i̱ mi dɔ̱ŋ kɛ pek mi bäär bɛ ji̱ jakä ɣöö bi rɔ gör wargakni ciɛɛŋä ti ba ŋäcni ji̱ rɛy wec ɛ ŋot.
text_en: In general, staying in any foreign country for an extended period of time will require you to obtain a visa in advance.

text: Wargakni ja̱l gan duël gɔ̱rä tekɛ kɛ ti gööl ti la görkɛ thi̱n kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ thieŋä min la duŋ nɛɛni ti ja̱a̱l kiɛ wargakni lätni.
text_en: Student visas generally have different requirements and application procedures from normal tourist or business visas.

text: Wi̱i̱c ti ŋuan, ba ji̱ moc kɛ wargak mi cɔl ji̱ duel gɔ̱rä min bi gɔ̱a̱r thi̱n, amäni mi nyooth yio̱w tin bi yiɛɛn ni rɔ kɛ pek runä kɛl a wä nham gua̱a̱th in gɔ̱ɔ̱ri la̱tdu.
text_en: For most countries, you will need an offer letter from the institution you wish to study at, and also evidence of funds to support yourself for at least the first year of your course.

text: Guuri jɛ kɛɛl kɛ ji̱ duël gɔ̱rädu, amäni muktäb jeli wec in wi̱i̱ gɔ̱a̱r thi̱n kɛ tin diaal tin görkɛ kä ca guir.
text_en: Check with the institution, as well as the immigration department for the country you wish to study in for detailed requirements.

text: Ɛni mi̱ ɛ ji̱n ram la kuäär wi̱c dɔ̱diɛn, la̱t wi̱c mi dɔ̱ŋ lotdɛ ni ɣöö bi tho̱lbo̱k in ca rialikä wi̱c in lätdi thi̱n thöp.
text_en: Unless you are a diplomat, working overseas generally means that you will have to file income tax in the country you are based in.

text: Tho̱lbo̱k yio̱o̱ni tin ka̱pkɛ gua̱cɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ wi̱i̱cni ti gööl, kä pek tho̱lbo̱kä min thöpkɛ lɛ̱̈ɛ̱̈nykɛ rɔ̱ kam wec ɔ kɛnɛ wec ɔ.
text_en: Income tax is structured differently in different countries, and the tax rates and brackets vary widely from one country to another.

text: Rɛy tha̱a̱ŋ wi̱i̱ni tin kɔ̱ŋ, ce̱tkɛ United States kɛnɛ Canada, tho̱lbo̱k yio̱o̱ni tin ka̱pkɛ ca jɛ la̱th rɛy ŋuɔ̱tni ji̱ kumɛ tin te nhial kɛnɛ ji̱ ŋuɔ̱tni tin te piny, kɛ ɣöö bi yio̱w tin yuɔrkɛ piny kulɛ te kɛ dääk dhɔr ɔ kɛnɛ dhɔr ɔ.
text_en: In some federal countries, such as the United States and Canada, income tax is levied both at the federal level and at the local level, so the rates and brackets can vary from region to region.

text: Kɛ ɣöö la thiɛlɛ guec mi di̱i̱t ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä nɛy tin ka̱p kɛ guäth jeli kiɛ lääri ti thuɔ̱ɔ̱k gua̱a̱th in ci cop cieendu, guur ŋuɔ̱tni kuakni deri la riɛk ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: While immigration check is usually absent or a formality when you arrive in your homeland, customs control can be a hassle.

text: Läthni jɛ lät ɛn ɣöö bi min deri ŋa̱c kä deri kui̱c mi deri nööŋ rɛc ŋa̱c kä guuri lätni kɛ pek ŋuɔ̱tni tin ca rialikä.
text_en: Make sure you know what you can and cannot bring in and declare anything over the legal limits.

text: Duɔ̱p in thia̱k ni jɛn kɛ wädu rɛy lätni jeli la̱t gɔ̱rä ɛ ɣöö bi tin diaal tin luäŋi kɛ la̱t la̱th rɛy jɔam kä wɛpthait.
text_en: The easiest way to get started in the business of travel writing is to hone your skills on an established travel blog website.

text: Mi ci ɣöö deri duɔ̱ɔ̱r luäŋ kɛ cuɔ̱th kiɛ deri jɛ rep rɛy jɔam, kɛ kɔrɛ, deri wɛpthaaydu la̱t.
text_en: After you become comfortable with formatting and editing on the web, then later, you might create your own website.

text: Kuëny ran kɛ rɔ kä rɔa gua̱a̱th in te naath jel ɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p mi gɔa ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛni ɣöö /ciɛ tho̱pni ŋɔani.
text_en: Volunteering while travelling is a great way to make a difference but it's not just about giving.

text: Ciandu kɛnɛ kuënydu kɛ rɔ kä rɔa rɛy wec mi dɔ̱ŋ ɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p mi gɔa mi deri ŋäc ni ciaaŋ nɛɛni ti gööl, jëkdu kɛ nɛy ti kɔ̱ŋ, ŋäcdu kɛ rɔ, ŋäc ŋɔanidu kɛ nyin teekä ti ŋuan amäni jekdu kɛ lua̱ŋ ŋäcä ŋɔani.
text_en: Living and volunteering in a foreign country is a great way to get to know a different culture, meet new people, learn about yourself, get a sense of perspective and even gain new skills.

text: Bɛ la duɔ̱ɔ̱p kɛl mi gɔa mi dee yio̱w ran jääny kɛ jɛ kɛ gua̱th mi bäär kɛ ɣöö lät diaal tin läth raan rɔ thi̱n kä rɔa la mooc kɛn raan kɛ duel kɛnɛ muktäb kä tha̱a̱ŋkiɛn la mooc kɛn naath yio̱w ti tɔt.
text_en: It can also be a good way to stretch a budget to allow a longer stay somewhere since many volunteer jobs provide room and board and a few pay a small salary.

text: Vikings la jelkɛ kɛ dup yiëër ji̱ Russia kɛ wädiɛn Baar Black kɛnɛ Caspian. Tha̱a̱ŋ dupni ti̱ti̱ dee naath ja̱l kɛ kɛ bä. Go̱rɛ kä thiecni mi derɛ tekɛ wargakni ja̱l ti dee jɔɔc, tin dɔ̱ŋ dee jekdiɛn bɛ̈c.
text_en: Vikings used the Russian waterways to get to the Black Sea and Caspian Sea. Parts of these routes can still be used. Check possible need for special permits, which may be difficult to get.

text: Ɛn Duɔ̱ɔ̱p pi̱i̱ni min Bo̱r Bar Baltic ro̱mɛ Bäpdiit Arctic kɛnɛ Bar Baltic, kɛ luäl mi bä Puul Onega, Pul Ladoga kɛnɛ Saint Petersburg, ti la yiër kɛnɛ puɔ̱l ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: The White Sea–Baltic Canal connects the Arctic Ocean to the Baltic Sea, via Lake Onega, Lake Ladoga and Saint Petersburg, mostly by rivers and lakes.

text: Pul Onega bä cakɛ röm kɛnɛ Volga, mi lotni ɣöö jiɛɛn kä Caspian kɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p Russia ŋotdɛ mi lotdɛ rɔ.
text_en: Lake Onega is also connected to Volga, so coming from the Caspian Sea through Russia is still possible.

text: Ŋäcni jɛ ɛn ɣöö wi̱i̱ gua̱a̱th känyä piny babuuri wä cop bi ti̱ diaal la ti gɔw. Bi kööt bötni ti cie ji̱ wä jek kä bikɛ läärikiɛn nyuak kɛ ji̱ kɛɛl.
text_en: Be assured that once you hit the marinas everything will be pretty obvious. You will meet other boat hitchhikers and they will share their information with you.

text: Bi lääri kɛ kui̱ lua̱kädu la̱th lät, ja̱lu wädu gua̱thni bötni kɛnɛ babuuri, wädu kä nɛy ti lak bötnikiɛn, ŋäcdu kɛ rɔ kɛ ja̱a̱l yiëër rɛy duëël in la mäth naath thi̱n kɛ pi̱w ti gööl.
text_en: Basically you'll be putting up notices offering your help, pacing the docks, approaching people cleaning their yachts, trying to make contact with sailors in the bar, etc.

text: Ruacni kɛ nɛy ti ŋuan kɛ pek luäŋädu kɛɛliw. Kɛ kɔr gua̱th mi tɔt ba ji̱ ŋa̱c ɛ nɛy diaal kä ba ji̱ la̱r lär mi wëë te böt mi go̱o̱r raan.
text_en: Try to talk to as many people as possible. After a while everyone will know you and will give you hints as to which boat is looking for someone.

text: Deri ria̱a̱c in dee la ko̱t kɛ ji̱ ni ciaŋ rɛy buni kuany ɛ gɔa.
text_en: You should choose your Frequent Flyer airline in an alliance carefully.

text: Cäŋni min guici jɛ ɛn ɣöö i̱ deri rɔ mat rɛy ria̱a̱c in la kɔtdi ɛlɔ̱ŋ, biɛ ŋa̱c ɛn ɣöö gɔy tin la thöpkɛ gua̱ckɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä kuak ria̱a̱c in la kɔtdi dee gɔw ni kɛn ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ riääc mi dɔ̱ŋ mi te ɛn rɛy buni ria̱thni tɔ̱tɔ̱.
text_en: Although you may think it is intuitive to join the airline you fly most, you should be aware that privileges offered are often different and frequent flyer points may be more generous under a different airline in the same alliance.

text: Ria̱th Emirates, Etihad, Qatar kɛ Turkey cikɛ jel ria̱thnikiɛn rep ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä Apirka, kä no̱o̱ŋ kɛn mat mi di̱i̱t ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä wi̱i̱ Apirka tin di̱t tin ŋa̱ckɛ kɛ köt mi kuiy mi leny ria̱th Yurɔp tin kɔ̱ŋ.
text_en: Airlines such as Emirates, Etihad Airways, Qatar Airways & Turkish Airlines have greatly expanded their services to Africa, and offer connections to many major African cities at competitive rates than other European airlines.

text: Kɛ ruɔ̱n 2014, riääc nhial ji̱ Turkey la wëë gua̱thni ti 39 kä wi̱i̱ ti 30 kä Apirka.
text_en: Turkish Airlines flies to 39 destinations in 30 African countries as of 2014.

text: Mi ti̱i̱ kɛ thaak ja̱l mi ca reepni ji̱, go̱rɛ kä guicɛ mi päär yio̱w kötdu tin la wee kɛ ji̱ kä Apirka kɛ yio̱w ria̱thni tin kɔ̱ŋ wi̱i̱ muɔ̱ɔ̱n kɛɛliw.
text_en: If you have additional travel time, check to see how your total fare quote to Africa compares with a round-the-world fare.

text: /Cu yio̱w tin pieemkɛ wargakni ja̱lu päl ruëëc, tho̱lbo̱k jiɛɛnä, ja̱l piɛny, amäni tin kɔ̱kiɛn kɛ gua̱th diaal tin te raar Apirka.
text_en: Don't forget to add in the extra costs of additional visas, departure taxes, ground transportation, etc. for all those places outside of Africa.

text: Mi̱ go̱o̱ri̱ ɣöö bi̱ wi̱cmuɔ̱ɔ̱n win kɛ ja̱l kɛ nhial rɛy jɔak Hëmi̱thpiër, jɛn min dëë ja̱l kɛ ji̱ kɛnɛ gua̱a̱th in dëri̱ wä thi̱n dakɛ kɛ ɣöö thiɛlɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p mi̱ jääl kam bäbdiitni̱.
text_en: If you want to fly around the world completely in the Southern Hemisphere, the choice of flights and destinations is limited due to the lack of transoceanic routes.

text: Thiɛlɛ ji̱ ria̱ynhiali̱ ti̱ ci̱ rɔ mat ti̱ lät kɛɛl ti̱ jääl kɛ kɛn bäbdiitni̱ da̱ŋdiɔ̱k diaal tin te jɔɔk Hëmi̱thpiër ( Kä I̱thkaiTi̱i̱m /cɛ kɛ bäl gua̱th ni̱ kiɛn diaal)
text_en: No airline alliance covers all three ocean crossings in the Southern Hemisphere (and SkyTeam covers none of the crossings).

text: Cäŋni ɣöö nɔ, I̱thtaar Allian cop ɛ kɛn dial kän ni̱ jɛn kui̱c cueec Jɔak Pa̱thi̱pik ɛ took ɛ ni̱ kä Thantiagö de Ci̱lɛ ɛ wä kä Tahi̱ti̱ , min laa ja̱l kɛl kä LATAM
text_en: However, Star Alliance covers everything except the eastern South Pacific from Santiago de Chile to Tahiti, which is a LATAM Oneworld flight.

text: Jɛn ja̱l kɛ nhial ɛmɛ /ciɛ jɛn min dëri̱ kuany ni̱ jɛ kä rɔa mi̱ go̱o̱ri̱ ba̱l Jɔak Pa̱thi̱pik kɛnɛ jɛn thok baar in te kui̱c cueec kä jɛn Jɔk Mɛrkɛm. ( biɛ jek piny)
text_en: This flight is not the only option if you want to skip the South Pacific and the west coast of South America. (see below)

text: Kɛ 1994, jɛn do̱r ji̱ Armɛnia ni̱ Nagörnö-Karabakh ri̱jɔ̱n duŋ Adhɛrbaijan cuɛ ko̱r ŋuɔ̱k Adhɛri̱th.
text_en: In 1994, the ethnically Armenian Nagorno-Karabakh region of Azerbaijan waged war against the Azeris.

text: Kɛ ɣöö caa kɛ luäk ɛ ji Armɛnia, cua wec mi̱ ji̱di̱t cak. Cäŋ ni̱ mee, thiɛlɛ wec mi̱ caa yiath piny-ɛ cäŋ jɛn Armɛnia- ka̱nɛ ŋic ɛ nɛy tin ka̱p kɛ wi̱c nath.
text_en: With Armenian backing, a new republic was created. However, no established nation - not even Armenia - officially recognizes it.

text: Jɛn ŋaknɔm kä kɛn di̱plömatik kɛ kui̱c ri̱jɔ̱n ŋotdɛ kɛ mi̱ yärɛ ni̱ maar kamä Ji Armɛnia kɛnɛ Adhɛrbajian.
text_en: Diplomatic arguments over the region continue to mar relations between Armenia and Azerbaijan.

text: Jɛn Kanal Di̱thtrik (Dutch: Gra̱ctɛŋgɔrdɛl) ɛ jɛn di̱thtrik ee ci̱ kɛ̈kdɛ jɔɔc kɛɛ 17th thënciɛri̱ mee ci̱ Bi̱nneni̱thtad go̱l piny kä Ami̱thtɛrdam.
text_en: The Canal District (Dutch: Grachtengordel) is the famous 17th-century district surrounding the Binnenstad of Amsterdam.

text: Jɛn Di̱thtrik kɛliw ca jak kä Gua̱th Hëri̱tɛg wecmuɔ̱n ɛ UNESCO kɛ ɣöö tee kɛ ka̱lciɛr mi̱ /cɛ mat kɛ nɛy ti̱ kɔ̱ŋ kɛn ɛ gɔɔy lätni̱kiɛn tee wal kɛn ɛ kuak tin di̱t ni̱ kökdiɛn tin mät rɔ̱ kuak tin ŋuan ni̱ yio̱wkiɛn rɛy wec.
text_en: The whole district is designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its unique cultural and historical value, and its property values are among the highest of the country.

text: Ciŋki Tɛrrɛ, mi̱ lot ni̱ muɔ̱n dhieec, min te rɛydɛ kɛ kɛn dho̱r da̱n dhiëëc tin kuiy thook baar kä Riöaggiörɛ, Manaröla, Kɔ̱niglia, Bɛrnadha kɛnɛ Mɔntɛröthö mi̱n te kä jɛn ri̱gɔn Italia kä Li̱guria.
text_en: Cinque Terre, which means Five Lands, comprises the five small coastal villages of Riomaggiore, Manarola, Corniglia, Vernazza and Monterosso located in the Italian region of Liguria.

text: Caa kɛ gɔa̱r rsy cio̱o̱tni̱  ɛ UNESCO kä Hëri̱tɛg wecmuɔ̱ɔ̱n.
text_en: They are listed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

text: Kɛ kɔr runi̱ ti kur te ci̱ wä, ci̱ naath këk la̱t ɛ gɔaa wi̱i̱ kɔa̱kni̱ , gua̱th ti̱ lɛɛr pinyni̱ ɛ wä ni̱ wi̱i̱ pa̱a̱m min guic gua̱th ɛ mɔ piny.
text_en: Over the centuries, people have carefully built terraces on the rugged, steep landscape right up to the cliffs that overlook the sea.

text: Min bɛɛr naath thi̱n ɛ thiɛl la̱t min ka̱nɛ täth ɛ kumɛ, Dup, baabuuri̱ kɛnɛ botni̱ kɛ kɛn kua wi̱i̱c lɛ jäl kɛ kɛ, kä thiɛlɛ thuɔ̱rbiɛli̱ ti̱ dee ben go̱lä.
text_en: Part of its charm is the lack of visible corporate development. Paths, trains and boats connect the villages, and cars cannot reach them from the outside.

text: Jɛn ta̱a̱ thuɔk Pra̱nth min ruac kɛ naath kä Bɛljiëm kɛnɛ I̱thwi̱tdhɛrland tee kɛ dääk ɛ määth kɛ thok pra̱nth in ruac kɛ naath kä Pra̱nth, cäŋni min thiɛlɛ dääk ɛ liŋ kɛn rɔ gua̱th ni̱ kiɛn diaal.
text_en: The varieties of French which are spoken in Belgium and Switzerland differ slightly from the French spoken in France, though they are similar enough to be mutually intelligible.

text: Jɛn puɔ̱nydɛ kä rɔa, jɛn ta̱a̱ nämbäri̱ kä thok Pra̱nth min ruac kɛ naath kä Beljiëm kɛnɛ Ithwitdhɛrland tee kɛ dääk ɛ määth kä tha̱a̱ŋ kɛ ta̱a̱ mi̱ /cia̱ jɔc kɛ ruacdɛ kä ruac Ji Pra̱nth kä Pra̱nth, kɛnɛ ta̱a̱ in laa kɛɛ riëët gua̱ckɛ ɛ määth.
text_en: In particular, the numbering system in French-speaking Belgium and Switzerland has some slight peculiarities that are different from the French spoken in France, and the pronunciation of some words is slightly different.

text: Ŋotdɛ päärɛ, kɛn Ji̱ Bɛljiëm kɛnɛ Ji̱ I̱thwi̱tdhɛrland tin ruac kɛ thok Pra̱nth dëë kɛn thok Pra̱nth mi̱ päär gɔ̱r duël gɔ̱rä, kɛ kui̱c ɛ mɔ dëë kɛn ji̱ liŋ mi̱ cäŋ lätdi̱  ta̱a̱ nämbäri̱ Ji̱ Pra̱nth min caa pa̱a̱r.
text_en: Nevertheless, all French-speaking Belgians and Swiss would have learned standard French in school, so they would be able to understand you even if you used the standard French numbering system.

text: Gua̱th ti̱ ŋuan wi̱i̱cmuɔ̱ɔ̱n, mi̱ ri̱t i̱ tetdu kɛɛ maalɛ lot ɛ ni̱ ta̱a̱ malä, mi̱ lot ni̱ "malɛ̈."
text_en: In many parts of the world, waving is a friendly gesture, indicating "hello."

text: Cäŋ ni̱ ɣöö nɔ, kä Malecia, pëk mi̱ ro̱ŋ kä kɛn Ji Malecia tin te rɛy cieŋ, lot dɛ ni̱ ɣöö "ber gua̱th ɛmɛ," päärɛ kɛ ta̱a̱ in dëri̱ yiɛ̈t in cuɔŋ kui̱c in lot puɔ̱nydu, ɛ ta̱a̱ jäälä tetdä min lät kɛ naath kä tha̱a̱ŋ wi̱i̱cni̱ tin te kui̱c Caam ɣɔaa, kä baa la̱t ni̱ la̱t ɛmɔ kɛ jɛ kä rɔa.
